subject: CH ST
title: Central Americans in the United States
description: Provides an interdisciplinary historical overview of Central American migrations to the U.S., and a cultural and political analysis of resulting individual and group identities. Transnationalism, diasporas, politics, and community building among Central Americans, or "Central American-Americans" are explored.

subject: CH ST
title: Chicano/a Film Studies
description: Study of Chicano/a cinema to view film as an art form and projection of the filmmaker. Techniques, messages, and ideology stressed as instruments which propose film truth within the context of Chicano/a experience.

subject: CH ST
title: Chicana Art and Feminism
description: An overview of contemporary Chicana art and feminist theory from the late 1960s to the present placed within the context of the Chicano movement and other historical events.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: De-Colonizing Feminism
description: Surveys contemporary forms of feminist consciousness expressed U.S. women of color. Can U.S. women of color be considered a political class? What relations exist between women of color across race, culture, sex, and class differences?
prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.

subject: CH ST
title: Gender and Sexuality in the Americas
description: Examines cultural, social, political and representational aspects of gender and sexuality across the Americas. Organized around various themes--control and repression; the politics and culture of resistance; and sexual transgression as affirmation of marginalized identities--this course challenges conceptions of gender and sexuality across the Americas. Covering topics ranging from normative sexuality, transgender expression, gay sexuality, and lesbian expression, the course is designed to examine developments in gender and sexuality within the U.S. and across the Americas.
prereq_text: Departmental approval required to finalize registration.

subject: CH ST
title: Latinidades
description: What it means to be Latina/o/x varies not only based on class, nationality, and citizenship status but also on race and ethnicity. This undergraduate seminar interrogates Latinidad as a historical, political, and racial project. Students will trace the origins of Hispanic and Latina/o/x identities to the settler logics from which they emerged, particularly those that rely on the erasure of Indigenous and Afro-descendent populations. Special attention will be placed on how race and racism manifest in the material conditions and lived experiences of Indigenous, Afro-Indigenous, Afro/Black Latinxs.

subject: CH ST
title: Afro-Latina/o Diasporic Performance
description: Offers an introduction to performance practices rooted in the African diaspora of the Americas focusing on the United States, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Interrogates identity articulation in dance, music, literature, visual art, and theatrical texts. Examine how performers negotiate race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexuality with attention to what constitutes performance. Employingtransnational frameworks, explore how these performances have historically functioned and continue to inspire social transformation and the recovery of shared histories of Afro-Latina/o diasporas.

subject: CH ST
title: Ethnic Studies Teacher Education Seminar
description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American Studies, and/or Feminist Studies majors in the ÉXITO program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students’ pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning Ethnic Studies. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs, professionalization workshops, and conducting independent research.
prereq_text: At least one course in one of these departments: Asian American Studies, Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Feminist Studies.

Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning Ethnic Studies. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and applying to Masters/Teacher Education Programs, professionalization workshops, and conducting independent research.

description: Designed for students who are Black Studies, Chicana/o Studies, Asian American Studies, and/or Feminist Studies majors in the ÉXITO program. Central to the year-long seminar will be preparations for students’ pursuit for a career as K-12 Ethnic Studies educators. Students will have direct assistance for preparing and presenting their original research projects at URCA Day.

subject: CH ST
title: Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA)
description: Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA) introduces students to a method for reading, writing, thinking, and performing before an audience of peers. This method is based on the shaman-witness ritual proposed by Chicana theorist and writer, Gloria Anzaldua.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C; a previous upper-division course in Chicano Studies.

subject: CH ST
title: Storytelling as Activism Lab
description: Accompanies Storytelling as Activism (SWAPA) course. Focuses on creative production, atriculation, and vocal expression.

subject: CH ST
title: Latinx Youth
description: Focuses on Latinx immigrant youth and the children of Latinx immigrants’ experiences with identity formation, assimilation, race and ethnicity, and media representation. Delves into how racial ideologies inform the U.S. immigration system, as well as how racial ideologies from Latin America and the United States converge to inform the lives of people of Latin American descent.
prereq_text: Departmental approval required to finalize registration.

subject: CH ST
title: Xican* Indigena Media
description: Low cost digital tools have created a revolution in video. Course explores creative approaches to practical techniques of independent digital video production. Students establish a production strategy by employing "guerrilla tactics" for creative and unconventional uses of digital machineries.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C; two upper division courses in Chicana and Chicano Studies; Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 162L.

subject: CH ST
title: Xican* Indigena Media Lab
description: Lab for producing guerrilla digital video.

subject: CH ST
title: Exposing Health Inequities
description: Given the continuous rise of anti-immigrant sentiment felt across the United States and across the globe, this course brings the realities of immigrants of color to the forefront by exposing health inequities. It especially focuses attention on the structural inequities, drawing on Latinx Critical Race Theory, Chicana/o/x feminist epistemologies, and sociological insights into how and why ‘illegality,’ racism, and health converge and their critical intersections in exposing larger health inequities.

subject: CH ST
title: History of the Chicano
description: The history of the Chicanos from the indigenous/colonial past to 1900. Explores the evolving history of Mexican descent people during the Pre-Columbian, Spanish, Mexican, and the U.S. periods.
advisor_comments: Same course as History 168A.
prereq_text: History 17A or 17B or 17C or Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: History of the Chicanos
description: The history of the Chicanos from 1900 to the present. Explores issues such as immigration, second-generation experience, civil rights struggles, the Chicano Movement, the post-Chicano Movement, the role of women in Chicano history, and the new Latino millennials of the 21st century.
advisor_comments: Chicano Studies 168B and History 168B are the same course.
prereq_text: History 17A or 17B or 17C or Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: History of the Chicano Movement
description: History of the Chicano Movement. An examination of the Chicano movement in the United States from the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s. Topics will include the student movement, the farmworker movement, the Plande Aztlan, the Raza Unida Party, Chicana feminists, the anti-war movement, and Chicanostudies.
advisor_comments: Same course as History 168E.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: Latino Religious Traditions in Historical Perspective
description: Focuses on the role of religion in the Chicano/Latino historical experience. Includes pre-Columbian traditions, Spanish colonial traditions, religion of the U.S.-Mexico borderlands, immigrant religious traditions, the changing nature of Latino religions in the twentieth century.
advisor_comments: Same course as History 168T. Not open for credit to students who have taken CH ST 168R or HIST 168R.
prereq_text: A previous course in History or Chicano Studies.

subject: CH ST
title: The Brown/Black Metropolis: Race, Class, & Resistance in the City
description: Traces the transition of Browns/Blacks from a rural urban population and examines trends in family size, language, usage, segregation and social inequality. Issues of urban decay and community conflict are also examined.

subject: CH ST
title: Global Migration, Transnationalism in Chicana/o Contexts
description: This course considers Chicana/o and U.S. Latina/o culture(s) within the context of transnational practices and patterns including both hemispheric and global migration trajectories.

subject: CH ST
title: Survey of Chicano Literature
description: The course encompasses a general overview of all genres (poetry, novel, theater, short story and essay) of Chicano literature. A people's socio-historical experiences are examined to understand ethnicity, creativity, and world view.

subject: CH ST
title: Chicana/o Novels
description: Reading, analysis and critique of the contemporary Chicano novel as it pertains to the Chicano experience.
advisor_comments: Spanish 179 and Chicano Studies 181 are the same course.

subject: CH ST
title: Contemporary Chicanx Environmental Justice Writers
description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Centers on engagement with ecological themes. Feminist, queer, and environmental justice theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry, drama, and other narrative works written by such authors as María Amparo Ruiz de Burton, Jovita González, Cherríe Moraga, Ana Castillo, Helena María Viramontes, and others.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of LM or a class level of SB or a class level of SP or a class level of SS or CH ST 1A or CH ST 1B or CH ST 1C

subject: CH ST
title: Border Narrative
description: Reading and analysis of U.S./Mexico border narratives (novels, essays, short stories, autobiographies) focusing on the problems associated with relations between countries.

subject: CH ST
title: Chicana Writers
description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Feminist theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry and dramatic works written by such authors as Sandra Cisneros, Ana Castillo, Helen Viramontes, and others.
prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.

subject: CH ST
title: Decolonial CyberCinema
description: Cybercinema is one of the most recent and innovative technologies for representing reality. What are its aesthetic forms, and how do they work to de-colonize the imagination under postcolonial conditions? Can we identify a specific "Chicana/o" criticism or aesthetics?
prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185L; upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: Decolonial Cyber Cinema Lab
description: Mandatory Laboratory for CHST 185.
prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185; upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: Language, Power, and Learning
description: Critical examination of institutional power related to education and linguistic and cultural diversity. Focus on Latinx communities; formal and informal learning; family practices; bilingual education; heritage languages; language and labor; language and racism; immigrant languages; racialized varieties of English.
advisor_comments: Same course as LING 187.
prereq_text: Departmental Approval Required to Finalize Registration.

subject: CH ST
title: Chicano Theater Workshop
description: Reading and analysis of contemporary bilingual chicano plays, in conjunction with acting and technical training. A dramatic piece will be rehearsed and performed.
prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.

subject: CH ST
title: Immigration and the U.S. Border
description: Immigration and the U.S. border. An analysis of the socioeconomic and political factors which have determined and continue to form the basis for the development of United States immigration policies and practices toward Mexico and the U.S.-Mexican border.

subject: CH ST
title: El Plan de Santa Barbara, El Centro Arnulfo Casillas, and UCSB Chicanx/Latinx Student Activism, 1960s-Present
description: Examines the history of UCSB Chicanx/Latinx student activism on campus from the late 1960s until the present. Starting with the April 1969 El Plan de Santa Barbara conference, the class examines critical events such as the 1968 and 1975 North Hall protests, the 1989 and 1994 hunger strikes, and the student-led movement to save El Centro from demolition in the mid-2010s. Special focus is placed on conducting archival research on Chicanx/Latinx student activism and solidifying El Centro Arnulfo Casillas a sacred site/home for future generations of students, particularly those engaged in struggles to decolonize the university.

title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

subject: CH ST
title: Maya History & Resistance
description: The course examines Maya History and Resistance in the Mayab’, or where the Maya live/are. It attempts to de-center the nation-state, while also recognizing the ways that governments have played a role in repressing Indigenous Peoples. The course analyzes the Maya through time and space, with each week focusing on a particular topic.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

subject: CH ST
title: Environmental Justice in Central America
description: Examine environmental justice issues in Central America through the history of environmental social movements, with a focus on campesino, Indigenous, and Black resistance to extractivist industries such as mining and hydroelectric projects. Topics covered include environmental degradation, climate change, forced displacement and alternative forms of development.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

subject: CH ST
title: Indigenous Latinx Migrations
description: Through an examination of national and Indigenous contexts, this course considers how race and migration to the United States affects Indigenous peoples from Latin America. For many Indigenous Latinx immigrants, the racism and discrimination they experience in the United States is informed by both settler colonialism in the United States as well as the racist logics of their home countries. Given that both contexts shape Indigenous immigrants’ experiences, students will think about injustice and resistance across borders. Students will explore how Indigenous migration complicates and transforms notions of Latinidad in ways that are generative and that have shaped labor, social movements, gender dynamics, and the field of Chicana/o Studies.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

title: UCSB-Universidad Ixil (Guatemala): Caminos Futuros
description: Examines Indigenous ways of knowing and education, and decolonizing knowledges, and is taught in collaboration with the Ixil University in Guatemala. The course is a result of years or organizing and seeks committed students who will collectively examine a range of themes and topics related to Maya history, culture, representation, resistance, and other indigenous concepts. The course and readings are taught in Spanish, and students are required to have a fluency in Spanish.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

subject: CH ST
title: Internship in Poverty, Inequality, and Social Justice
description: Students gain practical experience by working in organizations or initiatives engaged in addressing poverty and inequality through policy analysis, advocacy, direct social provision, community action, and/or political organizing. Opportunities to cultivate problem-solving, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills needed to work effectively in institutional or collectively organized settings and to gain exposure to professional, post-graduate education and training, and related career opportunities in anti-poverty and social justice fields. Students work under faculty supervision to produce reports, a research paper, or other types of creative material based on their experiences.
advisor_comments: This course fulfills a requirement for the Minor in Poverty, Inequality, and Social Justice (HIST). Must be taken for a letter grade. CH ST 196SJ, HIST 196SJ, & GLOBL 196SJ are the same course.

title: Honors Project Seminar
description: Seminar for the development of the honors research project. Emphasis is on the design of the project and the establishment of methodologies to be utilized. Background and initial research is undertaken.
prereq_text: Acceptance into the Chicana and Chicano Studies honors program; senior standing; consent of department; open to Chicana and Chicano Studies majors only.

description: Independent research comprising the bulk of the data acquisition and organization for the honors project.

description: Allows students to complete the writing of the honors thesis. Time is allotted to prepare a presentation of the project before an audience of peers and faculty members.

description: Independent studies in Chicana/o students under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Students wishing to enroll should prepare a short plan of study.

description: Examines critical theories and methods in the production of historical narratives, social myths, and ideologies of racialization and ethnicity. Special attention is given to employment strategies, tropes, and allegorical forms in the construction of historical events and narratives.

subject: CH ST
title: Social Processes
description: Explores critical theories and methods in the production of knowledge relevant to social, political, economic, and institutional structures. Special attention is given to interdisciplinary articulations with theories and methods in the humanities.

subject: CH ST
title: Cultural Texts
description: Explores critical theories and methods in the production of cultural knowledge in the humanities. Special attention is given to interdisciplinary articulations with theories and methods in the social sciences.

subject: CH ST
title: Research Seminar
description: Introduces students to the practice of original research in the interdisciplinary field of Chicana and Chicano Studies, including articulating a research problem, placing it within theoretical discussions, selecting appropriate methods, and analyzing and writing data, results, and/or findings.

subject: CH ST
title: Interdisciplinary Methods
description: A critical introduction to a broad range of approaches and methodologies used in Chicana and Chicano Studies. These methods include (but are not limited to) fieldwork, archival and historical research, textual analysis, action research, visual production, political economy, and statistics.

subject: CH ST
title: Ethnography & Ethnographic Methods
description: This course examines the epistemology, ethics, and politics of ethnographic fieldwork and is designed to provide students with the methodological tools to conduct ethnographic research. Through close reading and seminar discussions, students reflect on the origins of ethnographic inquiry and engage with decolonial responses to Western ethnographic inquiry. Having developed a critical understanding of ethnographic research as theory and method in the first half of the course, students develop and workshop their own ethnographic research project and gain hands-on experience collecting, analyzing, and writing up ethnographic data.

subject: CH ST
title: De-Colonizing Feminism
description: Key writings by US feminists-of-color have transformed intellectual and cultural production, and re-generated new modes of de-colonizing philosophy. Graduate students write a substantial paper. They also participate in organizing and leading class discussions on a rotating basis.

subject: CH ST
title: Indigenous Texts
description: Treats translations of primary indigenous documents. Investigates the oral performance inherent to written indigenous records. Attention focuses on the Popol Vuh and the Codex Chimalpopoca, but Classic Maya hieroglyphic texts and Aztec codices are considered as well.

subject: CH ST
title: Reading Anzalda: Text, Context, and Interpretation
description: Seminar surveys the major and minor works of Chicana feminist thinker Gloria Anzalda and considers the influence that her work has had in a range of disciplines, from Chicana/o Studies and queer theory to political science and philosophy.

subject: CH ST
title: Globalization and Immigration
description: Tracks the migration of people and cultures across national boundaries, focusing on the itinerary of Mexican migrations to the U.S., with selected examples of migrations into Europe. Attention is paid to the changing significance of the nation.

subject: CH ST
title: Teaching Assistant and Associate Training
description: Supervised teaching of lower division Chicana/o Studies courses. Required participation in occasional workshops related to teaching.
advisor_comments: Units earned do not apply toward completion of advanced degrees. S/U grading only. Required of all teaching assistants in Chicana and Chicano Studies.

subject: CH ST
title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
description: Introduces incoming Teaching Assistants to key campus resources and services available to graduate and undergraduate students. It is intended to foster an ongoing dialogue about teaching within the academy.

subject: CH ST
title: Introduction to Graduate School
description: Introduces the new cohort of graduate students to the graduate program. The purpose is broadly defined as providing information, discussing Department norms, answering questions from graduate students, attending Department events and discussions to explore questions on research and graduate training. This course is open to new directions and incorporation of new topics and activities according to each new graduate cohort.

subject: CH ST
title: Special Topics in Chicano Studies
description: Designed to allow courses of varying topics in areas of expertise of visiting professors to broaden opportunities for students. Examples might be: immigration, Native American, Mexican, or Latin American influences on the Chicano, legal issues, the migrants.
advisor_comments: Course may be taken up to three times (12 units) providing the letter designations are different.

subject: CH ST
title: Independent Studies
description: Independent study under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers students the opportunity to undertake independent study or work in a group.
advisor_comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.

subject: CH STW
title: Maya History & Resistance
description: The course examines Maya History and Resistance in the Mayab’, or where the Maya live/are. It attempts to de-center the nation-state, while also recognizing the ways that governments have played a role in repressing Indigenous Peoples. The course analyzes the Maya through time and space, with each week focusing on a particular topic.
advisor_comments: CH STW 116 is the online version of CH ST 116

subject: CH STW
title: Chicana Writers
description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Feminist theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry and dramatic works written by such authors as Sandra Cisneros, Ana Castillo, Helen Viramontes, and others.
advisor_comments: CH STW 184A is the online version of CH ST 184A.
prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.

subject: CH STW
title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.
repeat_comments: CH STW 1B is the online version of CH ST 1B.

subject: CH STW
title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
description: This course explores contemporary Chicana/x cultural practices—from music, fashion, poster art, and murals to perspectives on social identities and sexualities. Focusing on culture, race, class, gender, and ideas of “home,” we examine how traditions and rituals reflect national and transnational politics. Drawing from Chicana/o Studies, Sound Studies, Feminist Studies, Art, and Media Studies, we analyze how communities use cultural practices to navigate, resist, and speak against injustice.
repeat_comments: CH STW 1C is the online version of CH ST 1C.

description: Includes fundamental topics, such as matter, measurements, atomic/electronic structure, atomic theories, bonding, reactions, and stoichiometry.
advisor_comments: Designed as a preparatory course for Chemistry 1A. Intended for students with limited or no high school chemistry background, and/or students who received an SAT Math Score of 550 or below.

subject: CHEM
title: Undergraduate Seminar
description: Seminars for undergraduates presented by faculty, guest speakers, and/or students.

subject: CHEM
title: SciTrek 2nd-12th Science Outreach
description: This course allows students to earn 1 unit of credit for serving as a mentor in the SciTrek program, a 2nd -12th grade science outreach program. Students will receive activity specific training on working with elementary or secondary students and then implement that training in an elementary or secondary classroom.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Research
description: Directed study, normally experimental, to be arranged with individual faculty members. Course offers exceptional students an opportunity to participate in a research group. Basic techniques and the operation of instruments used in research. A few students in chemistry are quite advanced having had extensive laboratory training in high school or elsewhere. This course allows them the opportunity to participate in a research group before they acquire 84 units and are then eligible for and capable of handling 199, Independent Studies.
advisor_comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.

subject: CHEM
title: Teaching Chemistry at the High School/Junior High Level
description: Students will work to develop a high school/junior high curriculum unit. In addition, students will work in either a high school or junior high classroom and share their experiences through class discussions. Students will also have the opportunity to participate in one of two elementary outreach programs that are run out of the chemistry department.
advisor_comments: Upper Division course credit toward Science and Mathematics Education minor. Will not count towards the Biochemistry, Chemistry BA or Chemistry BS major requirements.

subject: CHEM
title: The Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
description: Framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis is on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.
advisor_comments: Equivalent upper-division coursework in thermodynamics and kinetics from outside of department will be considered. CHEM 104 and CH E 141 are the same course.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry
description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109AH.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, and nomenclature of organic molecules including alcohols, radicals, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and carboxylic acid derivatives, and aromatic rings. Other topics include organometallic compounds and reactions at the alpha carbon. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 109B or 109BH.
repeat_comments: CHEM 130B can be taken as a legal repeat of CHEM 109B.
prereq_text: Chemistry 130A, 109A or 109AH with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis and nomenclature of organic molecules including aromatic heterocycles, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes, lipids, polymers, and their mechanisms. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed 109CH.
repeat_comments: CHEM 130C can be taken as a legal repeat of CHEM 109C (or CHEM W 109C).
prereq_text: Chemistry 130B, 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallics in Organic Synthesis
description: Synthetic methods and applications to natural products total syntheses involving transition metals.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Synthetic Chemistry
description: A comprehensive discussion of modern synthetic organic methods, including the applications of addition, condensation, substitution, and rearrangement reactions for building complicated molecules from scratch.
prereq_text: Chemistry 109A-B-C; upper-division standing; open to chemistry, biochemistry, and CCS chemistry and biochemistry majors only.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Synthesis of Biological Molecules
description: The synthesis, manipulation, and modification of biological molecules including peptides, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other metabolites are essential to advances in biomedicine. This course surveys chemical methods for the production of these molecules and their application to biological problems.

subject: CHEM
title: Epigenetics: Biology, Mechanisms and Therapies
description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants, mammals, imprinting, gene regulation, repeat-induced point mutation (RIP), X-chromosome inactivation, epigenetic mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, and epigentically based therapeutics and pharmaco-epigenetics.
prereq_text: Chemistry W142A or 142A, 142B-C; or, MCDB 108A-B-C; upper-division standing.

subject: CHEM
title: Biochemistry
description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.
prereq_text: Chemistry 107A-B-C or 109A or 109AH-109B or 109BH-109C or 109CH or W 109C
prereq_gold: CHEM 107C or CHEM 109C or CHEM 109CH or CHEM W 109C; CHEM 107A or CHEM 109A or CHEM 109AH; CHEM 107B or CHEM 109B or CHEM 109BH

subject: CHEM
title: Biochemistry
description: Chemical aspects of intermediary metabolism. The chemistry and elementary dynamic properties of enzymes; study of enzyme active sites; characterization of metabolic pathways and methods of examining cellular regulation.

subject: CHEM
title: Biochemistry
description: Macromolecular biosynthesis and specialized cellular processes. A survey of nucleic acid and protein biosynthesis, characterization of lipids and membranes; function of membranes in transport, energy transduction, and cellular control; mechanisms of muscle contraction and cell motility.

subject: CHEM
title: The RNA World
description: Introduction to RNA structure and thermodynamics. Biological roles of RNA in contemporary organisms. Implications for the origins of life.

subject: CHEM
title: Computational Biochemistry
description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.
advisor_comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 245 and BMB 245.
prereq_text: Chemistry 113A-B or Chemistry 112A-B; and, Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.

subject: CHEM
title: Astrobiology and the Origins of Life
description: Discusses the origins and evolution of the solar system and the earth, the origins and evolution of life on earth, and the possibilities for life elsewhere in the cosmos, all from the perspective of contemporary, terrain biochemistry.
prereq_text: Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.

subject: CHEM
title: How Science Works
description: Combined lab and discussion course on how science works. Includes three labs on student-generated questions. Discussions include the analysis of research papers, science controversies, how science defines new areas of ignorance, and the observation of research group meetings.
advisor_comments: This course requires attendance/participation in a lab once (three to four hours) during three different weeks of the quarter.

subject: CHEM
title: Analytical Chemistry
description: Principles of analytical chemistry including classical techniques, spectrophotochemistry, electroanalytical techniques, and separation processes.
prereq_gold: (CHEM 1A and CHEM 1B and CHEM 1C) or (CHEM 2A and CHEM 2B and CHEM 2C)

subject: CHEM
title: Post-translational Protein Processing
description: Structure/function relationships in interesting macromolecules isolated from marine organisms. Focus is on well-characterized pathways from horseshoe crabs, abolones, mussels, and fish as well as others.
advisor_comments: Same course as MCDB 145.
prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A or CHEM 142A or CHEM W142A with a grade of C or better.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Analytical Techniques
description: Principles of analytical methodology, as in spectroscopy, electroanalysis, and chromatography. Applications to environmental problems, forensic and clinical analysis, and industry. Analysis of solids and surfaces.
advisor_comments: Designed for graduating seniors.

subject: CHEM
title: Enzyme Mechanisms
description: Chemistry, structure and function of enzymes; theory, experimental design, and data analysis. Enzyme models and non-classical enzymes.
prereq_gold: (CHEM 142A and CHEM 142B and CHEM 112B) or (MCDB 108A and MCDB 108B and CHEM 112B)

subject: CHEM
title: Drug Design
description: Sources for new drugs. Biochemistry of diseases. Target validation techniques. Mechanism of action of enzymes and receptors. Enzyme inhibition and receptor binding studies. Structure based drug design: conformational analysis, docking and binding affinity calculations. Course also teaches proposal writing skills.
prereq_gold: (CHEM 142A and CHEM 142B and CHEM 142C) or (CHEM W 142A and CHEM 142B and CHEM 142C) or (MCDB 108A and MCDB 108B and MCDB 108C)

subject: CHEM
title: Drug Design
description: Medical chemistry for lead optimization, combinatorial synthesis, quantitative structure-activity relationships, pharmocokinetics, drug metabolism and toxicity, pharmacogenomics. Drugs that interact with DNA and protein drugs. Clinical trials, intellectual property in drug design. Students develop their own drug design project.

subject: CHEM
title: Arrow Pushing in Organic Chemistry
description: Covers the arrow pushing formalism and addresses organic reactions from this perspective.
prereq_text: Chemistry 109A-B-C; upper-division standing; open to chemistry, biochemistry, and CCS chemistry and biochemistry majors only.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
description: Selected topics in bioinorganic chemistry, and metallo-biochemistry. Discussions of metalloproteins and corresponding model compound investigations. Emphasis will be on reaction mechanisms and spectroscopy or properties of metal sites.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure Determination by X-ray Diffraction
description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and Fourier series

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Models for bonding in molecules of nontransition and transition elements. Applications of symmetry to bonding, electronic and vibrational spectroscopy. Stereochemistry of transition metal complexes and introduction to organometallics.
prereq_gold: (CHEM 113A and CHEM 113B and CHEM 113C) or (CHEM 112A and CHEM 112B and CHEM 112C)

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Structures of ordered crystalline solids, X-Ray crystallography. Introduction to solid state chemistry, inorganic materials and chemical catalysis. Bioinorganic chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry
description: Bonding theory, thermodynamics, and structure of inorganic compounds. Applications of physical techniques to the study of inorganic (and organometallic) reactions and their mechanisms.
advisor_comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 275.

subject: CHEM
title: Photochemical and Photophysical Properties of Inorganic and Organometallic Compounds and Materials
description: Discussion of the mechanisms of fundamental physical and chemical events which follow absorption of light by inorganic and organometallic chromophores. Consideration of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems as well as the design and operation of photo-optical and photoelectrical devices.
advisor_comments: Offered concurrently with Chemistry 276.

subject: CHEM
title: Protein Crystallography
description: Introduction to diffraction techniques. Protein crystal growth and morphology. Data collection and reduction strategies. Approaches for solving the phase problem. Crystallographic refinement, including molecular dynamics. Interpretation of crystal structures.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Teaching in Chemistry
description: Students will assist the teaching assistant in teaching a lab course in which the student previously received a grade of A- or better. Activities will be determined in consultation with the instructor and include instruction of 1 or 2 lab sections per week. Undergraduates enrolled in Chem 183 are learning assistants (LAs) in the general chemistry laboratory. LAs teach and mentor first-year university students. LAs assist students with experiments, lab technique, data analysis, calculations, learning chemistry concepts, and problem solving. As the LAs learn STEM education pedagogy, they can practice what they learn as LAs in the chemistry lab.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 5 units. May not be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing, a chemistry grade point average of 3.5 or above and consent of instructor.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Literature
description: Lectures and exercises on the literature and other information resources of use in chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallic Chemistry: Structure, Bonding, and Applications
description: Synthesis, structure, and reactivity of organometallic complexes, with an emphasis on bonding and electronic structure. Homogeneous catalysis and small molecule activation, especially in the context of the energy conversion and storage, will also be discussed.

subject: CHEM
title: Honors Research Seminar
description: Independent research project carried out under the supervision of faculty member. Goal is to write an original, publishable, research paper. The project can be on a topic of the student's choice, or it can be an extension of an ongoing research project under the direction of a faculty member in the department.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.5 GPA. No units may be applied to the major. An application must be completed and submitted to the undergrad advisor early in the first quarter of the senior year. Students successfully completing the program are eligible to graduate with Distinction in the Major.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor and department.

subject: CHEM
title: Internship in Chemistry
description: Opportunity to obtain practical non paid chemistry-related research and work experience by working under faculty and/or staff direction as an intern.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA. No units may be applied to the major. An application must be completed and submitted to the department chair.
prereq_text: Chem 1AL, 1BL, 1CL, and consent of Chem instructor.

subject: CHEM
title: Teaching, Mentoring, or Research in K-12 STEM Education
description: This course allows students to earn 1 unit per 32-40 hours of work in a given quarter with a K-12 science outreach program. Students will do one or more of the following activities with the program: mentor K-12 students, help with program operations, or help with research on the program.

subject: CHEM
title: Special Topics
description: Special topics and courses as a means of meeting special curriculum needs.
advisor_comments: Chem 196 may apply to major requirements by petition only.

subject: CHEM
title: Research in Chemical Education
description: Coursework shall consist of research in chemical education supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internship credit.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters.
repeat_comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing in a physical science, life science, or engineering major.

subject: CHEM
title: Independent Studies
description: Coursework shall consist of academic research supervised by a faculty member. This course is not intended for internship credit.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing in the major; completion of two upper division courses in chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
description: The course provides a framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis will be on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.
advisor_comments: Same course as Ch E 241.

subject: CHEM
title: Electrochemistry
description: Theory and applications of electrochemistry. Thermodynamics and kinetics. Discussion of practical technologies, including batteries, fuel cells, electrolysis, electroplating, biosensors and/or other selected topics.
advisor_comments: Not open to students who have completed CHEM 114AL or 214AL

subject: CHEM
title: Statistical Mechanics
description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics, partition functions for ideal gases and crystals, quantum statistics, calculations of thermodynamic properties.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 117A.

subject: CHEM
title: Statistical Mechanics
description: Fundamentals of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, kinetic theory of gases, Boltzmann equation, correlation functions, linear response theory, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations.

subject: CHEM
title: Photochemistry and Radiation Chemistry
description: Interaction of light and matter, reaction paths from electonically excited molecules, flash photolysis, high energy radiation.
prereq_text: Open only by consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

subject: CHEM
title: Selected Topics in Physical Chemistry
description: The content of this course will vary and will cover a range of topics and disciplines, including: orbital symmetry rules for chemical reactions; classical theory of light, radiation, and spectroscopy; electronic structure theory, catalysis, biophysics, and theoretical chemistry.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated with a different topic (18 units maximum).

subject: CHEM
title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
description: Introduction to quantum mechanics-postulatory approach; particle in box, on ring, harmonic oscillator; lineral operator theory, matrix algebra; hydrogen atom; perturbation theory, variation theory; applications.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.

subject: CHEM
title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
description: Molecular Orbital theory and Valence Bond theory (Secular Equ.) applications to conjugated systems, electronic spectra, and term symbols; introduction to infrared, raman, and microwave spectroscopy.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.

subject: CHEM
title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
description: Introduction to NMR, EPR, group theory; applications.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 115A-B-C.

subject: CHEM
title: Current Events in Organic Chemistry
description: Faculty and students present and critically discuss current chemical literature.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Spectroscopic Analysis
description: Structure determination of complex organic molecules. Topics include NMR, IR, UV, and mass spectrometry.

subject: CHEM
title: Computational Chemistry
description: Introduction to computational chemistry and molecular modeling. Applications of molecular mechanics, quantum mechanics, and computer graphical interfaces to problems in chemistry, biochemistry, drug design, and pharmacology.

subject: CHEM
title: Structure and Reactivity in Organic Chemistry
description: Electronic structure, resonance, acid/base chemistry, thermodynamics, kinetics, transition state theory, and isotope effects.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
description: Mechanisms of thermal, photochemical, organometallic, electrochemical, asymmetric or other processes in organic chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthetic Organic Reactions
description: A survey of reactions of organic substances with emphasis on those with practical synthetic utility, including discussion of mechanism, scope and limitations, and stereochemical issues.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallics in Organic Synthesis
description: Synthetic methods and applications to natural products total syntheses involving transition metals.
advisor_comments: Designed for majors. Concurrently offered with 132. Quarters usually offered: Spring.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Synthesis of Biological Molecules
description: The synthesis, manipulation, and modification of biological molecules including peptides, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other metabolites are essential to advances in biomedicine. This course surveys chemical methods for the production of these molecules and their application to biological problems.

subject: CHEM
title: Selected Topics in Organic Chemistry
description: Selected topics from organic chemistry. Contents of the course will vary.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Complex Molecule Synthesis
description: Original contributions in the area of complex molecule total synthesis based on the most recent literature. Focus is on synthesis strategy and design, and any unusual chemistry transpired in the course of synthesis with complex substrates and intermediates.
advisor_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Molecular Photoswitches: Chemistry, Properties and Applications
description: This course covers the emerging field of photoswitches and their applications in materials science and biology.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Methods for Asymmetric Synthesis
description: Surveys synthetically useful methods for stereoselective organic synthesis. The general principles underlying these processes are discussed. Applications of these methods are then examined in the context of target oriented synthesis.
advisor_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Carbohydrate Synthesis and Basic Glycobiology
description: Course topics include: Monosaccharide, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides – structure, biosynthesis and function; Chemical glycosylation: general synthetic approaches and the state-of-the-art stereoselective glycosylation; Chemoenzymatic glycan synthesis; Bioactive glycosylated nature products and examples of their synthesis; Glycomedicine and carbohydrate-based vaccines.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Epigenetics: Biology, Mechanisms and Therapies
description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants, mammals, imprinting, gene regulation, repeat-induced point mutation (RIP), X-chromosome inactivation, epigenetic mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, and epigentically based therapeutics and pharmaco-epigenetics.
prereq_text: Chemistry W142A or 142A, 142B-C; or, MCDB 108A-B-C; graduate standing.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.
prereq_text: Open only by consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
description: Chemical aspects of intermediary metabolism. The chemistry and elementary dynamic properties of enzymes; study of enzyme active sites; characterization of metabolic pathways and methods of examining cellular regulation.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Aspects of Biological Systems
description: Macromolecular biosynthesis and specialized cellular processes. A survey of nucleic acid and protein biosynthesis, characterization of lipids and membranes; function of membranes in transport, energy transduction, and cellular control; mechanisms of muscle contraction and cell motility; neurochemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: The RNA World
description: Introduction to RNA structure and thermodynamics. Biological roles of RNA in contemporary organisms. Implications for the origins of life.

subject: CHEM
title: Informational Macro- and Supra-Molecules
description: Selected topics at the interface of chemistry and biology; informational molecular coding, molecular machines, self-assembling and self-replicating molecular systems, evolution and selection of molecules with binding and catalytic properties, biopolymer-based materials, special emphasis on cutting-edge technologies.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 244.

subject: CHEM
title: Computational Biochemistry
description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.
advisor_comments: CHEM 245 and IQB 245 are the same course.

subject: CHEM
title: Membrane Biochemistry
description: Introduction to the structures and roles of lipids an their behavior, liposomes, membrane proteins and kinetics, protein sorting, and signal transduction.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 246

subject: CHEM
title: Strategy in Organic Synthesis and Methodology
description: The design, development, presentation, and organization of new concepts for organic synthesis and methodologies is an essential skill for graduate students. Course focuses on advances in these areas and developing skills for writing and presenting research proposals.

subject: CHEM
title: Selected Topics in Biological Chemistry
description: Selected topics from bio-organic, biophysical, or biological chemistry. The content of this course will vary.
advisor_comments: CHEM 259 and IQB 259 are the same course.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Stimuli-Responsive Materials for Biomedical Applications
description: Stimuli-responsive chemistries and materials are programmed to react in the presence of changes in their surrounding environment to produce a measurable output, such as a change in shape, release of active moiety, assembly, or mechanical output. Examples of stimuli can include electric field, magnetic, thermal, light,** mechanical, pH, ROS, enzyme, glucose, and others (e.g. salts, solvents, electron beam). We will discuss the properties, design, and applications of these stimuli-responsive materials that have aided the development of active-, as opposed to passive, biomaterials for the advancement of biomedicine. This course makes use of modern scientific literature to discuss the topics at hand.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioenergetics
description: The study of biological energy transduction, with emphasis on physical constraints, raw materials, mechanisms, and evolution of metabolism.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Emerging Methods and Applications of Cryogenic Three-Dimensional Transmission Electron Microscopy
description: Course covers the fundamentals and current state of the art of 3D cryogenic electron microscopy, the theory and a diverse set of applications: 3D single particle methods, correlative light and electron microscopy & cryogenic in situ tomography; provides a solid foundation for 3D cryo-EM and an opportunity to network with the cryo-EM community; features lecturers and renowned leaders in the field presenting their work, interactive and practical exercises: basic sample handling, sample preparation protocols & an introduction to computational analysis on a preselected dataset. Course requirements: reading classic and/or representative papers, presenting papers prior to respective lectures and a final written report on a chosen cryo-EM topic.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: ENZYME, COENZYME & METABOLIC PATHWAYS
description: This course reviews the latest discoveries in biochemistry, including new enzymatic functions, cofactor biosynthesis, and metabolic pathways for secondary metabolites. Students with a strong background in organic chemistry and a keen interest in biochemistry are encouraged to take this course.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Gene Therapy
description: The field of gene therapy is inherently interdisciplinary, drawing on concepts and tools from molecular biology, biochemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, and synthetic biology. This course will delve into a wide array of topics at the intersection of the aforementioned disciplines, including gene delivery, reporter gene imaging, viral and non-viral vectors, genetic editing, metabolic disease, clinical trial design, FDA-approved gene therapies, and the social/ethical considerations surrounding gene therapy.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Epigenetics
description: Covers epigenetic processes and molecular mechanisms in bacteria, fungi, plants and mammals. Topics include: Epigenetic processes - Parental and maternal imprinting, Gene regulation, Repeat-induced point mutation, X-chromosome inactivation Epigenetic mechanisms - DNA methylation/histone modification/chromatin remodeling, RNA silencing, Methods of detection including patterns of DNA methylation Applications - Epigentically based therapeutics, Pharmaco-epigenetics
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 259.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Enzyme Mechanisms
description: Chemistry, structure, and function of enzymes; theory, experimental design,and data analysis. Enzyme models and non-classical enzymes.

subject: CHEM
title: Drug Design
description: Sources for new drugs. Biochemistry of diseases. Target validation techniques. Mechanism of action of enzymes and receptors. Enzyme inhibition and receptor binding studies. Structure base drug design: conformational analysis, docking and binding affinity calculations. Course also teaches proposal writing skills.

subject: CHEM
title: Drug Design
description: Medicinal chemistry for lead optimization, combinatorial synthesis, quantitative structure-activity relationships, pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and toxicity, pharmacogenomics. Drugs that interact with DNA and Protein drugs. Clinical trials, intellectual property in drug design. Students develop their own drug design project.

subject: CHEM
title: Arrow Pushing in Organic Chemistry
description: Covers the arrow pushing fomulasism and addresses molecular rearrangements and other organic reactions from this perspective.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Catalysis
description: Theories of reaction rates. Heterogeneous and homogenous catalysis, including physical structure and characterization of catalysts. Catalyst poisoning.
repeat_comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 240C and Chemical Engineering 246.

subject: CHEM
title: Photophysics and Device Science of Organic Materials
description: Examination of what happens when organic molecules absorb a photon or when they are incorporated within an optoelectric device. Specific subjects include phtoexcitation and relaxation processes, energy transfer, flourescence depolarization, the design of flourescence-based biosensors, organic light emitting diodes and field effect transistors.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Models for bonding in molecules of nontransition and transition elements. Applications of symmetry to bonding, electronic and vibrational spectroscopy. Stereochemistry of transition metal complexes and introduction to organo- metallics.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 173A, or 272A.
prereq_text: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Structures of ordered crystalline solids, x-ray crystallography. Introduction to solid state chemistry, inorganic materials and chemical catalysis. Bioinorganic chemistry.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Chemistry 173B or 272B.
prereq_text: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
description: Selected topics in bioinorganic chemistry and metal-lobiochemistry with a major focus on recent developments. Topics will include discussions of metalloproteins and corresponding model compound investigations. Emphasis will be on reaction mechanisms and spectroscopic properties of metal sites.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Properties of Macromolecules
description: Basics of preparation of polymer and macromolecular assemblies, and characterization of large molecules and assemblies. Discussion of chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.
repeat_comments: MATRL 271A and CHEM 271A are the same course.

subject: CHEM
title: Reaction Mechanisms in Organometallic and Inorganic Chemistry
description: Discussion of chemical reaction mechanisms. Emphasis will be on fundamental reactions of metal compounds such as substitution, addition, elimination, and redox reactions for homogenous catalysis mechanisms and other complex systems.

subject: CHEM
title: Structural Inorganic Chemistry
description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and fourier series.
advisor_comments: Same course as Materials 241.

subject: CHEM
title: Solid State Inorganic/Materials
description: An introductory course describing the synthesis, physical characterization, structure, electronic properties and uses of solid state materials.
advisor_comments: Same course as Materials 274.

subject: CHEM
title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry
description: Bonding theory, thermodynamics, and structure of inorganic compounds. Applications of physical techniques to the study of inorganic (and organometallic) reactions and their mechanisms.

subject: CHEM
title: Photochemical and Photophysical Properties of Inorganic and Organometallic Compounds and Materials
description: Discussion of the mechanics of fundamental physical and chemical events which follow absorption of light by inorganic or organometallic chromophores. Consideration of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems as well as the design and operation of photo-optical and photoelectrical devices.

subject: CHEM
title: Introduction to Inorganic Materials
description: Structures of inorganic materials: close-packing, linking of simple polyhedra. Factors that control structure: ionic radii, covalency, ligand field effects, metal-metal bonding, electron/ atom ratios. Structure-property relationships in e.g. spinels, garnets, perovskites, rutiles, flourites, zeolites, b-aluminas, graphites, common inorganic glasses.
advisor_comments: Same course as Materials 218.

subject: CHEM
title: Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
description: This course is designed to reflect recent developments in inorganic chemistry.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
description: Radioactive decay kinetics and energetics, nuclear models, nuclear reactions, radiation detection, radiochemical techniques, and applications of radioactivity.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Sustainability (with a Chemistry Emphasis)
description: This course will address and identify a number of issues in sustainability that are challenging a sustainable world and the potential research and technical opportunities for addressing these. Topics include: Climate Change—causes and effects; Environmental Monitoring; Energy – production and storage; Chemical resources - challenges and solutions; Recycling; Sustainable Materials; Research and Development Opportunities; Intellectual Property and Innovation.
repeat_comments: May be repeated provided topics are different. Only 18 units of total credit may apply to the major.

subject: CHEM
title: Protein Crystallography
description: Introduction to diffraction techniques. protein crystal growth and morphology. Data collection and reduction strategies. Approaches for solving the phase problem. Crystallographic refinement, including molecular dynamics. Interpretation of crystal structures.

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Bonding of Small Conjugated Molecules
description: Examination of small organic molecules used in optoelectronic devices: film transistors; light emitting diodes and solar cells. Methods for their synthesis. Influence of molecular structure on energies of molecular orbitals. Development of structure/function relationships based on solid state arrangements.

subject: CHEM
title: Instrumental Methods in Materials Chemistry
description: Principles and practice of advanced research instrumentation for soft materials characterization including spectroscopy, microscopy, and X-ray techniques

subject: CHEM
title: Chemical Literature
description: Lectures and exercises on the literature and other information resources of use in chemistry.
advisor_comments: Does not count toward core academic units for the Chemistry PhD program.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallic Chemistry: Structure, Bonding, and Applications
description: Synthesis, structure, and reactivity of organometallic complexes, with an emphasis on bonding and electronic structure. Homogeneous catalysis and small molecule activation, especially in the context of the energy conversion and storage, will also be discussed. Graduate students will be required to demonstrate a deeper understanding of the course material during class discussions and in submitted work. Graduate students will additionally be graded separately on all course work, including exams.

subject: CHEM

description: Examines Chinese popular religion, Daoism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Christianity, and Islam as shaped and transformed by revolution and nationalism, and the recent rapid commercialization, urbanization, and globalization of China. Religiosity and changing notions of self, family, gender, community, and citizenship.
advisor_comments: Chinese 32 and Religious Studies 32 are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Popular Culture in Modern Chinese Societies
description: Provides an overview of Chinese popular culture from PRC, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, covering various media and genres such as popular literature, film, online culture, music, video games, and cartoons.

subject: CHIN
title: Introduction to Chinese Medicine
description: Looks at major concepts and practices that inform the plural traditions of Chinese medicine. Also considers the cultural and historical contexts in which these therapeutic traditions emerged as well as, briefly, their relation to other medical systems in Asia.
advisor_comments: Religious Studies 41 and Chinese 41 are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Global Yoga
description: This course examines the complex, transcultural, and entangled history of the contemporary global yoga phenomenon. It sheds light on the connection between modern transnational yoga and various posture-based systems of self-cultivation from Asia (India, Tibet, China) to Europe. It also considers the basic features of primarily physical modes of spiritual refinement.
advisor_comments: Religious Studies 42 and Chinese 42 are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Nature and Ethics in Chinese Philosophy
description: A look at how major thinkers in classical Chinese thought grappled with questions related to the individual's place in society and their relationship to their environment. Highlighting their relevance, classical views will be applied to contemporary ethical, social, and environmental debates.
advisor_comments: Religious Studies 48 and Chinese 48 are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Masterpieces in Chinese Literature
description: Examines a selection of works from Chinese literature, with the goal of understanding the major genres and their development over time. The cultural roles of literature, as well as criteria for critical evaluation, are also addressed.

subject: CHIN
title: Modern Chinese Literature
description: This course, taught in English, surveys an archive of seminal short fiction, novellas, novels, and poems that tell the story of China and the Chinese from the end of the Qing dynasty to the present. What has been the place of literature in China in the modern era? What vision of modern China do we find in its literature? How, moreover, does literature subvert the national narrative? Through literature as a window on the history of modern China, students gain a better understanding of Chinese history and culture with regard to its social reform, revolution, war, cultural revolution, cultural revival, and economic growth.
advisor_comments: Chinese 82 and Comparative Literature 82 are the same course.

subject: CHIN

subject: CHIN
title: Readings in Taiwan Literature
description: Offers a close reading of postwar Taiwan and exile literature from the 1940s to the present, and provides a basic introduction to literary criticism and analysis. Taught in English, the assigned texts are in traditional Chinese and English translations will be provided.

subject: CHIN
title: Readings in Taiwan Literature
description: Offers an in-depth study of Taiwans nativist literature from select authors and provides a basic introduction to literary criticism and analysis. Examines the motifs and visual expression in the readings and how these texts contributed to the distinct Taiwanese cultural identity. Taught in English, the assigned texts are in traditional Chinese and English translations will be provided.

subject: CHIN

description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from literary works, newspapers, internet, and films.
advisor_comments: Heritage and high-proficiency Chinese language students can contact the instructor for approval to enroll.

subject: CHIN

description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from literary works, newspapers, internet, and films.
advisor_comments: Heritage and high-proficiency Chinese language students can contact the instructor for approval to enroll.

title: Advanced Chinese in Practice III
description: Course series for students who have advanced levels in Chinese. Extensive reading and discussion of various styles and practices of the Chinese language in addition to topics on modern and contemporary China. Teaching materials from newspaper, internet, and films.

subject: CHIN
title: Chinese Painting I
description: Chinese painting and theory, from beginnings through the fourteenth century. Introduction to major developments and masters in their cultural context with a focus on meaning and agency.
advisor_comments: CHIN 134CA and ARTHI 134CA are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Art and Modern China
description: An exploration of trends and issues in nineteenth and twentieth-century Chinese art, as China awakens and responds to the challenges of modernity and the West. Topics include the continuity of tradition, the exile of identity, and the trends after Tiananmen (1989)
advisor_comments: ARTHI 134D is the same course as CHIN 134D.

subject: CHIN
title: Chinese Calligraphy- History and Aesthetics
description: Examines the different scripts in historical context, surveys significant movements and artists, and considers the ideas, theories and aesthetic principles that have enriched the art of writing to elite status in China.

subject: CHIN
title: Special Topics in Taiwan Studies - Humanities
description: Special topics in Taiwan studies with respect to literature, history, and culture from the period of Japanese rule (1895-1945) to the present, including modernity, national identity, intellectual movements, and popular culture. Topics and reads will vary with instructors.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit in the major to a maximum of 8 units providing topics are different.

subject: CHIN
title: Special Topics in Taiwan Studies - Social Science
description: Special topics in Taiwan studies with respect to historical, economic, political, cultural, and social changes in Taiwan from the period of Japanese rule (1895-1945) to the present. Topics and readings will vary with instructors.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit in the major to a maximum of 8 units providing topics are different

subject: CHIN
title: China in Translation: Theory, Art, History
description: Uses case studies of translations into and out of China--long regarded as a civilization distinct from the West--to explore themes in translation studies. Topics include ideograms, orientalism, modernization, world literature, annotation, musicality, poetic license, and adaptation.
advisor_comments: CHIN 139 and C LIT 139 are the same course.
repeat_comments: CHIN 139 and C LIT 139 are the same course.

subject: CHIN
title: Tang Literary History
description: Examines the history of literature during the celebrated Tang dynasty (618907). Focus on changes in literary norms, practices, and theory as they intersected with societal, political, intellectual, and religious developments. Also considers problems of historiography. Emphasis varies by quarter.

subject: CHIN
title: Urban Legends: Traditional Chinese Stories and Their Afterlives
description: Masterworks of fiction from the Ming and Qing periods as products of urban culture in late imperial and contemporary China. Stories by Feng Menglong, Li Yu, tales by Pu Songling, and excerpts from classic novels.

subject: CHIN
title: Women Writers of Late Imperial China
description: A study of Chinese women writers in the late imperial period (roughly 1500-1900), a newly rediscovered part of China's literary history. Examination of their personal lives and writings in relation to the Chinese literary tradition, women's history and feminist criticism.

subject: CHIN
title: Poetic Culture in late Imperial China and Beyond
description: An examination of the role poetry played in both social and individual lives in late imperial China, with particular attention to self-expression and literary community. Relevant practices in later times and in Japan and Korea are also covered.

subject: CHIN
title: Storytelling and Chinese Culture
description: Taught in Chinese, this course is designed to elucidate Chinese history and culture from the perspective of storytelling. Readings are original narrative texts from the Tang, Song, and Ming-Qing eras.
prereq_text: Reading knowledge and skills in advanced modern Chinese

subject: CHIN
title: History of Sexuality in China
description: Examines the role of gender and sexual relations in the development of politics, society, culture, and personal life in China and the Sinophone world.

subject: CHIN
title: Queer China, Crip China
description: In this course we study the representation of non-normative bodyminds and desires (e.g. disability and homosexuality) in modern Chinese literature and film. We discuss the meanings embedded in Chinese discourses of gender, sexuality, and disability; investigate how these discourses have been appropriated in the construction of a modern Chinese national identity; and connect our specific inquiry into Queer China and Crip China to our general attempt to answer the broader question of how the modern nation-state China has been imagined into being over the past century. Our approach is interdisciplinary, comparative, and transnational.

subject: CHIN
title: Taiwan Cinema
description: Explores Taiwan cinema in socio-political contexts. Emphasis on the creation of a cinematic experience that resonates globally while reflecting Taiwans unique identity, cultural heritage, and artistic vision. Specific themes or topics will vary depending on the instructor.

subject: CHIN
title: Fiction and Film in Contemporary China
description: Presents a critical historical overview of Chinese literature and film from 1949 to the present. In addition to writers and filmmakers from mainland China such as Mo Yan and Zhang Yimou, course considers literary and cinematic development from Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the Chinese diaspora.

subject: CHIN
title: Chinese Cinema: Nationalism and Globalism
description: A critical overview of some of the major cinematic trends in Chinese-language film over the past several decades. Works from the PRC, Taiwan and Hong Kong, as well as Chinese cinema will be considered in a global context.
