subject: FAMST
title: Directors: Kathryn Bigelow
description: Surveys Kathryn Bigelows work from her performance in the 1983 womens film classic Born in Flames, through her vampire-, cop-, surf-, sci-fi-genre films and, most recently, her highly-acclaimed war films. Her movies are both entertaining and complex, and reveal a deep love and knowledge of film genre and history as well as her distinctive, and very American, auteur vision.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated an unlimited number of times, provided the letter designations are different. Only eight units may be counted for credit in the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Directors: New Hollywood Cinema
description: Course considers the films of several significant male and female American directors in the context of the historically and critically important "New Hollywood Cinema" era, which many film critics and historians consider one of the film industry's "golden ages." In addition to exploring the theoretical notion of "auteurism" and its focus on the prominent themes and styles of an individual director's films, the course considers several factors that enabled the emergence and development of the so-called "New Hollywood" period, from the late 1960s until the early 80s, including films like Bonnie and Clyde, auteur criticism, film schools, Roger Corman, and television.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated an unlimited number of times, provided the letter designations are different. Only eight units may be counted for credit in the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Stanley Kubrick
description: A study in depth of the films of one or two filmmakers of international stature and significance.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated an unlimited number of times, provided the letter designations are different. Only eight units may be counted for credit in the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Directors: Satyajit Ray
description: This lecture course examines the career of Satyajit Ray, film director of the famed Apu Trilogy (1955-59) and recipient of a "Lifetime Achievement" Oscar. Celebrated as a modernist master, Ray was a towering postcolonial auteur who explored the challenges faced by modern Indian society. Still the best-selling author of young adult fiction in Bengali, his creativity also spanned music, the fine arts, and commercial graphic design. The course critically situates Ray's entire oeuvre in relation to the cultural milieus of mid-century Bengal, India, and the world.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated an unlimited number of times, provided the letter designations are different. Only eight units may be counted for credit in the major.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of SB or a class level of SS or a class level of SP or a class level of LM or FAMST 46

subject: FAMST
title: Directors: Star Wars
description: Class will explore the Star Wars franchise as an American phenomenon that became an international powerhouse by considering it in relation to the following: the origins of the blockbuster and the development of the super-blockbuster; George Lucas's inspiration and auteur influences; the significance of the franchise for subsequent Star Wars auteurs; and in terms of the franchise's enormous critical and fan responses.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated an unlimited number of times, provided the letter designations are different. Only eight units may be counted for credit in the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Women and Film: Feminist Perspectives
description: Survey of the major debates on questions of women and representation in contemporary film criticism. Topics to be covered include the representation of sexuality and the family in the Hollywood cinema; feminism and the avant-garde.

subject: FAMST
title: Film and Social Reality
description: An inquiry into the interrelationships between film and history and/or film and ideology. The course examines how cinema reflects and/or influences the attitudes of a society.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

subject: FAMST
title: Film and Social Reality: Algorithms and Culture
description: In this course, students take a critical design approach to analyze various algorithms (i.e., Search, PageRank), their relationship with their structured data (i.e., tweets), and their impact on contemporary infrastructures and social flows.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

subject: FAMST
title: Film and Social Reality: Black Auteurs
description: From the filmmaking interventions of Oscar Micheaux and Spencer Williams to Ivan Dixon, Ousmane Sembene Melvin Van Peebles, Gordon Parks, Spike Lee, Julie Dash, Charles Burnett, Oprah Winfrey, Tyler Perry, Issac Julien, John Akomfrah, Shonda Rhimes, Ava DuVernay, and Issa Rae and among many others, this course explores the cyclical rise, fall, and persistence of black media makers from the dawn of the global film industry to the present day digital media environment. This includes analyzing black auteurs within a transmedia context (film, TV, and New Media platforms).
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

subject: FAMST
title: Cinema and Censorship
description: This course provides a historical survey of film and television censorship from the origins of motion pictures to the early twenty-first century. The first half of the course places emphasis on specific censorship cases in the United States. We will study the foundations of the Motion Pictures Producers and Distributors of America, the Production Code Administration, the studio ratings system, and approaches to content regulation that have occurred since the ratings system was adopted in 1968. In the second half, we will take on case studies from around the world, examining films and controversies related to politics, religion, and sex.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

subject: FAMST
title: Film and Social Reality: The Essay Film
description: In this course we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw on a range of established practices including documentary, narrative, and avant-garde cinema forms. We emphasize the films’ relation to the archive and traditional research methods; history; political intervention and reflection; and critical engagement with visual representation and image making.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

title: Film and Social Reality

prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing; consent of department.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
description: Uses cultural studies as a critical paradigm to closely examine a particular topic or theme.
prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.

subject: FAMST
title: Asian American Digital Media
description: Explores Asian American digital media through a consideration of how Asian American racialization and technology have been co-constituted. This course covers a range of Asian American digital media from YouTube skits to makeup artistry to food creators and more.
prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of LM or a class level of SB or a class level of SP or a class level of SS or FAMST 46 or FAMST 70

subject: FAMST
title: Alchemy and Imagination
description: Uses cultural studies as a critical paradigm to closely examine a particular topic or theme.

subject: FAMST
title: Border Media
description: Examines the proliferation of border security technologies used to surveil, detect, categorize, detain, and deport people who cross borders without state permission. Together we explore global examples of border security regimes and resistance movements, including artist and activist media practices that expose and disrupt the violence of state borders, while inviting students to consider their own proximity to and lived experience of the US-Mexico border here in California.
prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of LM or a class level of SB or a class level of SP or a class level of SS or FAMST 46 or FAMST 70

subject: FAMST
title: Cinema in the Digital Age
description: Explores a range of issues related to the digitization of cinema’s production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics include digital cinematography’s relation to cinematic realism, the politics of digital special effects, and the representation of social media and digital devices in films.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Green Games
description: This course puts game studies in conversation with environmental science and media. Explore whether analog and digital games present unique opportunities to engage with ecological crisis and human-environment relations, and work with others to develop your own green game prototypes.

subject: FAMST
title: Gender and Sexuality in Film
description: A survey of gender and sexuality in film that traverses the onscreen and industrial representation of configurations of both gender and sexuality throughout history and transnationally. Along with film theory informed by feminist, queer, and critical race studies, topics may include the male gaze, the monstrous feminine, female subjectivity, the oppositional gaze, New Queer Cinema, industry inequities, and female and/or queer filmmakers. Each week, students will attend lecture and screening to become familiar with feminist and queer critical analytical tools to augment film analysis related to the many permutations of gender and sexuality articulated in film from early cinema to the present.
prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70 or upper-division standing.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of LM or a class level of SB or a class level of SP or a class level of SS or FAMST 46 or FAMST 70

subject: FAMST
title: Queer Media Histories and Historiography
description: This class explores the means by which queer filmmakers have used the work of others to reimagine their own individual and collective pasts, presents, and future possibilities.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies: Media, Technology and Society
description: This critical studies course explores how technology functions as part of media industries, societies, and cultures. Through lectures, screenings, and assignments, the course will help students understand technology as an array of objects, ideologies, fantasies, labor practices, and industrial formations.

subject: FAMST
title: Film Noir
description: Study of the conventional themes, structures, and visual motifs of the detective film. American films of the forties and fifties and contemporary American and European works will be considered.

subject: FAMST
title: Experimental Film
description: A survey of the experimental film tracing the major stylistic and thematic trends in the diverse movements that have considered themselves outside of the commercial narrative cinema. Bunuel, Dulac, Cocteau, Leger, Deren, Brakhage, Baillie, Frampton, Snow, Rainer, and others.

subject: FAMST
title: Introduction to Environmental Media
description: Ties the acquisition of critical viewing skills for film to the practice of conceiving and writing short environmental documentaries. Students screen narrative films and documentaries, deconstruct them, and use their new proficiency to write their own documentary treatments.

subject: FAMST
title: Film Music
description: Examines the musical score as an integral structural element of cinema. topics include the model of "silent" cinema; the theoretical basis of soundand image synchronicity; the narrative functions of film music; and contemporary development of the film score.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film, television, digital media, and the consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Critical Approaches to Animation
description: This seminar examines animated films as sites for critical intervention. Research methods integrate historical, theoretical and formal analysis, and discussions explore the ways in which the practices and aesthetics of animation actively engage their social, cultural and political contexts.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Artificial Intelligence and Media Industries
description: In this seminar, students will read and discuss current research articles and writings related to AI and the media industries. The course will consider AI tools and systems in relation to media production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics addressed include: ownership and capacities of AI tools and systems; changing work roles and labor relations; authorship, creativity, and copyright issues; AI-related modes of storytelling and aesthetics; impacts of AI on streaming and distribution; and infrastructural requirements of AI in the media industries.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Humane Cinema: Media and Animal Studies
description: From Eadweard Muybridge’s equine motion photography experiments to lions and tigers and bears (oh my), to an internet made of cats, animals and media have always been inextricably linked. This course takes a multifaceted, interdisciplinary approach to the study of onscreen beasts. How have animals been used as characters, as actors, as metaphors? What are the ethics of putting real animals onscreen? What do stories about animals tell us about ourselves? We will consider fictional and nonfictional modes of storytelling, historical and contemporary works, real and computer-generated creatures in our global cinematic safari. Screenings may include Nope, Jaws, Princess Mononoke, Grizzly Man, and EO.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Buster Keaton
description: Buster Keaton's silent comedies in depth. Topics include: the history of comic performance styles, narrative and non-narrative comic film forms, the imagery and themes of modernity in American art and culture, and pragmatism as an aesthetic and philosophical stance.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Theories of Comedy
description: This seminar explores historical developments in screen comedy through the lens of various explanations for the human phenomena of comedy and laughter, with attention to questions of social and political context and changing processes of technological mediation.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Cinema and Revolution: Media Forensics, Surveillance, and Contemporary Global Protests
description: Examines the cinema of contemporary protest, tracking successive waves of revolt from the 2011 Arab Spring to recent uprisings in Eastern Europe, East Asia, and the Middle East. We trace a spectrum of moving-image practice, from anonymous citizen footage and mobile livestreams to festival documentaries and dramatic features, treating protest footage as at once evidence and artifact. Throughout, the course asks who gets to document an uprising, whose visibility is claimed and whose is withheld, and how facial recognition, surveillance, and digital forensics now reshape events and their representation. Students complete an original research project analyzing the visual record of a single movement.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Essay Film
description: In this hybrid theory/practice seminar, we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw from and subvert a range of established practices, including nonfiction, narrative, and avant-garde cinema. What is the history of essayistic filmmaking? What does the essayistic mode offer filmmakers and scholars today? Through readings, screenings, student-led presentations, and exercises, students will gain both a conceptual foundation and hands-on experience with the essay film. The course culminates in a final independent project.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Fan Culture
description: This course allows students to closely examine and analyze the communities that arise around the shared enjoyment of an aspect of popular culture.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: The Future of Media
description: This seminar takes a critical-industrial approach to analyzing 21st century digital media culture. We survey ongoing developments related to social media, streaming media, advertising, business models, and content development, among other topics, throughout the quarter. We also look at the various stakeholders ranging from Hollywood studios, Big Tech corporations, music and gaming companies, and YOU - the user - in order to understand the forces controlling, directing, creating, obstructing, and/or unleashing whatever is on the horizon for medias future.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis Global Cinema Going
description: Explores prevailing themes in contemporary and historical film exhibition in a variety of global contexts. Readings include scholarly work and popular sources to assist students in reflecting on the research process and preparing a high-quality paper.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Global Genres
description: Discusses the transnational iterations of diverse genrescomedy, melodrama, science fiction, action cinema, and horror to situate genres as expressive forms that respond to popular anxieties around change, movement, and dislocation engendered by the geopolitical flux.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Gender, Romance, and Cinema
description: Explores how films about romantic love shape, reinforce, or challenge cultural norms of gender and sexuality. Focusing on romantic comedies, melodramas, and global reworkings of these genres, the course traces how constructions and critiques of romance appear in cinema from classical Hollywood to the present. Readings from feminist film theory, queer theory, and sociology guide discussions on spectatorship, heteronormativity, gender performativity, race and masculinity, and more.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Latin American Cinema
description: Study of the central issues in contemporary Latin American cinema from 1990 to the present with an emphasis on aesthetics, social and political cultures, and global networks.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Marxist Film
description: Is Marx still useful in addressing social inequalities still prevalent in our times? This course aims to answer this question by examining a series of political films that attempt to challenge the logic of modern capitalism from a Marxist perspective.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Media and Violence
description: This seminar examines several of the issues related to representations of and discourses about violence in film and media. We begin with a consideration of the precursors to and emergence and consolidation of the so-called "ultraviolent" aesthetic (in the mid-to-late 1960s), then we consider a few of the film genres whose most prominent conventions include representations of violence (such as the gangster, horror, war, and boxing genres). In addition, the seminar includes a comparative approach to the issue of violent representations in film and media (especially television) by surveying the terms and themes that characterize both social scientific and humanities discourses.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Oil Culture
description: This seminar examines how our dependency on oil shapes modern ways of seeing and being. The course traces the media worlds of oil, from the origins of documentary film to contemporary contemplations of a world after oil.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Occult and Psychedelic Horror
description: Focuses on the occult and/or psychedelic dimensions of horror films and popular culture. Critical, historical, and theoretical approaches to fear, disgust, the monster, the supernatural, delirium, esotericism, limit experiences, “good” and “bad trips.”
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Pakistani Cinema: Exploring the Nation through Cinema from 1947-Present
description: What do you think when you think of “Pakistan?” What feelings does it engender? What visions does it (re)create? What about “Pakistan” and “cinema?” This course examines the idea of a national culture and the cinema of Pakistan in terms of major periods, themes, formal parameters, and institutions in relation to both national and international cultural histories. In choosing Pakistan and its cinema history which correlates with a complex political history of constantly changing regimes as our locale, we will both problematize and work through the concept of a national cinema culture through a burgeoning subfield of film studies, Pakistani cinema.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Russian War Films, 1911Present
description: Examines the genre of war films in Russian and Soviet cinema from the pre-revolutionary era to the present. Together, we explore films on Russian military conflicts from World War I to the ongoing war in Ukraine. Following the evolution of a wide range of cinematic styles through the historic peripeteia of Russian imperialist, Soviet, and post-Soviet societies, we explore how movies have shaped the countrys popular historical narratives. In addition to viewing and discussing a feature-length film each week, we discuss short readings on the history of Russian cinema. Students also write weekly posts on the viewing assignments, which will go towards the creation of a collective zine.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Screendance
description: This course asks students to consider dance-like rhythmic movement to be integral to its representation as screen media. In addition to written assignments, students are asked to produce a short video production drawing on the reading and weekly screenings.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis:Adaptation Studies: Screening Shakespeare
description: This seminar investigates how to study screen adaptations, focusing on Shakespeare, arguably the most adapted author. Film and TV-focused topics covered include intertextuality, critical race theory (#ShakeRace), and queer theory. Screenings may include: Haider, Romeo + Juliet, Game of Thrones.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Critical Encounters with "True Crime"
description: Investigates the history and theory of "true crime" as an evolving intermedial genre from early modern broadsides to 19th-century penny dreadfuls to contemporary podcasts, docuseries, and amateur digital investigations. Students will analyze "true crime" case studies through different lenses, such as economics and industry, aesthetics and pleasure, and ethics and representation.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
prereq_gold: a class level of JR or a class level of SR or a class level of LM or a class level of SB or a class level of SP or a class level of SS or FAMST 46

subject: FAMST
title: The Selfie from Caravaggio to the Present
description: The digital “selfie" is ubiquitous. But what constitutes the lure of reproducing one’s image through technical media in the first place? This course examines histories and theories of self-imaging media, tracing how widespread concepts of selfhood have shifted over time alongside––and in relation to––the development of specific media technologies: from paintings to daguerreotypes, snapshots, cinema, video, and digital media. By analyzing broad tends and “case studies” of specific artists, filmmakers, and theorists; we will ultimately consider the historical context, and develop the conceptual skills, needed to survey and scrutinize ethical problems and potentials posed by selfies in the present.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Youth Culture
description: This seminar examines the origins and development of the American media's many preoccupations with youth, including as on-screen protagonists and a key demographic off-screen. Issues explored include: the terms and meanings of "youth media" and "youth culture"; themes associated with youth; and the ways producers have sought to attract youth.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Basic Screenwriting
description: A study of the creativity and the technique of screenwriting for the conventional narrative film and for TV. Students will be required to complete writing exercises, a treatment, and master scenes of a full-lengthproject.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.

subject: FAMST
title: Advanced Screenwriting
description: A course intended for students who have successfully completed Film Studies188A and have a full-length screenplay in process which they want to complete.

subject: FAMST
title: Musical Theatre
description: An introduction to the unique techniques and challenges of writing for musical theatre, focusing on the collaborative art of telling a story through music, lyrics, script (the “book”) and dance. A historical overview of musical theater from early operetta to contemporary Broadway and West End hits, will inform our exploration of both the “show” and the “business.” Students will learn foundational vocabulary, analyze how songs advance character and plot, and develop scenes and songs in weekly, hands-on exercises, culminating in a workshop presentation of original works-in-progress.

subject: FAMST
title: Short Form Comedy
description: A fast-paced, writing-intensive dive into the world of sketch-writing, digital shorts, monologues, and stand-up comedy. We explore the foundational principals of scene-structure, joke-structure, and comedic voice through analysis of classic and contemporary examples, with an emphasis on developing your own unique point-of-view. Through in-class collaboration and a supportive “room-writing” environment, writers practice pitching, punching-up, producing, and performing individual, team, and group-generated material on a professional deadline, culminating in a performance/portfolio of written work, as well as tools to take a funny idea from concept to completion.

subject: FAMST
title: Storytelling for the Screen
description: Part one of a two-part program. Aimed at students who already have basic screenwriting strengths, and are in the intermediate-to-advanced skill range. While focus will depend on the writer-in-residence, the course will include sessions in plot and structure, character and dialogue, tension and conflict, tone and symbolism, and revision strategies.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.

subject: FAMST
title: Writing for Television
description: Introduction to fundamentals of writing for television including: the situation comedy, the hour-long drama, the MOW, the miniseries, and children's programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for navigating successful television scripts.
advisor_comments: Students are required to submit a writing sample.

subject: FAMST
title: The Writers Room
description: A writing-intensive practicum in creative collaboration. Working together, students will develop skills of improvisation, team-ideation, and room-writing to harness the power of diverse perspectives as we conceptualize, develop, and generate scripted material.

subject: FAMST
title: Workshop for the Screen
description: Part two of a two-part program. Team workshop structure will allow students to expand their screenwriting skills through a fundamental and intensive story-writing experience, an immersive and craft-focused writing calendar, with access to seasoned writers. Emphasis on multiple rounds of table-readings and group critiques.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory
description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to globalization, feminist aesthetics, critical race theories, technologies, algorithms, and the writings of key authors.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Algorithms and Culture
description: In this seminar, students take a critical design approach to analyze various algorithms (i.e., Search, PageRank), their relationship with their structured data (i.e., tweets), and their impact on contemporary infrastructures and social flows.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Alternative Media Futures
description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to structuralism, semiotics, metaphor/metonymy, point of view, and the writings of Burch, Barthes, Metz, Heath, Bordwell, Willemen, Wollen.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Cozy Games
description: Provides an opportunity to probe deeply into the genre of “cozy” games, which came to prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic with games like Animal Crossing: New Horizons (2020). We consider not only how gentle, wholesome, and domestic games predated the “cozy” label, but also how the moniker “cozy” predates cozy games (for instance, in cozy mysteries). In addition to questioning the typical gender coding of these games and their players, we will read and play extensively in order to think about the genre’s contested boundaries and why its classic themes of comfort, domesticity, and interpersonal relations often dovetail with (implied) violence, nature and the outdoors, and even death.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: FemTech Lab
description: FemTech Lab is a theory/practice seminar on feminism, cyberfeminism, and feminist theories of technology. We engage the political potency of feminist media practicethe use of installations, performance, public engagements, and web-based platforms appealing for change or hacking systemic bias.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Invisible Labors: The Past, Present, and Future of Media Technology and Work
description: Explores how media and communications technologies, ranging from the telegraph and early computers to social media platforms and artificial intelligence, have shaped the politics of work and workplace control. Introduces students to theories of race, gender, and work, as well as literature from science and technology studies, the history of technology, and labor studies.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Japanese American Internment Media
description: Explores the role of visual and print media in the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans through various historical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include the production and remediation of domestic wartime propaganda, race and representation, and public and private memory.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Media and Globalization
description: This theory course explores medias constitutive role in our experiences of globalization. Topics include: accumulation of capital and forms of dispossession; borders and migration; flows and frictions; geographies of displacement; global media conglomerates and piracy; risk and securitization; resource extraction, the commons, and grassroots mobilization.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Media In/Through Iran
description: Explores how Iran's cultural, technological, and political landscape offers generative ways of studying media: their alternative histories, adaptive practices, and subversive circulations. Engaging with an eclectic range of Iranian objects and practices from the nineteenth century to the present, students examine the role of media in forming identity and negotiating power while considering the material conditions that transform communications technologies.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory – Film & Media and Policing
description: This seminar investigates the relationship between police power and film and media from the late nineteenth century to the present. Students will analyze a range of media including, photography, silent cinema, American and international studio and independent features, avant-garde film, dash cam, body cam, and cell phone footage, and digital technologies that employ crime statistics and predictive policing. In addition to film and media theory, students will study theories of criminality, punishment, and abolition.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Sports, Media and Modernity
description: Explores the relationship between sport, media, and modernity through two critical lenses: first, how sport acts as a cultural apparatus mediating institutions, collective identities, and power structures of modern societies; second, how evolving media technologies (from print cultures to data-driven platforms) transform how sport is staged, performed, and experienced today. Thinking through the topics of colonialism, nationalism, race, gender, technology, and spectatorship, students examine how sport both expresses and structures the cultural dynamics of modern life.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Occult Media
description: In this seminar, we will contend with definitions of media and how they interface with the occult. Throughout the quarter, students will conduct archival research, learn about media archaeology, and discover occult media in its many forms, including horror films, online folklore, divination tools, Ouija boards, tabloid reports of the Satanic Panic, magic lantern shows, spiritualist and countercultural periodicals, optical toys, podcast episodes, popular music, religious technology like Scientology’s E-Meter, and more. Each student will be guided through a personalized archival research project that includes a trip to special collections at UCSB Library.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Plant Humanities
description: In a world dominated by humans and other animals, plants have become an unlikely but productive focus of academic attention. Scientists and humanists are unearthing neglected aspects of plant life and being in everything from digital design and fire suppression to philosophy, history, literature, food, culture, and archives. Our class explores what thinking through and with plants offers to film and media studies, but will also draw on botany, feminist science and technology studies, and work on indigeneity, colonialism, and extraction.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Race and/in AI
description: Critical work on artificial intelligence has, by now, revealed it as an intense tool of surveillance, policing, and racialization. This work has demonstrated the vastly unequal distributions of the political effects of race; however, this work has also demonstrated alternative practices, both current and speculative, with, alongside, and/or against AI. This course traces these diverse accounts of race and/in AI with the goal of answering the following three questions: What, when, and where is race in AI?
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Sound, Media, and Society
description: Builds conceptual and analytical tools for a critical understanding of sound, media, and auditory cultures. Special attention is paid to how social and historical factors inform sound media and how sound media, in turn, inform cultural perceptions and practices.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Software and Society
description: If “data is the new oil”—a phrase often championed by venture capitalists, Big Tech advocates, and engineers—then software might be likened to refineries that transform raw data into commodities, video games, and social media platforms. But what exactly is software, and how does it interact with social, political, and cultural forces? This course explores these questions by tracing software's history from the mid-20th century to today’s Artificial Intelligence systems. We will examine primary and secondary sources to understand software’s role in everything from surveillance and warfare to art and finance. Our central goal will be to develop our understanding of how, as one popular commentary puts it, “software is eating the world.”
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Television Studies - Technologies, Theories, and Methods
description: This advanced seminar functions as an intro to TV Studies thru an analysis of the key developments, formats, genres, &infrastructures of the televisual medium. As a medium w/ continually shifting meanings&in relation to an ever-changing landscape of technologies, examining TV in a global context offers a chance to think thru the cultural, political, aesthetic, &technological structures which function on the level of region&intersect w/ transnational &global media trends. Drawing from infrastructural studies, globalization studies, cultural studies,&media industry approaches, this class will provide a critical examination of the history &structures of TV, as well as the discipline of TV Studies thru an interdisciplinary&intersectional lens
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: The Wire: TV in Focus
description: Examines HBOs crime drama television series, The Wire (2002-2008). Discusses the series through critical, historical, and theoretical approaches from fields like urban studies and television studies. Students work on projects related to city media of their choice.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts: Anti-War Media
description: In this seminar, we focus on global and local oppositional media and crafts practices that seek to prevent, stop, and undermine the death-making of war, offering ways to sustain life for civilians, heal the survivors, and commemorate the dead: From memoirs and photographs to zines and social media, from carpets and cooking recipes to apps and video games. By Interrogating warfare through anti-war media, we closely engage with the ethics of witnessing, limits of representation, and militarization of everyday life. Simultaneously, by studying media through anti-war frameworks we consider less-discussed aspects, kinds, and practices of media such as failure and repair, handmade and low-tech, and tactical and communal.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Feminist Media Studies
description: Provides an introduction to the theoretical and practice-based frameworks and approaches within feminist media studies. The seminar begins with an examination of archival erasure in the early days of cinema, moves through avant-garde cinematographic experiments, then looks at documentary approaches and questions around representing history, labor and care, and finally culminate in contemporary digital media practice and cyberfeminist critique. Explores work by key theorists and practitioners and dedicates particular attention to the practice of “looking sideways” – examining the folds and interstices between feminist, queer, and decolonial approaches to cinema and media theory and praxis.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.

subject: FAMST
title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Women, Work, and Gambling
description: This rigorous, interdisciplinary seminar examines contemporary gaming, gambling, and digital media platforms. In this course we ask: How are entertainment and work shaped by capitalism and mediated by digital platforms? Who works and plays on digital platforms? How does digital media change, distort, warp, or adapt our work lives and leisure time? Drawing from texts in feminist studies, history, sociology, critical theory, gaming and gambling studies, political economy, and film theory, students will develop a high-quality, well-argued, original final paper throughout the quarter. Students will closely engage with course texts and fellow classmates’ written work in writing workshops.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units provided the letter designations are different, but only 8 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Cultural Thory
description: This course introduces students to theoretical approaches and frameworks that are crucial to understanding our social and cultural contemporaneity. Topics include ideology and social determination; knowledge and power; history, memory, and trauma; postcolonial/decolonial critique; neoliberal globalization; biopolitics; risk and precarity.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Digital Theory
description: Histories and theories of digital media and their users, from early computers and networks to video games and selfies. Approaches include comparative media analysis, cultural studies, science and technology studies, software/platform studies, and environmental media critique.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Theories of Filmgoing and Mass Culture
description: In our age of online streaming platforms, diminishing theatrical ticket sales, and individual media devices, one may reasonably ask: what is the value of filmgoing in a space shared with others? This course will help us consider this pressing question by engaging past and present theories of cinema’s effect on landscapes of mass culture. Beginning with film photography at the cusp of modernity, before tracing positive and negative appraisals of cinema’s ideological power, we will ultimately consider arguments for why public filmgoing should matter: insofar as collective viewership may challenge insufficient assumptions, open up newfound ethical possibilities, and incite astonishing alternatives to the status quo.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Genre Theory
description: Examines the study of film genres through a theoretical lens. Topics include semiotic, structuralist, psychoanalytic, and phenomenological theories of the musical, the horror film, melodrama, and the concept of genre itself.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Popular Music and Youth Culture
description: Explores the social history and cultural politics of popular music and youth culture, with an emphasis on the relations between musical meaning, technological mediation, cultural value, and social power.
repeat_comments: FAMST 192FT is not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192A. FAMST 192CM and FAMST 192CT are not open for credit to students who have completed FLMST 192B
prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.

subject: FAMST
title: The Carsey-Wolf Center Practicum: Contemporary Programming, Distribution, and Exhibition.
description: This course will use the Pollock Theater and its programming as a laboratory for studying contemporary programming and exhibition practices. Topics under consideration will include media distribution and exhibition contexts, constructing programming series and conducting interviews with guests, and the way contemporary tastes are shaped through algorithms and curation practices. Students will have opportunities to gain hands-on experience with camera equipment. Regular attendance at Carsey-Wolf Center events in the Pollock Theater will be required.
prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Focus Media Journal
description: For members of the editorial board of the Focus Media Journal at UCSB. UCSB Focus Media Journal is an annual scholarly journal issued every spring quarter. As a literary publication for the Film and Media Studies Department, the journal’s goal is to engage students from all disciplines, with a focus on media forms.
advisor_comments: Not for credit in the global major.

subject: FAMST
title: Internship in Film/Television
description: An opportunity for training, career sampling, and contacts in the film or television industry. Required are approximately 100 hours of work a quarter, a final five-page report, and a supervisor's letter of verification.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters.

subject: FAMST
title: Independent Studies
description: Selected research under the direction of a faculty member.
advisor_comments: Students must have a 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in film studies; consent of instructor and department.

subject: FAMST
title: Independent Research Assistance in Film Studies
description: Course work shall consist of faculty supervised research assistance.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in film studies; consent of instructor and department.

subject: FAMST
title: Critical Analysis and Method
description: Seminar examining a range of methodologies and critical approaches to the study of film and media, with the specific topics chosen by the instructor.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film Analysis
description: Close examination of an element of film style - such as sound, color, or camera movement - and its impact on interpretation.

subject: FAMST
title: National Cinemas
description: Close analysis of theories of nation, nationalism, and national cinema, with a focus on the contentious relations between culture, history, media capital and the state. Topics include evolving genres, styles, movements and institutions; local lifeworlds and cultural difference within a post-national context; and the spectral nature of contemporary national formations.Offered concurrently with Film Studies 187AA-ZZ.

subject: FAMST
title: Philosophy of Film History
description: Studies works and concepts in the philosophy of history that have informed the researching and writing of film and media history. Will also consider the ways in which film and media texts have extended debates and concepts of historiographic practice.

subject: FAMST
title: Media Historiographies
description: Comparative analysis of various historical accounts of cinema, television, and digital media that have shaped the field of film and media studies. Emphasis on issues and debates that have dominated efforts to write rigorous, methodologically explicit histories of different media.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media History
description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media history.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media History: Global Film Exhibition
description: Examines the industrial, social, cultural, and racial practices employed in theatrical and non-theatrical exhibition venues around the world and the local, national, and transnational film cultures developed around moviegoing and other consumption activities related to cinema.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media History: Revisiting Weimar Culture
description: This course explores the art, politics and culture of the Weimar Republic, the period between the defeat of Germany in World War I and Hitler’s rise to power in 1933. It focuses on film and visual culture, with attention to questions of gender, sexuality, and class. It examines questions of history and historiography as well as the work of theorists who proposed new ways of thinking about art, popular culture, and technological innovation that remain resonant today.

subject: FAMST
title: Film Theory
description: Examines the history and rhetoric of thinking about the ontology, epistemology, ideology, and aesthetics of film.

subject: FAMST
title: Television and Digital Media Theory
description: Explores important theoretical writings concerning electronic and digital media. Course readings define the unique properties of these mediums, consider their ontological status, and discuss how they differ from one another and other cultural forms.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory
description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media theory.

subject: FAMST
title: Adaptation Theory
description: This graduate seminar examines key theoretical concepts in adaptation studies. Focusing on literature-to-film adaptation, FAMST 242AT takes a long-historical, diachronic approach to adaptation theory, engaging with classical and early modern thinking about imitatio as well as with contemporary theoretical arguments in the subject.

subject: FAMST
title: Cloud Infrastructure: Pipelines, Platforms, and Data
description: This course examines cloud infrastructure in the form of Internet pipelines, digital platforms, and data. We look at the various histories, forms of governance, and impact of these sociotechnical systems on digital civil liberties and cultural formations of access, truth, privacy, and free speech. Studying this array of infrastructural affordances and their development also allows us to look at values of de/centralization, privatization, scarcity and abundance, competition, networks, and public utility in relation to the concept of being in the cloud. We will embrace a humanistic and historical perspective but we will also rely on interdisciplinary materials and methods throughout the course.

subject: FAMST
title: Computing Power: Computation and Society from Babbage to Bitcoin
description: Examines the historical and contemporary relationship between computing and social power. Students learn about influential historiographical and theoretical developments within social studies of computing, including recent intersections with the study of race, sexuality and gender, and global capitalism.

subject: FAMST
title: Game Studies
description: Provides a general, graduate-level introduction to the academic field of game studies, ideal for students working on interactive digital media objects or platforms and/or cultures of play. We will discuss select foundational texts in order to consider the field’s initially contested relationship to literary and film studies and turn-of-the-century new media theory. We will also examine a plethora of recent work that simultaneously expands and critiques canonical game studies through the lenses of the analog, race, queer theory, feminism, ecology, affect, historical preservation, and labor. Students will be encouraged to read and play, and to consider research, presentation, and pedagogical methods specific to this field.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory
description: Close examination of a topic in film and/or media theory.

subject: FAMST
title: Media and Policing
description: An examination of the relationship between police power and modern image-making technologies from a variety of critical historiographical and theoretical perspectives. We will trace a genealogy of the present by putting eighteenth- and nineteenth-century methodologies and visual culture in conversation with new research methods and media. Topics to be discussed include: the production of criminality, physiognomy and phrenology, carceral geography, crime statistics and predictive policing, carceral aesthetics, counter forensics, and abolition. Course readings will be discussed in relation to screenings and close study of artifacts and technologies that operate at the intersection of policing and media.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and Media Theory: Science and Technology Studies
description: Introduces theories and methods in science and technology studies. Students learn about scholars, texts, and schools of thought that have shaped this interdisciplinary field, as well as more recent intersections with gender/sexuality, race, indigeneity, media, medicine, and the environment.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Critical Thinkers
description: Explores in depth the work of one particular thinker relevant to the field of media and cultural studies, for example, Freud, Barthes, Benjamin, and others.

subject: FAMST
title: Cultural Theory
description: Explores key ideas, issues, and developments in cultural studies and critical theory through close readings of primary texts. Possible approaches include the Frankfurt School, the Birmingham School, Freudianism/Lacanianism, semiotics/structuralism, and postmodernism/post-structuralism.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Cultural Studies
description: Close examination of a topic in cultural studies.

subject: FAMST
title: Sound and Aurality
description: Explores the interdisciplinary field of sound studies from a variety of critical historiographical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include architectural acoustics, eco-sonic media, vibrational ontologies, sound-reproduction technologies, noise and feedback, sonic warfare, aurality and modern rationality.

subject: FAMST
title: Special Topics in Film and/or Media Globalization
description: Close examination of a topic in globalization of film and/or media.

subject: FAMST
title: Global Hollywood
description: Close examination of a topic in globalization of film and/or media.

subject: FAMST
title: Creative-Critical Praxis
description: This graduate seminar explores the use of creative, artistic, and experimental methods in the production of interdisciplinary scholarly research through the examination of a variety of creative-critical modes, including filmmaking, game design, critical cartography, poetic practice, speculative non-fiction, and art curation.

subject: FAMST
title: Media Techniques of Wonder
description: Media Techniques of Wonder is focused on themes of media archaeology and their emergent literary context. The exchange between literature and media techniques serves as the focus, with literary texts creating a basis for real and imagined media technologies that radically reshape literary practices. Historical devices will serve as a basis along with visits to media collections.
advisor_comments: Comparative Literature 280 and Film Studies 280 are the same course.

subject: FAMST
title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
description: Designed to accommodate graduate students who serve as teaching assistants. Includes analyses of texts and materials, discussion section teaching techniques, formulation of topics and questions for papers and examinations, and grading papers and examinations under instructor supervision.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: FAMST
title: Programming and Curation Practicum
description: Examines issues related to curation, including the construction of canons, cultural value, and economies of prestige. Students work with the CWC director in curating programs for the Pollock Theater and related research events. Class discusses readings, screen media, research potential guests, writes questions for Q&A sessions with invited guests, and writes program notes for the CWCs website and Pollock programs. Students register for one unit per quarter. If taken for elective credit toward the Film and Media Studies PhD, it must be taken for two terms in a row, two units in each of the two terms.
advisor_comments: Graduate students from any department are eligible to enroll in 1 or 2 units. For elective credit toward the Film and Media Studies PhD, students must register for 2 units in each of the two terms.
