subject: MATH CS
title: Problem Solving I
description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine mathematical problems related with different problem-solving techniques. Possible topics are: Pigeonhole principle, use of invariants and symmetries in problem solving, coloring arguments, parity, recursive arguments, extreme principle, inclusion-exclusion principle.

subject: MATH CS
title: Problem Solving II
description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine problems in different areas of mathematics like Graph Theory, Number Theory, Combinatorics, Geometry, Game Theory, Topology, Algebra, and Analysis.

subject: MATH CS
title: Advanced Linear Algebra I
description: An introduction to the theory of Linear Algebra with topics: Algebra of matrices, linear systems of equations, vector spaces, linear independence, basis and dimension, infinite-dimensional vectors spaces, linear transformations, matrix representation, isomorphisms, quotient spaces, dual spaces, and determinants.

subject: MATH CS
title: Advanced Linear Algebra II
description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization. Canonical form under similarity: Jordan canonical form and rational canonical form, inner product and norm. Gram-Schmidt process, adjoint of a linear operator, normal and self-adjoint operators, unitary and orthogonal operators, spectral theorem.

subject: MATH CS
title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: A rigorous introduction to the elements of analysis. Covers sequences, accumulation points, Bolzano-Weierstrass, Cauchy's criterion, the completeness property of the real number system, limits of functions, continuity, differentiability, compact sets, and the Heine-Borel theorem.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics
description: Lectures on a coherent body of mathematical topics which are not usually presented in standard mathematics courses.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning: Foundations and Applications
description: This course provides an accessible introduction to the field of data science and related techniques from machine learning. The course will develop both mathematical foundations and theory behind learning algorithms as well as discussing practical aspects for their use in applications.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Math Book Club
description: A collaborative seminar on mathematical topics not ordinarily covered in the standard curriculum. Students work as a cohort under faculty supervision to study a common textbook or collection of research papers. Participants give weekly presentations, lead peer discussions, and solve related problem sets. The course emphasizes independent learning within a shared seminar setting, with focus on mathematical reading, proof analysis, problem solving, and oral communication. Topic varies by term.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Combinatorics
description: Combinatorics has its historical roots in mathematical recreations and games. Combinatorics is concerned with arrangements of the objects in a set into patterns satisfying specified rules.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Theory of Distributions and their Applications
description: Distributions, also known generalized functions, are objects that generalize the classical notion of functions in mathematical analysis. Distributions make it possible to differentiate functions whose derivatives do not exist in the classical sense. Distributions are widely used in the theory of partial differential equations, in physics and engineering where many problems naturally lead to differential equations whose solutions or initial conditions are singular, such as the Dirac delta function.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics: The Ellipse
description: The course delves into concepts using ellipses as a foundational shape: Synthetic & Projective geometry, theorems like Pascal's, Potential theory encompassing Newton’s cloaking, Elliptic functions aiding arc length computation, Quantization of ellipses involving Jacobi matrices, Moving boundaries (e.g., crystal growth) maintaining ellipses, with potential for broader topics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Algebraic Combinatorics
description: This class discusses applications of algebra (especially linear algebra) to various combinatorial problems.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Number Systems
description: An exploration of basic number systems including the integers, rationals, reals, complex and beyond.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Linear Optimization
description: In this course, students study optimization techniques in the area of Linear Programming whose goal is to find the maximum or a minimum of a linear function subject to linear constraints. This area of mathematics has broad applications in engineering, in data analysis, in industry, in medicine, etc. The only prerequisite for this class is Linear Algebra and some Multivariable calculus.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Topology
description: Basic concepts in point set and algebraic topology, including compactness and fundamental groups.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Game Theory
description: Introduction to game theory and related topics. Includes classical game theory and combinatorial game theory up through the Sprague-Grundy Theorem.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Knot Theory
description: This course introduces the mathematical study of knots and links focusing on how topology, algebra, and geometry interact to distinguish and classify them. Students will learn both classical and modern knot invariants. A more apt title for this course could be 'Topics in Geometric Topology,' as we will also touch upon the importance of knots and links in the broader field of low-dimensional topology. Possible topics include the study of codimension one embeddings in manifolds, the knot group, Seifert surfaces and Seifert genus, polynomial link invariants, braids, finite and infinite cyclic coverings, the Alexander module, surgery theory, hyperbolic knot theory, and quantum invariants.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Number Theory
description: Selected topics in number theory.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: P-adic analysis and p-adic zeta functions
description: Introduces p-adic numbers which can be obtained by completing rational numbers with respect to an absolute value different from the usual Euclidean absolute value. Discusses p-adic analysis and a p-adic version of Riemann zeta functions.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Topological Combinatorics
description: Two thieves have stolen a valuable necklace made of gems of several kinds. They want to divide the necklace so that each gets the same number of each kind of gem. How many cuts do they have to make? In this course you'll learn the answer to this and other combinatorial questions and how algebraic topology is used in the proof.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit providing letter designations are different.

subject: MATH CS
title: Probability
description: This is a course on probability. It covers discrete and continuous distributions, combinatorial methods, generating functions, conditioning, the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, stochastic processes, random walks, Brownian motion, and applications in biology, economics, engineering, and physics.

subject: MATH CS
title: Complex Variables I
description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

subject: MATH CS
title: Complex Variables II
description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

subject: MATH CS
title: Introduction to the Higher Mathematics
description: A formal introduction to the language and culture of mathematics. Students will learn how to rigorously think about mathematics and write mathematical proofs. Topics covered include: propositional logic, set theory, cardinality, number theory, and various number systems.

subject: MATH CS
title: Independent Studies
description: Serious independent study in mathematics with consenting faculty member.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit. Creative Studies students may enroll in a maximum of 24 units of Independent Studies courses per year, with a maximum of 45 units counted toward graduation.

subject: MATH CS
title: Group Studies
description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Mathematics.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.
advisor_comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 3 units for Math 2A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 3A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
repeat_comments: Math 2A and 3A are legal repeats. See Math Department to discuss appropriate repeat options.
prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.
prereq_gold: Math placement exam ≥ 2 or Math placement exam ≥ 3 or AP Calc AB ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 2 or AP 65 ≥ 3

subject: MATH
title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.
advisor_comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 3 units for Math 2B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 3B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
repeat_comments: Math 2B and 3B are legal repeats. See Math Department to discuss appropriate repeat options.
prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.
advisor_comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 2 units for Math 3A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.
repeat_comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2A, then Math 3A can be taken as a legal repeat as long as students get a qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam to take Math 3A.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.
advisor_comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 2 units for Math 3B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
repeat_comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2B, then Math 3B can be taken as a legal repeat.
prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: MATH 3A or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra with Applications
description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.
prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: MATH 2B or MATH 3B or MATH 3BI or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M ≥ 5 or IB M4 ≥ 5

subject: MATH
title: Differential Equations
description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.
prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.
prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.
prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Transition to Higher Mathematics
description: Introduction to the elements of propositional logic, techniques of mathematical proof, and fundamental mathematical structures, including sets, functions, relations, and other topics as time permits. Mastery of this material is essential for students planning to major in mathematics.
prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
prereq_gold: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3A or 34LA, or are simultaneously enrolled in 2A or 3A or 34LA, or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
description: Continued study of differential and integral calculus with differential andintegral calculus with applications. Introduction to mathematical modeling with differential equations. Calculus of several variables including an introduction to partial derivatives.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3B or 34LB or are simultaneously enrolled in 2B or 3B or 34LB, or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
prereq_gold: MATH 2A or MATH 3A or MATH 34A or MATH 34LA or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3A or 34A, or are simultaneously enrolled in 2A or 3A or 34A, or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems of more than one equation.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3B or 34B or are simultaneously enrolled in 2B or 3B or 34B, or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam.
prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: Group Studies in Mathematics
description: Lectures and discussions on special topics. Designed for transfer students only.
advisor_comments: Requires concurrent enrollment in MATH 191
prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
prereq_gold: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B; MATH 190 [may be concurrent]

subject: MATH
title: Classical Number Systems
description: A development of classical number systems starting with natural numbers and progressing through the integral, rational, real and complex number systems. Includes an introduction to number theory, mathematical induction, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic and the Euclidean algorithm. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Systems
description: The theory of operations within rings and fields. Polynomials, the fundamental theorem of algebra and other factorization theorems. Analyzing linear, polynomial, rational and exponential functions. Solving algebraic equations and inequalities. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prereq_text: Math 101A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prereq_text: Math 102A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction Into Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical methods for the solution of nonlinear equations (Newton method), for integration (quadrature formulas and composite integration), and for the initial value problem for ordinary differential equations (Euler and Kutta methods).
prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B; and, Math 8 or PSTAT 8, and Math 117 and, Computer Science 5AA-ZZ or 10 or 8 or 16 or Engineering 3, each with a grade of C or above.
prereq_gold: (MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 6B) or (MATH 4BI and MATH 6A and MATH 6B); (MATH 8 and MATH 117) or (PSTAT 8 and MATH 117); CMPSC 5* or CMPSC 10 or CMPSC 8 or CMPSC 16 or ENGR 3

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical methods for the solution of systems of linear equations (direct and iteractive methods), and the finite difference methods for boundary value problems for (ordinary and partial) differential equations.
prereq_text: Math 104A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Advanced Topics in Numerical Analysis
description: Topics in approximation theory; numerical methods for finding eigenvalues of a matrix; and advanced topics in numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations.
prereq_text: Math 104B with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Abstract vector spaces and subspaces. Span and linear independence. Basis and dimension. Linear maps. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
prereq_text: Math 4A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Diagonalization, inner product spaces, projections, least-squares approximations, invariant factors and elementary divisors, canonical forms, topics from advanced matrix theory, applied linear algebra, and group representation theory.
prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Matrix Analysis
description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and similarity; Unitary equivalence and normal matrices; QR factorization; Least squares; Singular Value decomposition; Moore-Penrose generalized inverse; Hermitian and symmetric matrices; Variational characterization of eigenvalues; Positive definite matrices; Nonnegative matrices; Perron-Frobenius Theorem.
prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C

subject: MATH
title: Abstract Algebra
description: An introduction to group theory, focusing on finite groups. Basic algebraic concepts including homomorphisms, normal subgroups, quotients, direct products and group actions. Classification of finitely generated Abelian groups. Other topics such as semidirect products and Sylow theorems as time permits.
prereq_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Abstract Algebra
description: Ring theory, ideals, factorization. Examples include number rings and polynomial rings. Module theory if time permits.
prereq_text: Math 111A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Abstract Algebra
description: Fields, field extensions, Galois theory.
prereq_text: Math 111B with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Non-euclidean Geometry
description: An introduction to hyperbolic geometry with some discussion of other non-euclidean systems.
prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Number-theoretic functions, divisibility, congruences, primitive roots and indices, quadratic residues and the quadratic reciprocity law.
prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Selected topics at the discretion of the instructor. Possibilities include (but are not limited to) Diophantine equations, the distribution of primes, number-theoretic methods in cryptography, quadratic forms, continued fractions, algebraic number theory, and partitions.
prereq_text: Math 115A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Combinatorial Analysis
description: Elementary counting principles, binomial coefficients, generating functions, recurrence relations, the principle of inclusion and exclusion, distributions and partitions, systems of distinct representatives, applications to computation.
prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

subject: MATH
title: Methods of Analysis
description: Introduction to methods of proof in analysis. topics include limits, sequences and series, continuity, compactness, as well as other topics. This course is intended to follow Mathematics 8 and to introduce students to the level of sophistication of upper-division mathematics.
prereq_text: Mathematics 8 or PSTAT 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

subject: MATH
title: Real Analysis
description: Axioms of the real numbers, topology of metric spaces, numerical sequences, infinite series.
prereq_text: Math 4B, 6A, 108A and 117, each with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 108A and MATH 117

subject: MATH
title: Real Analysis
description: Real functions: continuity, differentiability, Riemann integrals, power and trigonometric series.
prereq_text: Math 108B and 118A, each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Real Analysis
description: Multivariable calculus and a selection of other topics including differential forms or Lebesgue integral.
prereq_text: Math 118B with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Existence, uniqueness, and stability; the geometry of phase space; linear systems and hyperbolicity; maps and diffeomorphisms.
prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI and 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: (MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 8) or (MATH 4BI and MATH 6A and MATH 8)

subject: MATH
title: Chaotic Dynamics and Bifurcation Theory
description: Hyperbolic structure and chaos; center manifolds; bifurcation theory; and the Feigenbaum and Ruelle-Takens cascades to strange attractors.
prereq_text: Mathematics 6B and Math 119A, each with a minimum grade of C

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Complex Variables
description: Complex numbers, complex differentiation, analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, Taylor and Laurent series, classification of singular points, residues, evaluation of improper integrals.
prereq_text: Math 6A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Complex Variables
description: The argument principle, Rouche’s theorem, analytic continuation, conformal mapping, fractional transformations and applications, infinite products, harmonic functions. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor.
prereq_text: Math 122A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations
description: Introduces the derivation and solution of the fundamental linear partial differential equations (PDEs): the wave equation, the heat equation and the Laplace equation. These represent, respectively, hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDEs. Focuses on first and second order PDEs. Students will master methods for initial value problems (IVPs) and boundary value problems (BVPs), including the method of characteristics and the foundational techniques of the Fourier transform and potential theory, providing a rigorous basis for understanding dynamic and steady-state physical systems.
prereq_text: Math 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: MATH 4B or MATH 4BI; MATH 6A and MATH 6B and MATH 8

subject: MATH
title: Fourier Series and Numerical Methods for PDEs
description: Introduces specific solution techniques used to solve the wave, heat and Laplace equations. Focuses on separation of variables, namely Fourier series, and a variety of numerical methods. Provides students with modern methods, harmonic analysis and numerical analysis, necessary to study and solve PDEs in a variety of applications. The fast Fourier transform is studied as well as finite difference methods for parabolic and elliptic PDEs and the finite element method for elliptic boundary value problems.
prereq_text: Math 4B or 4BI, and 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and 124A with a minimum grade of C.
prereq_gold: MATH 4B or MATH 4BI; MATH 6A and MATH 6B and MATH 124A

subject: MATH
title: Optimization
description: Global and local optimization, constrained and unconstrained optimization, convex versus nonconvex optimization, Projection Theorem, linear search methods, gradient methods, Newton and Quasi-Newton methods, trust region methods.
prereq_text: Math 6A and 108A, each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Operations Research
description: Large scale optimization, stochastic gradient descent, inexact Newton methods, limited memory BSGF, least squares problems, global optimization, optimization in general normed spaces.
prereq_text: Math 132A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Graph and Network Theory
description: Elements of graph and network theory including paths, circuits, trees, coloring, planarity, matching theory, Hall's theorem, applications to scheduling theory, flows in networks, Menger's theorem, and other topics as time permits.
prereq_text: Math 4A and 8, each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Spectral Graph Theory
description: The graph Laplacian, eigenvalues of weighted graphs and random walks, the normalized Laplacian and Cheegers inequality, diameters and eigenvalues, expander graphs, eigenvalues of symmetric graphs, heat kernels.
prereq_text: Math 108A and 137A, each with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Topology
description: Metric spaces, continuity, compactness, classification of surfaces, Euler characteristics, and fundamental groups. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a C or better. Either Math 108A or Math 117 with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
description: Curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space, including Frenet formulas, signed curvature of plane curves, first and second fundamental forms, normal curvature and principal curvature, Gaussian and mean curvature, Gauss equation and Theorema Egregium, and a brief introduction to geodesics if time permits.
prereq_text: Math 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 108A or 117 with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
description: Parallel transport, geodesics, Gauss-Bonnet Theorem, fundamental theorem of surfaces. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor may include minimal surfaces, Codazzi equation, surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature, isothermal coordinates, and global theorems for curves.
prereq_text: Math 6B and Math 147A with a minimum grade of C.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Mathematical Finance
description: Describes mathematical methods for estimating and evaluating asset pricing models, equilibrium and derivative pricing, options, bonds, and the term-structure of interest rates. Also introduces finance optimization models for risk management and financial engineering.
advisor_comments: PSTAT 170 and Mathematics 170 are the same course.
prereq_text: PSTAT 120A-B and 160A, all completed with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: History of Mathematics
description: An examination of the major achievements in mathematical thinking throughout history. Topics may include the history of numerical systems in early civilizations, the development of formal proof, mathematical contributions from diverse populations and the impact of technological innovations on mathematics. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prereq_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

subject: MATH
title: Special Topics in Mathematics
description: An advanced treatment of mathematics content appropriate for undergraduates. The material for the course may come from algebra, geometry, analysis, applied mathematics or other areas of mathematics. Topics vary by instructor.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Reasonings of AI such as GPT and DeepSeek
description: This project-based course explores the mathematical reasonings of AI systems like GPT and DeepSeek. Students will work on exercises drawn from topics in Math 8, linear algebra, and calculus. For each project, the student will obtain an AI-generated solution, carefully examine it for errors, and then analyze and correct the AI's mistakes. Students will submit all project materials. Most projects will be provided by the instructor, but students will also be encouraged to find some on their own, with all projects receiving necessary instruction.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: A First Course in Algebraic K-Theory
description: An introduction to classical algebraic K-theory, focusing on the lower algebraic K-groups K0, K1, and K2 of commutative rings and their basic properties. These groups are fundamental invariants in algebra and geometry and also have connections to number theory and topology. The course explores some of these connections and known computations, and also focuses on relations with Galois cohomology, class field theory, Brauer group, and related arithmetic invariants. Prerequisites include basic knowledge of groups, rings, modules, and fields.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: MATH
title: Problem Solving
description: The Problem Solving in Mathematics course is designed to impart students with advanced problem-solving techniques and strategies in mathematics. Students will explore a diverse range of methods, including the application of parity, coloring, ordering, extremality, symmetry, invariants among others. The course emphasizes critical and creative thinking, allowing students to tackle complex mathematical challenges. Through collaboration and presentation exercises, students develop effective communication skills. The goal is to equip students with the basic abilities for research in mathematics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematics Transition for Transfer Students
description: Provides transfer students with a solid mathematical foundation to ease their transition into a four-year college environment. Students will explore the fundamental axioms of integers and their properties, gaining a deep understanding of this essential mathematical concept. The curriculum extends to the study of rational numbers, real numbers, and complex numbers, emphasizing the properties and principles that underlie these numeric systems. Through a structured approach, this course equips transfer students with the mathematical knowledge and skills necessary to excel in more advanced coursework.
prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better. Concurrent enrollment in Math 94.
prereq_gold: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B; MATH 94 [may be concurrent]

subject: MATH
title: Internship in Mathematics
description: Faculty sponsored academic internship in industrial or research firms.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to a maximum of four units. Credit will not be given toward upper-division Mathematics major requirements.

subject: MATH
title: Senior Thesis
description: Independent research under the supervision of a faculty member which will result in a senior thesis. Student will concentrate on reading and gathering material for a thesis.
advisor_comments: Up to four units may apply to the major. Up to eight units total in all Mathematics 197/199RA courses may apply toward the major. Students must have a minimum overall grade-point average of 3.0 and a 3.5 or better grade-point-average in the major.
prereq_text: Open to senior majors only; consent of department and instructor.

subject: MATH
title: Senior Thesis
description: Independent research under the supervision of a faculty member which will result in a senior thesis. Student will concentrate on writing a thesis.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum overall grade-point average of 3.0 and a 3.5 or better grade-point average in the major. Up to four units may apply towards the major.
prereq_text: Mathematics 197A. Open to senior majors only; consent of department and instructor.

subject: MATH
title: Independent Studies in Mathematics
description: Coursework consists of academic research supervised by a faculty member on a topic not available in established course offerings.
advisor_comments: Limit of 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all independent studies courses (98/99/99RA/198/199/199AA-ZZ) combined. Only 8 units in Math 197/199AA-ZZ courses may apply to the major.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in math; consent of instructor and department.

subject: MATH
title: Independent Research Assistance
description: Coursework consists of faculty supervised research assistance.
advisor_comments: Up to four units may apply to the major.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in math; consent of instructor and department.

subject: MATH
title: Real Analysis
description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

subject: MATH

description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

subject: MATH
title: Real Analysis
description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

subject: MATH
title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.
advisor_comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211A, ME 210A, ECE 210A, Geology 251A, and Chemical Engineering 211A.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Simulation
description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.
advisor_comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211B, ME 210B, ECE 210B, Geology 251B, and Chemical Engineering 211B.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.
advisor_comments: Students should be proficient in basic numerical methods, linear algebra, mathematically rigorous proofs, and some programming language. Same course as Computer Science 211C, ME 210C, ECE 210C, Geology 251C, and Chemical Engineering 211C.

subject: MATRL
title: Materials in Society, The Stuff of Dreams
description: A survey of new technological substances and materials, the scientific methods used in their development, and their relation to society and the economy. Emphasis on uses of new materials in the human body, electronics, optics, sports, transportation, and infrastructure.
prereq_text: Not open to engineering, pre-computer science, or computer science majors.

subject: MATRL
title: Structure and Properties I
description: An introduction to materials in modern technology. The internal structure of materials and its underlying principles: bonding, spatial organization of atoms and molecules, structural defects. Electricial, magnetic and optical properties of materials, and their relationship with structure.
advisor_comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS-Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs.
prereq_gold: CHEM 1A and CHEM 1B; MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 6B

subject: MATRL
title: Structures and Properties II
description: Mechanical properties of engineering materials and their relationship to bonding and structure. Elastic, flow, and fracture behavior; time dependent deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms. Thermo-mechanical interactions in materials.
advisor_comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS- Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs. Not open for major credit to students who have completed Matrl 101; If students take Matrl 101 and Matrl 100B, they will only receive major credit for one course.

subject: MATRL
title: Fundamentals of Structural Evolution
description: An introduction to the thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing structural evolution in materials. Phase equilibria, diffusion and structural transformations. Metastable structures in materials. Self-assembling systems. Structural control through processing and/ or imposed fields. Environmental effects on structure and properties.
advisor_comments: Preference for enrollment is given to students in the combined 5-year BS-Engineering/MS-Materials or BS-Chemistry/MS-Materials programs.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to the Structure and Properties of Materials
description: Introduction to the structure of engineering materials and its relationship with their mechanical properties. Structure of solids and defects. Concepts of microstructure and origins. Elastic, plastic flow and fracture properties. Mechanisms of deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms.
advisor_comments: Not open for major credit to students who have completed Materials 100B; If students take Matrl 101 and Matrl 100B, they will only receive major credit for one course. Upper-division standing. Students interested in following the BS Engineering/MS Materials program should not take this course.

subject: MATRL
title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).
advisor_comments: Same course as Physics 135.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Polymer Science
description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.
advisor_comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 160.
prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A or Chemistry 113A or equivalent.

subject: MATRL
title: The Quantum Description of Electronic Materials
description: Electrons as particles and waves, Schrodinger's equation and illustrative solutions. Tunneling. Atomic structures, the exclusion principle and the periodic table. Bonds. Free electrons in metals, periodic potentials and energy bands.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 162A.
prereq_text: ECE 130A-B and 134 with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE, senior students in the BS/MS programs and Materials graduate students only.

subject: MATRL
title: Fundamentals of the Solid State
description: Crystal lattices and the structure of solids, with emphasis on seminconductors. Lattice vibartations. Electronic states and energy bands. Electrical and thermal conduction. Dielectic and optical properties. Semiconductor devices: diffusion, P-N junctions and diode behavior.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 162B.
prereq_text: ECE 162A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE, senior students in the BS/MS programs and Materials graduate students only.

subject: MATRL
title: Materials in Engineering
description: Introduces the student to the main families of materials and the principlesbehind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 185.

subject: MATRL
title: Manufacturing and Materials
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of common manufacturing processes and their interplay with the structure and properties of materials as they are transformed into products. Emphasis on process understanding and the key physical concepts and basic mathematical relationships involved in each of the processes discussed.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 186A.
prereq_text: ME 151C; and ME 15; and Materials 101 or Materials 100C

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
description: Introduction to additive manufacturing processes: review ofmanufacturing methods and process selection consideration, economies of production, common additive manufacturing strategies, and brief description of the physics of photopolymerization, extrusion, selective laser melting and e-beam melting fabrication.
advisor_comments: ME 186B and Materials 186B are the same course.

subject: MATRL
title: Thermodynamic Foundation of Materials
description: The microscopic statistical mechanical foundations of the macroscopic thermodynamics of materials, with applications to ideal and non-ideal gases, electrons and phonons in solids, multicomponent solutions, phase equilibria in single and multicomponent systems, and capillarity.

subject: MATRL
title: Electronic and Atomic Structure of Materials
description: The free electron model; electron levels in periodic potentials. Classification of solids. Role of electronic structure in atomic bonding and atomic packing. Cohesion. Surfaces, interfaces and junction effects. Semiconductors. Transition-metal compounds. Amorphous solids. Liquid crystals. Colloids and soft materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Structure Evolution
description: Study of phenomena underlying the evolution of structure across the relevant length and time scales in Materials. Structural defects. Drving forces, mechanisms and kinetics of structural change. Diffusional transport. Fundamentals of phase transformations. Crystallization. Evolution of microstructural features and patterns.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics for Materials
description: A primer course on quantum mechanics for materials incoming graduate students who have had limited exposure to the subject. Topics include: The Schrodinger equation, wave functions, observables and operators; solutions to a particle in a box, harmonic oscillator and a free particle; the formalism of quantum mechanics, dirac notation; angular momentum, solutions to the hydrogen atom; spin and two state systems; perturbation theory, composite systems, entanglement, Pauli exclusion principle.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Structure and Phase Stability
description: A primer course for incoming graduate students with non-MSE background. Basic concepts of structure and descriptors: crystalline and non-crystalline solids, compounds, solid solutions. Structural imperfections: point defects, dislocations and strain fields, surfaces, interfaces. Defects in ionic crystals. Thermodynamic underpinnings of phase diagrams: phase rule, chemical potential, equilibrium conditions, metastability. Unary systems. Fundamentals of binary systems, allotropes, invariant reactions, phase fractions and compositions, relationship with structure evolution. Maps for reacting systems, Ellingham diagrams, predominance diagrams. Introduction to ternary systems: liquidus surfaces and basic invariant reactions.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Magnetism and Magnetic Materials
description: Review of elementary magnetostatics. Discussion of quantum mechanical origins of magnetism. Properties of ferro-, para- dia- and antiferro-magnetics and the theories that describe them. Magnetic phenomena and materials manifesting magnetic states in both localized and itinerant limits.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Materials 288D.

subject: MATRL
title: Wide-Band Gap Materials and Devices
description: Optical and electrical properties of wide and ultra-wide band gap semiconductors (Al,In,Ga) N, SiC, Ga2O3, diamond-based semiconductor materials. Theory and practical applications of wide-band materials in electronic and optoelectronic devices. Materials growth techniques of MOCVD and MBE are discussed in the particular context of WBG semiconductors. Applications of these materials in lasers, LEDs, high frequency transistors and power devices emphasized.

subject: MATRL
title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids I
description: Introduction into the physics of semiconductors for beginning engineering graduate students. Crystal structure. Reciprocal lattice and crystal diffraction. Electrons in periodic structures. Energy and bands. Semiconductor electrons and probes, fermi statistics.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 215A.

subject: MATRL
title: Fundamentals of Electronic Solids II
description: Phonons, electron scattering, electro nic transport, selected optical properties, heterostructures, effective mass, quantum wells, two-dimensional electron gas, quantum wires, deep levels, crystal binding.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 215B.

subject: MATRL
title: Mechanics of Materials
description: Matrices and tensors, stress and deformation, compatibility and equilibrium conditions, constitutive equations, and boundary conditions, applications in elasticity, plasticity and fracture.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 219.

subject: MATRL
title: Crystallography and Diffraction Fundamentals
description: Diffraction theory: fourier transformation, schrodinger equation, Maxwell's equations, kinematical theory, Fresnel diffraction, Fraunhofer diffraction, scattering of x-rays, electrons and neutrons by isolated atoms and assemblies of atoms, pair correlation and radial distribution functions. Basic symmetry operations, point groups, space groups.

subject: MATRL
title: X-Ray Diffraction II: Advanced Methods
description: Focuses on modern diffraction techniques from crystalline materials. High resolution x-ray diffraction. Analysis of epitaxial layers. X-ray scattering theory. Simulation of x-ray rocking curves. Analysis of thin films and multiple layers. Triple-axis x-ray diffractometry. Topography. Synchrotron techniques.

subject: MATRL
title: Electron Microscopy II: Crystalline Materials
description: Electron microscopy to study defect structures, elastic and inelastic scattering, kinematics theory of image contrast, bright and dark field imaging, two-beam conditions, contrast from imperfections, dynamical theory of diffraction and image contrast. Howie Whellan equations, dispersion surface.

subject: MATRL
title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics I
description: Wave-particle duality; bound states; uncertainty relations; expectation values and operators; variational principle; eigenfunction expansions; perturbation theory I. Treatment matches needs and background of ECE and materials students emphasizing solid state or quantum electronics.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 211A.
prereq_text: ECE 162A-B. Students must have some knowledge of linear algebra.

subject: MATRL
title: Engineering Quantum Mechanics II
description: Continuation of Materials 211A; symmetry and degeneracy; electrons in crystals, angular momentum; perturbation theory II; transition probabilities; quantized fields and radiative transitions; magnetic fields;electron spin; indistinguishable particles.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 211B.
prereq_text: ECE 211A or MATRL 211A, or ECE 215A or MATRL 206A.

subject: MATRL
title: Semiconductor Device Processing
description: Intensive theoretical and laboratory instruction in solid-state device and integrated circuit fabrication. Topics include 1) semiconductor material properties and characterization; 2) phase diagrams; 3) diffusion; 4) thermal oxidation; 5) vacuum processes; 6) thin-film deposition; 7) scanning electron microscopy. Both gallium arsenide and silicon technologies are presented.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 220A.

subject: MATRL
title: Semiconductor Device Processing
description: Continued theoretical and laboratory instruction and the characterization of junction and field-effect devices. Topics will include bipolar characterization, design fabrication, and testing. The laboratory effort initiated in 215A will be continued in these two quarters.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 220B.

subject: MATRL
title: Molecular Beam Epitaxy and Band Gap Engineering
description: Fundamentals and recent research developments in the growth and properties of thin crystalline films of electronic and optical materials bythe process of molecular beam epitaxy. Artificially structured materials with quantized electron confinement and artificially engineered electronic band structure properties.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 217.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Inorganic Materials
description: Structures of inorganic materials: close-packing, linking of simple polyhedra. Factors that control structure: ionic radii, covalency, ligand field effects, metal-metal bonding, electron/atom ratios. Structure property relationships in e.g. spinels, garnets, perovskites, rutiles, fluorites, zeolites, b-aluminas, graphites, common inorganic glasses.
advisor_comments: Same course as Chemistry 277.

subject: MATRL
title: Phase Transformations
description: Introduction to the unifying concepts underlying phas transformations in metals, ceramics, polymers, and electronic materials. Includes the thermodyanamics, kinetics, crystallography and microstructural characteristics of displacive and diffusional transformations. Role of elastics, compositional, configurational, electrical, magnetic and gradientenergy contributions.

subject: MATRL
title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
description: Concepts of stress and strain. Deformation of metals, polymers, and ceramics. Elasticity, viscoelasticity, plastic flow, and creep. Linear elastic fracture mechanics. Mechanisms of ductile and brittle fracture.
advisor_comments: Same course as Mechanical Engineering 264.

subject: MATRL
title: Colloids and Interfaces I
description: Introduction to the various intermolecular interactions in solutions and in colloidal systems: Van der Waals, electrostatic, hydrophobic, solvation, H-bonding. Introduction to colloidal systems.
advisor_comments: Same course as Chemical Engineering 222A and BMSE 222A.

subject: MATRL
title: Colloids and Interfaces II
description: Continuation of 222A. Interparticle interactions, coagulation, DLVO theory, steric interactions, polymer-coated surfaces, polymers in solution, thin film viscosity. Surfactant and lipid self-assembly: micelles, microemulsions. Surfaces: wetting, contact angles, surface tension. Surfactants on surfaces: langmuir-blodgett films, adsorption, adhesion. Non-equilibrium and dynamic interactions.
advisor_comments: Materials 222A, Chemical Engineering 222A or BMSE 222A recommended. Same course as Chemical Engineering 222B & BMSE 222B.

subject: MATRL
title: Symmetry and Tensor Properties of Materials
description: Description of the principles of crystal symmetry, functional materials, and their properties, including dielectrics, piezoelectrics, and magnetic and transport phenomena. Fundamental concepts, tensorial and mathematical description of functional behavior.

subject: MATRL
title: Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition
description: Electronic and optical properties of thin films grown by vapor phase transport techniques. Growth mechanisms, kinetics and thermodynamics of vapor phase epitaxy. Special emphasis on the process of metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy for optoelectronic materials and devices.

subject: MATRL
title: Computational Materials
description: Basic computational techniques and their application to simulating the behavior of materials. Techniques include: finite difference methods, MonteCarlo, molecular dynamics, cellular automata, and simulated annealing.

subject: MATRL
title: Elasticity and Plasticity
description: Review field equations of elasticity and plasticity. Energy principles and uniqueness theorems. Elementary problems in one and two dimensions, stress functions, and complex variable methods. Plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials. Torsion and bending of plastic flow, slip line theory. Bounding theorems.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 230.

subject: MATRL
title: Plasticity
description: Plastic, creep, and relaxation behavior of solids. Mechanics of inelastically strained bodies, plastic stress-strain laws; flow potentials. Torsion and bending of prismatic bars, expansion of thick shells, plane plastic flow, slip line theory. Variational formulations, approximate methods.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 232.

subject: MATRL
title: Fracture Mechanics
description: Analytic solutions of a stationary crack under static loading. Elastic and elastoplastic analysis. The J integral. Energy balance and crack growth. Criteria for crack initiation and growth. Dynamic crack propagation. Fatigue. The micromechanics of fracture.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 275.

subject: MATRL
title: Finite Element Structural Analysis
description: Definitions and basic element operations displacement approach in linear elasticity. Element formulation: direct methods and variational methods. Global analysis procedures: assemblage and solution. Plane stress and planestrain. Solids of revolution and general solids. Isoparametric representation and numerical integration. Computer implementation.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 271.

subject: MATRL
title: Structural Inorganic Chemistry
description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and fourier series.
advisor_comments: Same course as Chem 273.

subject: MATRL
title: Symmetries and Group Theory
description: Symmetries have profound and far-reaching effects on material properties. This course introduces the fundamentals of symmetry groups as they relate to molecules and crystalline solids. Topics covered include: point and space groups, irreducible representations, tensor properties of materials, Raman and IR selection rules, Landau's theory of phase transitions.

subject: MATRL
title: Electrochemistry and Electrochemical Methods
description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrochemical methods used to study (photo)electrochemical systems for energy storage and conversion (rechargeable batteries, fuel cells, solar cells). Introduction to corrosion electrochemistry.

subject: MATRL
title: Processing of Inorganic Materials
description: Fundamental concepts and mathematical models underlying major types of processes for inorganic materials, with emphasis on the relationships between processing and microstructure. Topics include: melting and solidification, powder synthesis and consolidation, coatings and surface treatments.
advisor_comments: Lecture, 3 hours.

subject: MATRL
title: Liquid Crystal Materials
description: Thermotropic and lyotropic liquid crystals (LC's). Classification and phasetransitions. LC's in display technology. Laboratory experimentation using x-ray diffraction and polarized optical microscopy to characterize LC phases.

subject: MATRL
title: Composite Materials
description: Stress and strain relations in composites. Residual stresses. The fracture resistance of organic and inorganic matrix composites. Statistical aspects of fiber failure. Composite laminates and delamination cracks. Cumulative damage concepts. Interface properties. Design criteria.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 265.

subject: MATRL
title: Thin Films and Multilayers
description: The development of stresses in thin films and its relaxation. Edge effects and discontinuities. Cracks in films and at interfaces. Delamination of residually stressed films. Buckling and buckle propagation of compressed films. Cyclic behavior and ratcheting effects.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 267
prereq_text: Materials 207 (same course as ME 219); consent of instructor

subject: MATRL
title: Semiconductor Lasers I
description: Review of semiconductor physics, growth technology, and materials properties; double-heterostructure and quantum-well laser structures; carrier and photon rate equations; light vs. current characteristics; scattering and transmission matrices; compound cavity, distributed bragg reflector, and distributed feedback lasers.
advisor_comments: Same course as ECE 227A.
prereq_text: ECE 162A-B-C; or MATRL 162A-B and ECE 162C; or ECE 144.

subject: MATRL
title: Biomaterials and Biosurfaces
description: Fundamentals of natural and artificial biomaterials and biosurfaces with emphasis on molecular level structure and function and their interactions with the body. Design issues of grafts and biopolymers.Basic biological, biophysical and biochemical systems reviewed for nonbiologists.
advisor_comments: Same as ChE 202 and BMSE 202

subject: MATRL
title: Synthesis and Properties of Macromolecules
description: Basics of preparation of polymer and macromolecular assemblies, and characterization of large molecules and assemblies. Discussion of chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.
repeat_comments: MATRL 271A and CHEM 271A are the same course.

subject: MATRL
title: Structure and Characterization of Complex Fluids
description: Structure, phase behavior, and phase transitions in complex fluids. Characterization techniques including x-ray and neutron scattering, and light and microscopy methods. Systems include colloidal and surfactant dispersions (e.g., polyballs, microemulsions, and micells), polymeric solutions and biomolecular materials (e.g., lyotropic liquid crystals).

subject: MATRL
title: Properties of Macromolecules
description: Fundamentals of the properties of macromolecular solutions, melts, and solids. Viscosity, diffusion and light scattering from dilute solutions. Elements of macromolecular solid state structure. Thermal properties and processes. Mechanical and transport properties. Introduction to electrical and optical properties of macromolecules.
advisor_comments: Lecture, 3 hours.

subject: MATRL
title: Mechanical Forces and Biomolecules
description: Explores single-molecule biophysics and the role of mechanical force in biomolecular behavior. Emphasis is placed on modern experimental techniques and the effects of mechanical stress on DNA conformation, protein unfolding, and force-generation by motor proteins. Recent literature is used throughout.
advisor_comments: Same course as BMSE 272.

subject: MATRL
title: Experiments in Macromolecular Materials
description: Experiments using X-ray and light scattering, optical and electron microscopy. Crystalline, quasi-crystalline and amorphous materials. Solid, solution, and colloidal samples.
advisor_comments: Lecture, 3 hours; laboratory, 4 hours.

subject: MATRL
title: Solid State Inorganic Materials
description: An introductory course describing the synthesis, physical characterization, structure, electronic properties and uses of solid state materials.
advisor_comments: Same course as Chemistry 274.

subject: MATRL
title: Biomolecular Materials I: Structure and Function
description: Survey of classes of biomolecules (lipids, carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids). Structure and function of molecular machines (enzymes for biosynthesis, motors, pumps).
repeat_comments: Same course as BMSE 276A.

subject: MATRL
title: Interaction in Biomolecular Complexes
description: Focuses on the interactions, structures, and functional properties of complexes comprised of supramolecular assemblies of biological molecules. Systems addressed include lipid membranes, lipid-DNA complexes, and assemblies of proteins of the cell cytoskeleton.

subject: MATRL
title: First-Principles Calculations for Materials
description: Basic theory and methods of electronic structure, illustrated with examples of practical computational methods and real-world applications. Topics: Band structure; Uniform electron gas; Density functional theory; Exchange and correlation; Kohn-Sham equations; Pseudopotentials; Basis sets; Predicting materials properties: bulk, surfaces, interfaces, defects.

subject: MATRL
title: Introduction to Organic Electronics
description: Electronic properties of organic semiconductors and the effects of molecular structure. Influence of processing on electronic properties. Processing methods for organic optoelectronic devices. Discussion of measurements of transport and exemplary devices including thin film transistors, light emitting diodes, and photovoltaics.

subject: MATRL
title: Technical Communication and Presentation Design
description: Focuses on a practical, hands-on, interactive approach to developing communication skills and presentation style. Using current literature and seminars, critical attributes such as clearly explaining complex ideas, the do's and don'ts of presentation will be covered.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Inorganic Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will include in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in inorganic materials.

subject: MATRL
title: In Situ/ In Operando Methods for Materials Science Research
description: Overview of various in situ / in operando techniques used to characterize functional materials during normal operation, to investigate the processes of materials synthesis and phase transformations, to isolate transient or metastable states. X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, IR, Raman, diffraction techniques, magnetic resonance techniques, electron microscopy, etc. Advantages and limitations. Important considerations when devising a new in situ set up / probe.

subject: MATRL
title: Advanced TEM
description: Intended for graduate students who are using transmission electron microscopy in their research. Covers imaging theory, lens aberrations, contrast transfer functions, dynamical diffraction theories, and diffraction contrast from a wide range of crystal defects (planar defects, dislocations, etc.). Also discusses the basics of scanning transmission electron microscopy techniques. Meant to complement the more practical training in 209C, but 209C is not a pre-requisite.

subject: MATRL
title: Two-Dimensional Moiré Materials
description: Explores two-dimensional moiré materials, focusing on how stacking and twisting atomically thin crystals creates highly tunable electronic properties. Small relative rotations produce moiré superlattices and flat electronic bands, enabling strong electron correlations and new quantum phases. Topics include fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, superconductivity, correlated insulators, orbital ferromagnetism, topological order, and model systems such as the triangular Hubbard model. Students develop the concepts needed to critically read current research papers and re-derive their central results.

subject: MATRL
title: Fundamental and Applied Concepts in Ceramics for Electrochemical Technologies
description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with ceramic materials used in state-of-the-art Li ion batteries and that can enable advanced electrochemical technologies such as solid-state and electrical grid batteries. The course will briefly cover fundamental aspects of ceramics and their processing, solid-state electrochemistry, and the design, manufacturing, and characterization of state-of-the-art Li ion and advanced battery concepts. Depending on class size, hands-on learning activities may be planned for the end of the semester where students or student teams will learn how to make and electrochemically characterize Li ion and Li metal electrodes with conventional liquid electrolytes and/or solid-state electrolytes.

subject: MATRL
title: Optical Characterization of Materials
description: Optical techniques encompass a wide variety of tools for materials characterization. After reviewing light-matter interactions and optical properties of materials, this course surveys a selection of optical techniques commonly used in materials science, including optical conductivity, Raman and IR spectroscopy, the magneto-optic Kerr effect, and photoemission spectroscopy.

subject: MATRL
title: Experiments in Inorganic Materials
description: Experimental methods of interrogating electronic ground states and phase behaviors in inorganic materials are presented. Examples include heat capacity, spin susceptibility, electrical/thermal transport, Raman, and spin resonance techniques. The fundamental physics and materials properties underlying each technique are be taught and illustrated by the states/phase behaviors accessible by each.

subject: MATRL
title: Functional Inorganic Oxides
description: Intended to give a broad overview of the properties, chemistry and applications of functional inorganic oxides. The course is organized according to structure types (rocksalts, fluorites, rutiles, spinels, corundums, garnets, perovskites, zeolites, etc.) picking up important themes and properties within each group.

subject: MATRL
title: Topics in Quantum Materials Measurement
description: Discusses current topics in Quantum Materials Measurement through journal readings, studies of background materials provided, and student presentations. Examples include mesoscopic and quantum transport phenomena as well as phenomena at interfaces and junctions.

subject: MATRL
title: Quantum Phenomena in Mesoscopic Materials and Devices
description: This course develops the physical principles behind quantum behavior in nanoscale solid-state devices where phase coherence, confinement, and interactions dominate transport. Topics include quantum point contacts (quantized conductance and shot noise), quantum dots (Coulomb blockade, single-electron tunneling, and Kondo physics), and focus on real materials like topological insulators and superconductors. The course also introduces superconducting hybrid structures and Josephson junction physics, emphasizing how mesoscopic effects emerge in real devices and measurement setups. Students will connect simplified theoretical models to experimental signatures commonly observed in low-temperature nanoelectronics.

subject: MATRL
title: Theoretical Foundations of Quantum Materials
description: A rigorous treatment of selected topics in modern solid state physics, including theoretical frameworks (second quantization, Green's functions, density matrix formalism, response functions), many-body effects (interacting electron gas, Fermi liquid theory, electron-phonon coupling, quantum spin models), superconductivity (Ginzburg-Landau theory, BCS theory, Josephson effect, quantum vortices), and topological phenomena (Landau levels and the quantum Hall effect, Berry phase and curvature, modern theory of polarization, topological insulators and superconductors, Majorana fermions).

subject: MATRL
title: The Art of Scientific Writing
description: This course is about reading the scientific literature critically, and about writing science that is simultaneously impactful and readable. We will discuss what makes scientific papers compelling without being obscure and ambiguous and will practice through critiquing each other’s written work. Preparing tables and graphics, and formatting text will be an intrinsic part of the discussion. Grades will be assigned based on manuscripts produced before the end of the quarter.

subject: MATRL
title: Solid State Ionics and Electrochem Devices
description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with ceramic materials used in state-of-the-art Li ion batteries and that can enable advanced electrochemical technologies such as solid-state and electrical grid batteries. The course will briefly cover fundamental aspects of ceramics and their processing, solid-state electrochemistry, and the design, manufacturing, and characterization of state-of-the-art Li ion and advanced battery concepts.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Macromolecular Materials
description: This course will be offered on a irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in macromolecular materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Structure and Symmetry
description: Fundamentals of structure and symmetry commonly observed in soft materials. Direct and reciprocal space lattices, symmetry operations, group theory categorization, and tensor calculations of distances, angles, and coordinate transformations. Experimental structure determination. Complex phases.

subject: MATRL
title: Sustainability in Materials Science
description: Survey of the role of materials in sustainability. Overview of topics in materials usage and recycling, materials designs for energy efficiency, and manufacturing. Key concepts and models for sustainability including life cycle/materials flow analysis, and energy content. Considerations for sustainability of major classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, and polymers. Applications in energy conversion and storage.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Electronic Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in electronic materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Materials for Quantum Information Science
description: Selected topics relating to materials issues in Quantum Information Science. Quantum Defects: single-spin centers, single-photon emitters. Natively Entangled Materials. Interfaced Topological States.

subject: MATRL
title: Power Semiconductor Materials and Devices
description: Material properties and transport physics relevant to power devices, power rectifiers and transistors, superjunctions, wide bandgap power device technologies, emerging topics in power semiconductors.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Electronic Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depth discussions of advanced topics in electronic materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Special Topics in Structural Materials
description: This course will be offered on an irregular basis and will concern in-depthdiscussions of advanced topics in structural materials.

subject: MATRL
title: Phase Stability & Microstructure Evolution
description: Phase diagrams for binary, ternary and higher order systems: thermodynamic foundation, construction and applications. Metastability upon synthesis and processing far from equilibrium: approaches, thermodynamic and kinetic principles, phase selection, solubility extension. Stability and evolution of metastable phases and microstructures.

subject: MATRL
title: Statistical Mechanics of Crystalline Solids
description: Covers first-principles methods to predict thermodynamic and kinetic properties of multi-component crystalline solids. Topics include: (i) a review of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics of crystalline solids; (ii) effective Hamiltonians for configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom with a focus on the Ising model, cluster expansions, harmonic and anharmonic lattice dynamical Hamiltonians; (iii) Monte Carlo methods, low temperature expansions, free energy integration methods; (iv) First-principles methods to calculate multi-component phase diagrams; (v) Order-disorder and structural phase transitions and (vi) Atomic diffusion, transition state theory, kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, Kubo-Green.

subject: MATRL
title: Crystal Growth and Solidification
description: Addresses crystallization from the melt and solidification of alloys and compounds. Fundamental macroscopic thermal, fluid and mass transfer aspects of growth. Nucleation, growth, the stability of solid/liquid interfaces and microstructure formation during solidification of multicomponent systems. Crystal growth processes are addressed, including Czrochralski and Bridgman growth, shape casting methods and directed energy processes.

subject: MATRL
title: Topics in Engineering Leadership
description: As technology increasingly drives strategy and innovation, technical professionals must nurture leadership skills to effectively guide teams, influence organizational decisions, and translate complex technical concepts into value. This graduate-level course introduces essential skills in self-awareness, team management, strategic communication, effective mentorship, negotiation, feedback delivery, and budget management. Each week combines theoretical foundations with hands-on practice through role-playing case studies and conversations with technical leaders. By course completion, students will have exposure to a comprehensive toolkit for charting their leadership journey and driving organizational success.

subject: MATRL
title: Dislocations and Dislocation Dynamics
description: Fundamentals of dislocations in crystalline solids and the dynamical behavior of dislocations. Topics covered include: elastic properties of dislocations, dislocation interactions, intersections, arrays, nucleation and sources. Thermally activated glide and climb are addressed along with statistical aspects of dislocation obstacle interactions. Partial dislocations, faults and unique aspects of dislocations in metals, semiconductors, ceramics and intermetallics are covered.

subject: MATRL
title: Machine Learning for Materials Science
description: Covers the fundamentals of machine learning tools used in materials science. Application areas include surrogate models for atomistic simulations as well as machine-learning tools for 3-dimensional image analysis and the analysis of experimental data. The course starts with an overview of probability theory and Bayesian inference followed by treatments of regularized regression, Gaussian process models and neural networks.
