description: Students attend the 33-day paid Leadership Development Advanced Course designed to further develop and evaluate leadership and officer potential. The challenges are rigorous and demanding, both mentally and Physically, and will test intelligence, common sense, ingenuity and stamina.
prereq_text: Students must have had successfully completed MS 131, 132, and MS 133, and three quarters of MS 22 prior to attending this course. Students must meet US Army Officer contracted Qualification and Documentation Requirements.
prereq_gold: MS 131 and MS 132 and MS 133; MS 22 and MS 22 and MS 22

subject: MS
title: Independent Studies
description: Independent studies with the professor to permit study on a subject agreed by the student and professor, not covered by regular course offerings.
advisor_comments: Students are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of at least two upper-division courses in military science; open only to ROTC advanced students approved by the department chair.

subject: MUS A
title: Wind Ensemble
description: Masterworks of the literature for ensembles smaller than orchestral or full band scoring. Although the basic ensembles feature winds, both strings and percussion are utilized.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units. Advanced players only.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: UCSB Chamber Choir
description: A select ensemble of voice majors and non-majors, the Chamber Choir prepares musicians for professional ensemble work and offers advanced study in choral literature, techniques, styles and interpretation covering five centuries of choral repertoire.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.
repeat_comments: May be repeated a total of 9 quarters in combination with A136A/A136B/A136C. Six quarters for credit in the major.

subject: MUS A
title: UCSB Concert Choir
description: The UCSB Concert Choir is a mixed-voice ensemble open to all voice types (SATB). No audition required. Singers build musicianship and ensemble skills through diverse repertoire, weekly rehearsals, and public performances.
repeat_comments: ?May be repeated for a total of 9 units and maximum of six units in the major.

subject: MUS A
title: UCSB Singing Gauchos
description: The UCSB Singing Gauchos is a tenor and bass choir performing fine choral literature representative of various style periods and vocal techniques from the global choral tradition. Regular performances on and off campus.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.
repeat_comments: May be repeated a total of 9 times.

subject: MUS A
title: Opera Workshop
description: Participation in opera scenes.
advisor_comments: Letter grade required for majors. May repeated for credit to a maximum of 9units.

subject: MUS A
title: The Fundamentals of Popular Guitar
description: A skills course designed for developing guitar technique used in folk, rock, blues, classical and jazz styles. The curriculum focuses on strumming patterns, finger picking, chords and their voicings, riffs and soloing. Emphasis is on learning to play songs by ear. Neck geography is taught through relational patterns of scales and modes. All guitar types (acoustic, classical, electric) are welcome, though acoustic/ classical are preferred. This class accommodates a variety of playing levels, from complete beginner to intermediate-advanced shredders and classical players, and everything in-between. Guitar to be provided by the student.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to six units.

subject: MUS A
title: Ensemble for Contemporary Music
description: Reading sessions and preparation for performance of contemporary music. There will be one or two concerts each quarter. Includes departmental scholarship players, and is open to composers who also perform.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 9 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Collaborative Creation Lab: Composers and Performers
description: A living laboratory of collaboration between composers and performers, exploring sound as a shared terrain through the creation of acoustic, electroacoustic, and hybrid works.

subject: MUS A
title: Piano Ensemble
description: Piano duets (1 piano, 4 hands) and duos (2 pianos) in separate sections.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units but only 6 units may be applied toward the major.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. Upper-division students only.

subject: MUS A
title: Orchestra
description: UCSB Chamber Orchestra performs pieces from the traditional chamber orchestra repertoire, as well as more contemporary pieces for chamber orchestra.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Flute Choir
description: The flute choir studies flute literature in depth, perfects technique and interpretation, employs the complete flute family of bass, alto flutes and piccolos. Prepares ensemble for public performances each quarter.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.

subject: MUS A
title: Chamber Music Ensemble
description: Chamber music ensemble.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 18 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Brass Quintet
description: Participation in scholarship brass quintet.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.

subject: MUS A
title: Brass Orchestral Repertoire
description: Intensive exploration of staple brass orchestral repertoire, emphasizing the works of important 19th and 20th century composers. Classes include rehearsal sessions, guided listening and analysis, mock auditions, resume and taped audition preparation.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.

subject: MUS A
title: Horn Ensemble
description: Horn ensemble.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.

subject: MUS A
title: Jazz Ensemble
description: Instruction in interpretation and performance of jazz music. Improvisation is stressed.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.

subject: MUS A
title: Percussion Ensemble
description: Rehearsal and performance of standard percussion ensemble literature. Instruction of appropriate playing techniques for standard and exotic percussion instruments.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Cello Choir
description: The cello choir studies cello literature in depth, including duos, trios, quartets and larger cello ensemble works. Cellists work together on blend of sound, perfecting technique and intonation, as well as balance.The choir will prepare works for public performances.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures: A. American folk music I. Indian music J. Gamelan M. Middle Eastern music P. West African drumming V. Gospel choir.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble: Music of India: Sitar
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures: I) Indian music.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-divisiostudents.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures, Gamalan.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures: M) Middle East Music.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to nine units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-divisiostudents.

subject: MUS A
title: Middle East Chorus
description: The chorus learns a variety of songs from Arab, Armenian, Greek, Persian Turkish music cultures and performs with the Middle East ensemble.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units, but only 6 units may beapplied toward the major.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-divisiostudents.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble: Son Jarocho
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures: Son Jarocho.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble: Mariachi
description: Group performance of music from selected world cultures: Mariachi.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 9 units.
prereq_text: Enrollment by audition with the exception of Music A170J. For upper-division students.

subject: MUS A
title: Ethnomusicology Performance Ensemble

subject: MUS CS
title: Algorithmic Composition with Max/MSP
description: A formalized journey into the basics of algorithmic composition, using Max/MSP as a tool to aid the artist and engineer alike. We explore how simple algorithmic models can provide intriguing sonic results across all genres. These methods are not only useful for schematic problem solving but can also be good for expanding musical and creative thinking.

subject: MUS CS
title: Art Song
description: Explorations of text setting, repertory, effective accompaniments. Content will vary by instructor.

subject: MUS CS
title: The Classical Guitar in Contemporary Composition
description: A survey of modern classical guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to popular music, the classical tradition, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original classical guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

subject: MUS CS
title: The Electric Guitar in Contemporary Composition
description: A survey of modern electric guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to rock, classical, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original electric guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

subject: MUS CS
title: Favorite Things
description: Students will analyze and present their favorite works, whether acoustic or electronic; tonal or atonal or serial; chamber or orchestral or vocal. Subsequently, students will write music of their own, based on a single, well-defined element from the works they admire.

subject: MUS CS
title: Language Lost: Music Creation and the Destruction of Meaning
description: How can composers maintain expressiveness in vocal music when specific meanings are elusive? We will focus on the manipulation of sound/speech qualities such as pitch, rhythm, phrasing, timbre, and tempo. Our multidisciplinary approach aims to both create and deconstruct language, exploring new technologies to enhance individual expression and innovate in musical communication.

subject: MUS CS
title: Landscape Music
description: A study of music written in response to the natural and the built landscape(s) around us.

subject: MUS CS
title: 1960S MUSICAL REVOLUTIONARIES: MILES DAVIS, JIMI HENDRIX, YOKO ONO, AND KARLHEINZ STOCKHAUSEN
description: Delves into the iconic 1960s, exploring the revolutionary impact of major figures Miles Davis, Jimi Hendrix, Yoko Ono, and Karlheinz Stockausen in their particular and overlapping domains. It offers a mix of music history and performative collaboration, welcoming students from all disciplines, regardless of their musical background.

subject: MUS CS

subject: MUS CS
title: Questions About Music
description: What is the essence of music? The nature of musical form and communication? What is at the heart of music making and music listening? What is music’s role in society? How do composers think and talk about music? This course explores these and other “questions about music” via the written word, personal reflection, and in-class discussion.

subject: MUS CS

description: Explore the intersection of "synths" and sci-fi cinema in this course. We'll analyze iconic film scores and director/composer collaborations from the 1950s to today, including Kubrick/Carlos and Nolan/Zimmer. The course blends viewing sessions with discussions, presentations, and performances. Students have the opportunity to compose or improvise their own sci-fi soundscapes.

description: Introduces students to ways of studying music as a cultural practice situated in society. Methods are drawn from musicology, ethnomusicology, history, anthropology, and sociology. Students will be taught to think critically about music as a universal human expression.

description: Examines how modern technologies and acoustical thought reshaped composition, moving from notation toward sound as structure, material, and expressive force.

subject: MUS

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1545-1745
description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations from Renaissance through Enlightenment (1545-1745). Topics include musicians’ careers and social life; spirituality; gender, race, emerging subjectivity; music for public stages; commercialism; colonialism; popular music practices. Western music notation experience required.

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1745-1848
description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1748-1848. Topics include a range of composers/performers/listeners and how conceptions of musical practices were shaped by socio-political context, colonialism, class, gender, race, religion, economics. Western music notation experience required.

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1848-1945
description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1848-1945, including its philosophical, artistic, and social contexts. Topics include nationalism; late romanticism and limits tonality; modernism; impact of popular music on western classical music; neoclassicism. Western music notation experience required.

subject: MUS
title: The History of Opera: 1600-1800
description: An overview of the history of opera from 1600-1800, placing selected works within a social context, and viewing opera as a musical work, dramatic spectacle, and cultural commodity.

subject: MUS
title: Music and Popular Culture in America
description: A survey of the relationships between music and popular culture in America. Music to be discussed includes blues, jazz, and rock, as well as classical music. Emphasis is on cultural, rather than technical aspects of music.

subject: MUS

advisor_comments: Contact departmental advisor for an approval code if concurrently enrolled in Music 3A.

subject: MUS
title: American Music History: From the Colonial Period to the Present
description: An overview of the varieties of American musical experience from the Colonial period to the present. Representative works from several genres are studies with a view to placing them in their cultural context and identifying major aesthetic issues.

subject: MUS
title: American Experimental Music: John Cage and After
description: A survey of the American experimental tradition in music and related arts, starting with John Cage and continuing through generations of those have followed in his path through the present day. Students will read primary sources by these artists as well as secondary literature from theoretical and historical perspectives; course activities will also include study and discussion of experimental artworks, written responses, and creative activities.

subject: MUS
title: Music and the Mind
description: Introduction to the psychology of music. Topics include music perception and cognition, learning and memory, emotion and meaning, music and language, music and the brain, emergence and development of skills, perspectives from social and cultural psychology, well-being and therapy, and others.

subject: MUS

description: Examines women’s musical practices from the past millennium to rethink narratives of Western music, past and present. We study musicians from the Middle Ages onward to examine and challenge feminine archetypes in Western music.

description: An intensive examination of the system of melodic modes (Maqamat) that governs present-day practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordel structures, and theories of intonation), analysis of standard repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

subject: MUS
title: Analysis of Popular Music
description: Explores different approaches to analyzing popular music (specifically post-1960, predominantly American popular music), including not only theory and analysis of harmony and melody, form, timbre, rhythm/meter but also issues of meanings and expression, intertextuality, race and gender.

subject: MUS
title: Film Music Cognition
description: A consideration of film music as a medium of communication between the director, composer, music supervisor, editors, performers and the audience. Emphasis given to cognitive psychological theories of meaning in terms of structure and affect in audio/visual contexts.

subject: MUS
title: Music and Documentary Film
description: View global popular music through the lens of documentary film. We will analyze a series of films depicting cultural and political histories, creative performances, and everyday lives of musicians in different representational frames and social contexts.

subject: MUS
title: The Musical World of the Grateful Dead: from Americana to Psychedelia
description: An examination of the Grateful Dead and its impact on popular culture, festivals and the music business. We study the Dead’s music from folk to improvisational rock as a creative Americana response to the political turbulence of the Sixties.

subject: MUS
title: Creative Arts, Memories and Experimental Performance
description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.
advisor_comments: Cross-Listing Course with Theater and Dance

subject: MUS
title: Music and Sports
description: In this course, students study connections between the human cultural practices of music and sport. We draw from rich literatures in performance studies, sports studies, and ethnomusicology to consider selected case studies where music and sport intersect.

subject: MUS
title: Birds, sonic arts & environmental sensitivities
description: Focusing on birds and sonic arts, this course engages creative, analytical & experiential activities. Topics include: ecoacoustics, sound maps, deep listening, sensory memory, soundscape ecologies and environmental issues, blurring borders between more-than-human/human interactions, art/science, and local/global.
repeat_comments: Repeat of MUS168G with Hellier-Tinoco in Spring 2021.

subject: MUS
title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music, Her Life, Her Times
description: Analysis of the music, life, an times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance practice, and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

subject: MUS
title: Understanding Brazilian Music in its Cultural Context
description: This course enables students to understand what Brazilian music is, and what is the role of Music in Brazilian culture. It offers a comprehensive panel of the history of music in Brazil. The course also provides students with a full cultural context, discussing the role of music during the two dictatorship periods in Brazil, 1930-1945 and 1964-1985 and the political impact of censorship. It also discusses the contributions of the Africans, brought to Brazil by the Portuguese colonizers, and the impact African culture has both in music and religion. Taught in English.
advisor_comments: MUS 178BR, C LIT 131B, and PORT 110 are the same course.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World: The Middle East
description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World: India
description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis on the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rhythmic structures (Raga and Tala).

subject: MUS
title: Music in Modern Japan
description: This course explores music and culture in modern Japan. What kind of society do we hear in its diverse mix of sounds and musical practices? We explore this question through traditional genres, national politics, and transnational exchanges of popular media.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World: Other Regions
description: A study of music traditions and genres from other regions of the world. Specific regions studied vary by quarter and are announced in advance by the department.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units.

subject: MUS
title: Environmental Sound Arts
description: Environmental Sound Arts focuses on responses to, and uses of environmental sounds in the broadest framework of soundscapes and environmental humanities, encompassing processes of fieldwork listening , analysis, and creation of new environmental sound art for public facing advocacy work.
prereq_text: Upper division standing, instructor approval required.

subject: MUS
title: Music, Community, Wellbeing: Advocacy and Activism
description: Taking a vocational and facilitatory approach, this course uses case studies to explore concepts and processes of generating and sustaining musical activity as community-engaged practice. Topics include: social justice, health and wellbeing, education, senses of place, ecology, and technology.

subject: MUS

description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.

advisor_comments: For Distinction in the Major must be taken with Music 192 or 197 or 197B.
repeat_comments: Music 196 is available not only in conjunction with Music 192, 197, and 197B for Departmental Senior Honors (Distinction in the Major), but can also be taken separately for other Honors projects by students in the College of Letters and Science Honors program.

description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers qualified students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group in topics in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor.

subject: MUS

description: Faculty supervised research assistance.

Students are limited to 4 units per quarter and 16 units total in Music 198/199 courses. No more than 4 units in combination with Music 199 may be applied to major.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor and department.

subject: MUS
title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods.
advisor_comments: Primarily intended for the MM and DMA graduate student in Music.

subject: MUS
title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: Survey and discussion of select historical, methodological, and theoretical approaches to research in musicology.
advisor_comments: Primarily intended for the M.A. and Ph.D. graduate student in musicology or theory.

subject: MUS
title: Bibliography and Research Techniques
description: A survey of music bibliography and research methods in theory.
advisor_comments: Primarily for the M.A. and Ph.D. graduate student in theory.

subject: MUS
title: Musicology-Theory Forum
description: Theory students, faculty and visiting scholars present their current research.
prereq_text: Graduate standing in musicology or theory emphasis.

subject: MUS
title: Graduate Composition
description: Individual instruction in composition.
advisor_comments: Required for M.A. and Ph.D. in composition.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: MUS
title: Direct Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
description: First quarter of general purpose computing for computer music applications. Topics include: introduction to the UNIX operating system and the vi editor, music synthesis using C-based computer programs and score input programs.
advisor_comments: Graduate music majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics, and mathematics.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Electroacoustic Music
description: An introductory course on electroacoustic music. Historical perspective. Analysis of different types of electronic/acousmatic/mixed compositions. Introduction to different techniques of sound transformation.
advisor_comments: Required for Composition majors. Music majors and non-majors may also enroll.

subject: MUS
title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
description: First quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on multi-track recording, mixing, digital signal processing using micro-computers and special purpose dsp equipment.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor. Graduate music majors and graduate non-majors in areas of electrical engineering, computer science, physics, and mathematics.

subject: MUS
title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
description: Second quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on digital synthesis (primarily frequency modulation, simple and complex; but also amplitude modulation and additive synthesis) using micro-computers, digital synthesizers and processing equipment.

subject: MUS
title: Real-Time Digital Music Synthesis, Processing and Composition
description: Third quarter of a three-quarter sequence course will concentrate on real-time computer music composition with micro-computer and digital synthesis/processing equipment.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Visual Music
description: Introductory course on Visual Music. Historical perspective. Introduction to Final Cut Pro, After Effects, Cinema 4D and other visual music composition software.Several short exercises will be required during the quarter.
advisor_comments: Designed essentially for majors. Non-majors may also enroll with the consent of the instructor.
prereq_text: Mus 211B or Mus 109IA or Mus 209IA or Mus 109LA or Mus 209LA or consent of instructor.

subject: MUS
title: Visual Music Composition
description: Visual Music composition. Mixing, synthesis, animation, sound-image integration. An original Visual Music composition is required after the end of the course.
advisor_comments: Designed essentially for majors. Non-majors may also enroll with the consent of the instructor. May be repeated with permission of instructor but used only once for credit in major.
prereq_text: MUS 209TA or consent of the instructor

subject: MUS
title: Contemporary Composition Techniques (Instrumental)
description: Study of different compositional techniques based on the analysis of pieces from the repertoire. Rhythm manipulation, harmonic contents, formal aspects, integration between instruments and electronics, extended techniques, gesture control, etc. A short paper explaining the application of one or more of these techniques in an original composition is required after the end of the course.
advisor_comments: Designed/required for Composition majors.
prereq_text: Passing grade on all theory placement examinations.

subject: MUS
title: Contemporary Composition Techniques (Electroacoustic)
description: Study of different compositional techniques based on sound objects transformations. Analysis of pieces from the repertoire. Synthesis, recording, mixing, sound object transformation techniques, spatialization. An original 5-8 min acousmatic/electronic music composition is required after the end of the course.
repeat_comments: Designed/required for Composition majors. Music majors and non-majors may also enroll with the consent of the instructor. Usually taught in Winter quarter. May be repeated with permission of instructor but used only once for major credit.
prereq_text: Mus 209L or Mus 209IA or Mus 209LA or consent of the instructor

subject: MUS
title: Applied Instruction
description: Applied vocal or instrumental instruction for graduate students other than in the performance emphasis discipline of MM and DMA degree programs.
advisor_comments: Not for the performance emphasis in MM or DMA degree programs.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: MUS
title: MM/DMA Performance Instruction
description: Applied instruction in the performance emphasis discipline (MM piano accompanying: instruction in piano) of MM and DMA degree programs.
advisor_comments: Restricted to MM and DMA majors admitted to the performance emphasis in voice or the specific instrument of study in Music 220.
prereq_text: Entrance audition for MM or DMA degree program.

subject: MUS
title: Practicum in World Music Performance
description: Individual or group instruction in non-Western instruments: the Indian sitar, the Middle Eastern `ud (lute) and nay (end-blown flute), and Middle Eastern percussion.
advisor_comments: Graduate standing.

subject: MUS
title: Practicum in World Music Performance
description: Individual or group instruction in non-Western instruments: the Indian sitar, the Middle Eastern `ud (lute) and nay (end-blown flute), and Middle Eastern percussion.
advisor_comments: Graduate standing.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Ethnomusicology
description: A graduate seminar examining special problems, current theories, analytic procedures, and recent innovations in ethnomusicology.

subject: MUS
title: Orchestral Conducting
description: Advanced conducting techniques, score reading and analysis, general rehearsal procedures and repertoire for each type of ensemble: symphony, chamber orchestra and large vocal/instrumental ensembles.
advisor_comments: Enrollment by audition. May be repeated for credit.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Conducting
description: Advanced conducting techniques, score reading and analysis, rehearsal techniques and repertoire for vocal and choral ensembles.
advisor_comments: Enrollment by audition. May be repeated for credit.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Techniques
description: Aspects of choral techniques, including: development of concert programs and rehearsal plans, rehearsal procedures, types of vocal ensembles and seating configurations, acoustical considerations, performance and recording procedures, long-term programming and artistic development, social and organization aspects of vocal ensemble.
prereq_text: Music 231 (may be taken concurrently) and consent of instructor.

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Music Theory
description: Analysis and theory of atonal music.

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Schenkerian Analysis
description: Readings in the theory of Schenkerian analysis. Basic analytical techniques.
prereq_text: Must be taken in consecutive order.

subject: MUS
title: Viola Orchestral Repertoire
description: The study of the entire standard orchestral repertoire for viola and audition procedures.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for up to 36 units.

subject: MUS
title: Vocal and Instrumental Coaching
description: Musical preparation of vocal or instrumental works.
prereq_text: Concurrent graduate vocal or instrumental study (Music 220, 219, 235) graduate standing; consent of instructor.

subject: MUS
title: Composition Forum
description: A forum for the presentation and discussion of new works by students, faculty, and guest composers.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units toward major.

subject: MUS
title: Opera/Song Repertoire
description: A detailed study of operatic literature and concert literature (Lieder, melodies, songs, and pieces with instruments). The interpretation of vocal music as a preparation for performance.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cognition
description: Surveys research in music cognition and introduces empirical methods for studying music. Topics include music perception and cognition, memory and expectation, emotion and meaning, emergence and development of skills and performance, perspectives from social and cultural psychology, among others.

subject: MUS
title: Tuning and Temperament
description: The course surveys a number of tuning systems around the world, including those of ancient Greece, Europe, India, China, the Arab Middle East, Turkey, and Indonesia. The mathematical, aesthetic, and symbolic basis of each system will be considered.

subject: MUS
title: The Arab System of Melodic Modes (Maqamat)
description: Examination of the system of melodic modes (maqamat) governing present-day melodic practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordal structures, theories of intonation), analysis of pieces in the repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

subject: MUS
title: Tonal Analysis Review
description: An in-depth review of elements and procedures of 18th- and 19th-century harmony, aimed at analyzing conventional formal types (binary, ternary, rondo, sonata, sonata-rondo, concerto).

subject: MUS
title: Other Issues in Ethnomusicology
description: A study of other cultural issues in ethnomusicology. Specific topics vary by quarter and will be announced in advanced by the department.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 16 units, provided topics are different.

subject: MUS
title: Music as Media
description: Recorded media are central to the way we hear, create, exchange and experience music in contemporary social life. Topics include the early uses of the phonograph, recording studios, file-sharing, online musical exchange and roles of technological media in globalizing cultures.

subject: MUS
title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music. Her Life. Her Times.
description: Analysis of the music, life and times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance, practice and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Musicology
description: Graduate Seminar in Musicology. Topics will vary.

subject: MUS
title: Seminar in Musicology: The Twentieth Century
description: Graduate seminar in music of the twentieth century.

subject: MUS
title: Studies in Music Theory
description: Selected topics in musical analysis.

subject: MUS
title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.

subject: MUS
title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.

subject: MUS
title: Proseminar in Classical Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of classical music.

subject: MUS
title: Proseminar in Romantic Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of romantic music.

subject: MUS
title: Proseminar in Contemporary Music
description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of contemporary music.

subject: MUS
title: Ethnomusicology Forum
description: A forum for the presentation of research and performances by students, faculty, and visiting scholars and performers. Students must be currently involved in a research or performance project.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Music 222.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World: Middle East
description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Music 221.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World: India
description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis given to the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rythmic structures (raga and tala).
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Music 216.

subject: MUS
title: Master of Music Performances
description: Preparation of: a. a full length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a full-length concert.)
prereq_text: Recital audition required. Master of Music students only.

subject: MUS

prereq_text: Recital audition required. Master of Music students only.

advisor_comments: DMA (including MM Plan 2) students only.

subject: MUS
title: Doctor of Musical Arts Performances
description: Preparation of a full-length recital (conducting: the equivalent of a full-length concert).
advisor_comments: DMA (including MM Plan 2) students only.

subject: MUS
title: Doctor of Musical Arts Seminar: Historical/Theoretical Aspects of Music
description: A study of selected repertories, not confined to a single genre or period, from the technical perspective of music thoery and history.

subject: MUS
title: Teaching Practicum
description: Teaching assistant: leads discussion of topics covered in the lecture. Associate: assumes full responsibility for the teaching of one or more courses.
advisor_comments: Appointment as teaching assistant or associate. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.

subject: MUS
title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
description: Designed to serve all A.B.D. graduate students in the academic areas who are at various stages of writing their dissertation thesis. Seminar will be organized as a workshop in which all students will present portions of their writing for discussion. As tailored to each students project, we will discuss a number of dissertation writing challenges and learn how to self-edit and critically evaluate effective thesis writing.
repeat_comments: No Restrictions on number of times students may take the course. Only two courses (4 Units) can be counted towards the degree as elective units.

subject: MUS
title: Special Topics
description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

subject: MUS
title: Special Topics
description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

subject: MUS
title: Music Pedagogy
description: Covers theories, principles, and practical techniques for teaching music, especially in undergraduate-level music classroom instruction. Topics may include learning objectives, assessments, music-specific challenges, inclusive pedagogy, lesson planning, and writing teaching philosophies. Recommended course for all teaching assistants.

subject: MUS
title: Group Studies
description: Critical review of research in selected problems of musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

subject: MUS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual tutorial for research in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance; instructor will usually be student's major professor.

subject: MUS
title: Individual Study for Master's Comprehensive and Doctoral Qualifying Exam- inations for Advancement to Candidacy
description: Individual study for master's comprehensive and doctoral qualifying examinations for advancement to candidacy.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor and graduate advisor.

subject: MUS
title: Preparation for Master's Degree
description: Instructor will be chair of student's committee in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

subject: MUS
title: Ph.D. Dissertation Research and Preparation
description: Instructor will ordinarily be chair of student's doctoral committee.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

subject: MUS
title: Preparation for Doctor of Musical Arts Post-Candidacy Recitals
description: Preparation of two full-length recitals (conducting: the equivalent of two full-length concerts) required after advancement to candidacy for the dma degree. Instructor should be student's performance instructor: ordinarily chair of DMA committee.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

subject: MUS
title: Preparation of DMA Document
description: Preparation of the DMA document required after advancement to candidacy for the DMA degree. Instructor should be a member of student's doctoral committee.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

subject: PHIL
title: Short Introduction to Philosophy
description: An introductory course in western philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Critical Thinking
description: Practical reasoning, argumentation, and the analysis of language as instruments of sound thinking in everyday life.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Ethics
description: An examination, at an introductory level, of such ethical issues as: why bemoral, moral relativism, the nature of virtues and vices; and possibly consideration of practical ethical problems such as abortion or war.

subject: PHIL
title: Biomedical Ethics
description: An examination of philosophical thinking about moral issues raised by the practice of medicine. Traditional ethical theories and problems will serve as background to, and in turn be illuminated by, such issues as informed consent, paternalism, abortion, euthanasia, and genetic engineering.

subject: PHIL
title: History of Philosophy
description: From Thales to Aristotle.

subject: PHIL
title: History of Philosophy
description: From Medievals to Rationalists.

subject: PHIL
title: History of Philosophy
description: From the Empiricists to Kant.

subject: PHIL
title: Ethics
description: An examination of the fundamental concepts, theories, and problems of moral or political philosophy.
prereq_text: One prior course in philosophy; or, Philosphy 3 (may be taken concurrently)
prereq_gold: PHIL * with a minimum grade of P [may be concurrent] or PHIL * [may be concurrent] or PHIL 3 [may be concurrent]

subject: PHIL
title: Theory of Knowledge
description: Investigates fundamental questions surrounding the nature of human knowledge and human justification, such as: What do I know? What am I justified in believing? What is it to know something? What is it to hold a justified belief?

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Language
description: Introduction to philosophical problems and theories concerning the nature of language. Topics typically include the notion of linguistic structure, theories of meaning and reference, names and descriptions, the relations between languages and thought, necessity and analytic truty, and conversational norms.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Mind
description: Discussion of some central questions about the mind: are people identical to their bodies? What is it to feel, believe, or desire something? What distinguishes intelligent thinking from a computer's activities? What is the connection between language and thought?

subject: PHIL
title: Metaphysics
description: Introduction to the philosophical study of the most general and fundamental features of reality. Topics vary, but may include universals, particulars, identity and individuation, substance, the nature of persons, causation, and the nature of time.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Science
description: An introduction to the philosophical analysis of the concepts and methods of science, treating such topics as: explanation, confirmation, causation, scientific laws, the interpretation, meaning and reference of scientific theories, theory reduction and theory change, and scientific revolutions.
prereq_text: One prior course in philosophy; or major in physics, chemistry, or biology.

subject: PHIL
title: Meaning and Reference
description: An examination of the classical theories of meaning and reference: John Stuart Mill, Gottlob Frege, Bertrand Russell, and the theory of direct reference. Investigation of solutions to the classical puzzles of meaning and reference.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
description: Advances in artificial intelligence and the widespread use of computers in society confront us with many interesting philosophical questions. What is computation? Is AI really intelligence? Could computers ever think or feel? Is the Turing test a good test? Are we really computers? Are there decisions computers should never make? Do computers threaten our privacy in special ways? Should AI be regulated, and how? We will survey some of the controversies and puzzles that AI has provoked.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
prereq_text: A course from PHIL 100A-F, or two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Political Philosophy
description: Analysis of fundamental political conceptions; the state, sovereignty, political obligation, natural rights, natural law, etc.
prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Science
description: What is science? How does it differ from non-science? Course examines both the history of science and the history of philosophy of science in an effort to discover just what science is and what it has to offer.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Space and Time
description: Is space a thing or a series of relations holding between objects? Does time pass differently for different observers, or in different parts of the universe? Consideration of these and other questions lead to an examination of contemporary physics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Biology
description: The biological sciences are distinctively different from the physical sciences. This course will focus on philosophical topics central to biology, such as evolutionary theory and its implications, the proper understanding of concepts such as function, fitness, selection, gene, or the nature of organisms and species.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophical Foundations of Cognitive Science
description: What is the mind and how can we model it? Cognitive science offers a distinctive approach to fundamental philosophical questions about the mind. This course begins with the classical foundations of cognitive science and surveys recent developments in the field, including neural networks, theories of embodiment, dynamical systems, and recent statistical approaches to cognition and artificial intelligence.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy and Neuroscience
description: The brain is the seat of who we are. This course will focus on topics at the intersection of philosophy and the brain sciences, such as neuroethics, philosophy of neuroscience, representation in the brain, or philosophical and scientific theories of consciousness.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL
title: Animal Minds
description: The goal of this course is to examine current research in animal cognition with a view to understanding how philosophical and scientific questions about animal minds interact. Topics may include whether nonhuman animals can feel pain; whether they can suffer; whether they have episodic memory; whether they are conscious. We will also consider ethical implications of the answers we find to the above questions.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit up to 8 units with consent of instructor.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100D, or two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Social Philosophy
description: This course will examine moral problems associated with economic activity; for example, economic justice and the moral basis of property rights.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Gender
description: Philosophical issues involving the concept of gender. Topics may include the distinction between sex and gender, gender and sexuality, theories of gender, gender identity and expression, non-binary and queer genders, and gender subordination and oppression.
prereq_text: One course from PHIL 100A-F and one additional course in Philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Feminist Philosophy
description: In this course, we examine philosophical approaches to feminism and feminist issues. Topics covered may include inequality in the workplace and in family structures; global feminism; objectification; pornography; and prostitution.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Freedom and Determinism
description: Determinism is the doctrine that the laws of nature plus the past necessitate the future. Is determinism compatible with the view that we often act freely and are often morally responsible for what we do?
prereq_text: Prerequisite: one prior course in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in Applied Ethics.
description: Advanced topics in applied ethics, such as the ethics of war; the ethics of procreation; and the ethics of how we treat animals.
advisor_comments: May be repeated with consent of department provided course content is different.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: History of Political Thought
description: A study of one or more important figures from the history of political thought.
prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.

subject: PHIL
title: Moral Psychology
description: An examination of the nature of desires, emotions, the imagination and other aspects of human psychology, and of the ways these bear on the moral evaluation of people and actions.
prereq_text: Philosophy 4 or 100A; and, Philosophy 100B or 100C or 100D or 100E.

subject: PHIL
title: Contemporary Philosophy
description: Systematic investigation of topics drawn from contemporary analytic or continental philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in Feminist Philosophy
description: Focuses on advanced topics in feminist philosophy, sometimes covering one topic or one author over the course. Content will vary but may include contemporary debates, such as gender, pornography, consent, single authors such as Wollstonecraft, or de Beauvoir, and themes, such as early feminist thinkers, or feminist epistemology.

subject: PHIL
title: Normative Ethics
description: An examination of what makes actions morally right or wrong and people morally good or bad.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Meta-Ethics
description: An examination of problems concerning the meaning and justification of moral judgments.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: History of Ethics
description: A study of one or more historically important moral philosophers.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Philosophy 100A; or, two prior courses in philosophy.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Law
description: An introduction to some of the main issues generated by the philosophical question, "What is law?" In what sense is conduct made obligatory by the existence of law? What, if any, is the relationship between law and morals? What are rules? What does it mean to say that a rule exists? Do courts really apply rules or merely pretend to do so?

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in the Philosophy of Law
description: Study of advanced topics in the philosophy of law.
prereq_text: Major in philosophy, law & society, political science, or global and international studies.

subject: PHIL
title: Punishment and Responsibility
description: An examination of some of the philosophical problems of punishment and responsibility: The rationale of punishment and the legal doctrine of Mensrea; the analysis of conditions of responsibility, relations between punishment, responsibility, retribution, guilt, shame, etc.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy in Literature
description: Introduction to major problems at the intersection of philosophy and literature. Issues addressed may include philosophical assessments of literature, authorship and interpretation, truth in fiction, significance of literary works and form for philosophy; texts include imaginative literature and philosophical essays.

subject: PHIL
title: Action Theory

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
description: Advances in artificial intelligence and the widespread use of computers in society confront us with many interesting philosophical questions. What is computation? Is AI really intelligence? Could computers ever think or feel? Is the Turing test a good test? Are we really computers? Are there decisions computers should never make? Do computers threaten our privacy in special ways? Should AI be regulated, and how? We will survey some of the controversies and puzzles that AI has provoked.

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

This course will focus on philosophical topics central to biology, such as evolutionary theory and its implications, the proper understanding of concepts such as function, fitness, selection, gene, or the nature of organisms and species.

subject: PHIL

description: What is the mind and how can we model it? Cognitive science offers a distinctive approach to fundamental philosophical questions about the mind. This course begins with the classical foundations of cognitive science and surveys recent developments in the field, including neural networks, theories of embodiment, dynamical systems, and recent statistical approaches to cognition and artificial intelligence.

Topics may include whether nonhuman animals can feel pain; whether they can suffer; whether they have episodic memory; whether they are conscious. We will also consider ethical implications of the answers we find to the above questions.

The project of understanding the mind requires tools drawn from fields that include psychology, computer science, philosophy, linguistics, anthropology, behavioral economics, neuroscience, and even the arts. This course is designed for graduate students from all disciplines wishing to understand the fundamentals of cognitive science. It will introduce you to the major tools and theories from these areas as they relate to the study of the mind. This course is the core requirement of the UCSB graduate emphasis in cognitive science, and It serves as a foundation for continued study in the cognitive sciences.

It orients students towards success in the Ph.D. program milestones: the qualifying paper, prospectus development, and completion of the dissertation. It also imparts skills that go beyond graduation, such as preparing a CV, crafting a syllabus, delivering research talks, and writing proposals for grants and fellowships. In the course of covering these topics, the class will also provide a forum for students to reflect on issues in academia more broadly. These include pedagogical innovation, work/life balance, the current state of the discipline, the purposes of the university, and how best to support our diverse undergraduate population.
