advisor_comments: Physics 3L is the same course as Physics 7L.
repeat_comments: Physics 7L can be taken as a legal repeat of Physics 3L.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.
advisor_comments: This course is highly recommended for those students who have not completed AP calculus BC with a score of 5.
repeat_comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 1 or 21.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors Introduction to Experimental Physics
description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, what conclusions can be reached, etc.
advisor_comments: Quarters usually offered: Fall. Same course as Physics CS 15A. Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 3L, Physics 13AH or Physics CS 15A.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors Experimental Physics
description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.
advisor_comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 4L, Physics 13BH or Physics CS 15B.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors Experimental Physics
description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.
advisor_comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 5L, Physics 13CH or Physics CS 15C.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Physics
description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation. Basic good practices in note-taking, data collection, data visualization, error estimation, error propagation, curve fitting, and drawing conclusions, all exercised in the context of phenomena from mechanics and electronics.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3L, Physics 13AH, Physics 13AL or Physics CS 15A.
prereq_text: Physics 29 and Physics 23 (may be taken concurrently)
prereq_gold: PHYS 2 or PHYS 22; PHYS 3 [may be concurrent] or PHYS 23 [may be concurrent]

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Physics
description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, continued. Basics of image analysis, technical drawing, additive manufacturing, oscilloscope use, searching and digesting scientific literature, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL in the context of electromagnetic and optical phenomena.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 4L, Physics 13BH, Physics 13BL or Physics CS 15B.
prereq_text: Physics 20AL and Physics 24 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Physics
description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, with an emphasis on Scientific Communication and Experimental Design. Searching the scientific literature, reading a scientific paper, proposing and executing a measurement, and formally reporting on a measurement in writing, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL and 20BL in the context of modern physics phenomena.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 5L, Physics 13CH, Physics 13CL, Physics 25L or Physics CS 15C.
prereq_text: Physics 20BL and Physics 25 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.
repeat_comments: Not open for degree credit to students who have completed Physics 1.
prereq_text: Mathematics 2A/3A and Mathematics 2B/3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam score of 5.
prereq_gold: MATH 2A or MATH 3A or PHYS 8 or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5; MATH 2B or MATH 3B or PHYS 8 or AP Calc BC ≥ 5 or IB M ≥ 5 or IB M4 ≥ 5

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Rotational dynamics, fluid mechanics, gravitation, periodic motion, temperature and heat, thermodynamics.
repeat_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 2.
prereq_text: Physics 21 with a grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Mechanical waves, sound, electric charge and electric field, Gauss Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3.
repeat_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 3.
prereq_text: Physics 22 with a minimum grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 4.
prereq_text: Physics 23 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4A.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Physics 5.
prereq_text: Physics 24 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6A.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Computer Programming for the Physical Sciences
description: An introduction to programming and data analysis for the physical sciences. Topics include syntax, goodcoding practice, basic algorithmic structure, plotting, basic data analysis, numerical root-finding and integration.
prereq_text: Mathematics 2B or 3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5
prereq_gold: MATH 2B or MATH 3B or PHYS 8 or AP Calc BC ≥ 5

subject: PHYS
title: Readings in Physics
description: Critical reviews and discussions of selected physics subjects, conducted under the supervision of a Physics faculty member.
advisor_comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students must have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and are limited to 3 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Physics Research
description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a Physics faculty member. Topic and scope varies, to be specified by student and supervisory faculty member prior to registration.
advisor_comments: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 units. Students must have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and are limited to 3 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.

subject: PHYS
title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Linear Algebra: Vector spaces, operators, spectral decomposition. Topics may include Sturm-Liouville equations, special functions. Fourier series and Fourier transforms, Dirac delta-function.
repeat_comments: Students who completed PHYS 102 with a C- or below may take PHYS 100A as a legal repeat
prereq_text: Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Analytic functions, contour integrals and branch cuts. Conformal mapping. Laplace transforms. Asymptotic series and the gamma function. Greens functions.
repeat_comments: Students who completed PHYS 101 with a C- or below may take PHYS 100B as a legal repeat
prereq_text: Mathematics 5C or 6B with a grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.
prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)
prereq_gold: PHYS 2 or PHYS 22; MATH 6A [may be concurrent]

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Mechanics
description: Calculus of variations. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics. Central force problems and collision theory. Non-inertial reference frames. Coupled oscillations and waves.
prereq_text: Physics 103 with a grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: Nonlinear Phenomena
description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.
advisor_comments: Same course as ME 169 and Physics 106. Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 163C.
repeat_comments: PHYS 103 was formerly PHYS 105A.
prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetism
description: Electrostatics, Laplace's equation, method of images, separation of variables, multipole expansion, magnetostatics, electric and magnetic fields in matter.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6B with minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetism
description: Electrodynamics, Maxwells equations, conservation laws, electromagnetic waves, potentials and fields for moving charges, radiation, special relativity.
prereq_text: Physics 110A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: The postulates of quantum mechanics, the Schrdinger equation and its consequences, the quantum harmonic oscillator and other one dimensional quantum systems, Hilbert Space and Dirac notation, the hydrogen atom.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 and Physics 100A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Spin and angular momentum, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, identical particles, symmetries and conservation laws, time independent perturbation theory.
prereq_text: Physics 115A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: The variational principle, time dependent perturbation theory, the adiabatic theorem. Topics from: WKB approximation, the Dirac equation, Berrys phase, Bells inequality, quantum cryptography, quantum computation.
prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Group Theory for Physicists
description: The emphasis is on developing some intuition about the role of symmetries in physics, rather than going through rigorous mathematical proofs. Theorems will be proved at the level of rigor customary among physicists.

subject: PHYS
title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
description: Principles of statistical physics, entropy, large numbers, thermodynamic principles, microcanonical ensemble, ideal gas, free energy, chemical potential, selected applications. Canonical ensemble, if time permits.
prereq_text: PHYS 22 and MATH 6B with a minimum grade of C-

subject: PHYS
title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
description: Canonical ensemble and partition functions, grand canonical ensemble, quantum statistics, Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein distribution laws. Topics from: Brownian motion, Langevin equation, dissipation and fluctuations, elementary kinetic theory, weakly interacting gases or mean field theory of magnetism, other topics illustrative of the breadth of the subject and/or selected applications.
prereq_text: Physics 115A and Physics 119A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics of California Waves, Weather, Quakes and Fires
description: Why do the waves hit the beach every five seconds? This course teaches students the relevant fluid dynamics and allows them to apply it to natural phenomena of California: seismic waves, tsunamis, maximum tree heights, fluid flow around fish.

subject: PHYS
title: Condensed Matter Physics
description: Classification of solids; crystal symmetry; thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators; band theory of electronic states; wave scattering by crystals; semiconductor devices.
prereq_text: Physics 115A with at least a C- or better, and upper-division standing.

subject: PHYS
title: Condensed Matter Physics
description: Tight binding model, topological insulator, magnetism, phase transition, introduction to superconductivity.
prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Elementary Particle Physics
description: Introduction to quarks and leptons and the phenomenology of the particles they comprise; fundamental symmetries, invariance principles, and the associated quantum numbers, strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions and their relationship.

subject: PHYS
title: Laboratory Optics
description: An introduction to optical phenomena and the methods and instrumentation used to generate, measure, and manipulate light. Experiments will cover imaging and aberrations, coherence, diffraction, interference, interferometry, Fourier optics, reflection and polarization, spectroscopy, lasers, fiber optics, and optical instruments.
prereq_text: Physics 141 with a grade of C- or better, Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.

subject: PHYS
title: Analog Electronics
description: Passive circuits, diodes, transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers, feedback and control. Design, building and testing of analog circuits.
prereq_text: Physics 13CL or 20CL and Math 3B with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Digital Electronics
description: Gates, combinational and sequential logic, ?multiplexers, counters, shift registers, memory and microprocessors. Design, building and testing of digital circuitry, including a modern microprocessor based computer system.
prereq_text: Physics 127AL with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Experimental Physics
description: Selected experiments in physics, i.e. saturated absorption spectroscopy, muon lifetime measurements, pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance, Mossbauer effect. Develop skills in detailing observations in a scientific notebook, data collection and error analysis, operating complex physical apparatus, and scientific communication.
prereq_text: Physics 13CL or Physics 20CL or Physics CS 15C. Physics 115A (may be taken concurrently).
prereq_gold: PHYS 13CL or PHYS 20CL or PHYS CS 15C; PHYS 115A [may be concurrent]

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Scientific Computation
description: A survey of computers, programming, and computational techniques for the natural sciences. Physical foundations of computation, binary arithmetic, computer architecture, programming languages, operating systems, UNIX shell and filesystems. Programming tools, variables and data structures, expressions, control flow, files, functions and scoping, objects, error handling, debugging, graphics, text processing, networking, data acquisition and transfer. Mathematics and algorithms for data processing and analysis, numerical methods, random numbers and simulation.
advisor_comments: Not open to graduate students.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better; Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better.
prereq_gold: (PHYS 5 and MATH 6B and PHYS 29) or (PHYS 25 and MATH 6B and PHYS 29)

subject: PHYS
title: Gravitation and Relativity
description: An introduction to Einstein's general relativity, the spacetime of special relativity, the principle of equivalence, gravity as geometry, the description of spacetime geometry, the spacetime of a relativistic star, solar system test of general relativity, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology.
advisor_comments: Physics 104 may be taken concurrently with consent of instructor
prereq_text: Physics 103-104 with a minimum grade of C- in each.

subject: PHYS
title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
description: Observed properties and classification of stars, the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, stellar atmospheres, hydrostatic equilibrium, energy transport, equations of state, thermonuclear reaction rates, origin of the elements, life history of stars, stellar death, compact objects, star formation.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Cosmology
description: The geometry, contents and evolution of the universe as a whole. The empirical and theoretical foundations for the Big Bang, the Hubble expansion, Friedmann models, dark matter, dark energy, the thermal history of the universe, the origin of the light elements, the cosmic microwave background, reionization, and structure formation.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Observational Astrophysics
description: Techniques and implementation of observational methods in astronomy/astrophysics. Sensors, digital-image processing and analysis, research projects with computer-controlled remote access telescope using a digital image sensor. Studies of variable stars, galaxy morphology, supernovae, etc.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).
advisor_comments: Same course as Materials 135.

subject: PHYS
title: Galaxies
description: The distribution of mass in galaxies, orbits of stars, Boltzmann equation, Jeans theorem, spiral structure & density waves, dynamics of star clusters, galaxy collisions, dynamical friction, gas dynamics, sound & shock waves, gas inflow & accretion, gas outflow & winds.
prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)

subject: PHYS
title: Planets and Exoplanets
description: An introduction to planets both in and out of the solar system. This course will provide a broad overview of planets in the solar system, the techniques used to detect planets outside the solar system, and demographics and characteristics of exoplanets.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)
prereq_gold: PHYS 5 or PHYS 25 or PHYS 115A; PHYS 104 [may be concurrent]

subject: PHYS
title: Soft Matter Physics
description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Biology of the Cell
description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.

subject: PHYS
title: Optics
description: Modern geometrical and physical optics. Polarization, coherence, interference, and diffraction phenomena. Fourier transform spectroscopy, intensity correlation interferometry, spatial filtering, and holography. Selected topics on lasers, light scattering, and quantum optics as time permits.
prereq_text: Physics 110B with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Research in Condensed Matter Physics
description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in research laboratories in condensed matter physics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Research in Elementary Particle Physics
description: Offers qualified under graduates the opportunity to work in experimental research in elementary particle physics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25; and consent of instructor.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Research in Biophysics
description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in research laboratories in biophysics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: PHYS
title: Experimental Research in Astrophysics
description: Offers qualified undergraduates the opportunity to work in experimental research in astrophysics. Each staff member has his/her own course identified by a number listed in the schedule of classes.
prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25; and consent of instructor.

subject: PHYS
title: Special Topics in Physics
description: Course varies from year to year according to the current interests.

subject: PHYS
title: Science for the Public
description: Provides experience in communicating science and technology to nonspecialists. The major components of the course are field work in mentoring, a biweekly seminar, presentations to precollege students and to adult nonscientists, and end-of-term research papers.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 12 units, but only 4 units may be applied to the major. Same course as Engineering 160. Open to graduate students in science and engineering disciplines and to undergraduate science and engineering majors.

subject: PHYS
title: Teaching and Learning Physics
description: Introduction to basic concepts in education literature and learning theory. The course involves readings of articles and text drawn from general and Physics education research and cognitive science. Students will engage in discussions and reflective activities that apply and relate the ideas from the readings to their own classroom experiences to help them become more effective teachers and learners.
advisor_comments: Required for Physics Education Concentration

subject: PHYS
title: Atomic Physics
description: An introduction to atomic physics. Covers basic atomic structure of one and two valence electron atoms, the Zeeman effect, and the semiclassical treatment of atoms interacting with near-resonant light. We also discuss laser cooling and trapping, as well as selected advanced topics such as atomic clocks, trapped ion dynamics, and the application of atoms in quantum information science.

subject: PHYS
title: Directed Reading
description: Each staff member has own directed reading course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Research in Physics
description: Directed individual study open to qualified seniors in the department. Each staff member has own independent studies course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined in the major.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Independent Research Assistance
description: Undergraduate research for qualified seniors to gain valuable experience in research methodology.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in 98/99/198/199/199DC/199RA courses combined. No more than 12 units may be earned in all Physics 198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Classical Mechanics
description: Review of lagrangian mechanics. Variational principles. Hamilton's equations. Canonical transformations. Hamilton Jacobi theory. Action angle variables. Time dependent and canonical perturbation theory. Central forcesand scattering. Small vibrations. Rigid body motion. Poincare maps. Non-integrable systems. Hamiltonian and dissipative chaos.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Theory
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary value problems, time varying fields, Maxwell's equations, radiation, multipole fields, scattering, relativistic particle dynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Theory
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary value problems, time varying fields, Maxwell's equations, radiation, multipole fields, scattering, relativistic particle dynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Fundamental principles; Schroedinger equation; angular momentum; perturbation theory; scattering theory, emission, and absorption of radiation; Dirac equation.

subject: PHYS
title: The Many Body Problem in Condensed Matter Physics
description: Field theoretic methods as applied to (non-relativistic) condensed matter systems. Green's functions and diagrammatic techniques applied to various examples of interacting many body systems, including fermions, bosons, and spins. Relationship of theoretical quantities to physical measurements.

subject: PHYS
title: The Many Body Problem in Condensed Matter Physics
description: Field theoretic methods as applied to (non-relativistic) condensed matter systems. Green's functions and diagrammatic techniques applied to various examples of interacting many body systems, including fermions, bosons, and spins. Relationship of theoretical quantities to physical measurements.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Mechanics
description: Fundamental principles of classical and quantum statistics. Non-interacting Boltzmann, Bose, and Fermi systems. Virial expansion and other approaches to interacting systems. Phase transitions.
prereq_text: Physics 205, 215A, and 119B or equivalent taken at another institution.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
description: Course will cover some of the following topics: A) critical phenomena-phase diagrams, first and second order phase transitions, scalingtheory, high-temperature expansions, renormalization group; B) nonequilibrium statistical mechanics-stochastic processes. Langevin equations, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, master equations, fluid dynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.
prereq_text: Physics 205, Physics 210A, Physics 210B, Physics 215A, Physics 215B, and Physics 215C; or consent of instructor.

subject: PHYS
title: Relativistic Quantum Field Theory
description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.

subject: PHYS

description: Introduction to the theory of Lorentz covariant quantized fields. Global and local conservation laws. Path integral formulation. Applications to quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and electroweak interactions. Other possible topics include grand unification, the renormalization group, anomolies, current algebra and supersymmetry.

subject: PHYS
title: Concepts and Phenomena of Condensed Matter Physics
description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

subject: PHYS
title: Concepts and Phenomena of Condensed Matter Physics
description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

description: Lattice and electron dynamics. Elementary excitations and collective phenomena. Transport properties. Disorder and localization. Long-range order and broken symmetries. Magnetism, superconductivity and liquid crystals. Properties and structures of polymers, membranes, and self-assembling systems.

subject: PHYS
title: Elementary Particle Physics
description: The phenomenology of the standard model of particle physics. QED and QCD process.

subject: PHYS
title: Elementary Particle Physics
description: Weak interactions; neutrino physics; C, P, and CP violation; electroweak gauge theory and symmetry breaking. Design of detectors and experiments; searches for new phenomena.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Techniques in Particle Physics
description: Bayesian and Frequentist approaches. Probability distributions used in particle physics. Hypothesis testing. Data fitting. Limit extractions. Confidence/credible intervals. Monte Carlo methods. Applications to realistic problems from current research.
prereq_text: None for graduate students. Consent of the instructor for undergraduates students.

subject: PHYS
title: Atomic and Molecular Physics
description: A survey of major topics in modern atomic physics. Topics in atomic structure include general features of atomic spectra, fine structure, hyperfine structure, the Lamb shift, hydrogen, helium, alkali atoms, complex atoms, excited states, and synthetic atoms. Topics in atom-field interactions and atom atom interactions include the DC Stark effect, the Zeeman effect, transitions, two-level systems, stimulated and spontaneous emission, selection rules, lifetimes, line shapes, broadening mechanisms, the AC Stark effect, multiphoton processes, scattering channels, and Feshbach resonances. Also coversmodern techniques including spectroscopy, laser cooling, atom traps, quantum gases, cold molecules, trapped ions, and atomic clocks.
prereq_text: Physics 215A and Phys 210A; or the consent of the instructor.

subject: PHYS
title: Gauge Theories of Elementary Particles
description: Quantum theory of non-abelian gauge fields. Local, global, and spontaneous symmetry breaking. Collective phenomena; solitons, instantons, and magnetic monopoles. Effective field theories. Lattice gauge theory. applications to the standard model of elementary particles.

subject: PHYS
title: Gauge Theories of Elementary Particles
description: Quantum theory of non-abelian gauge fields. Local, global, and spontaneous symmetry breaking. Collective phenomena; solitons, instantons, and magnetic monopoles. Effective field theories. Lattice gauge theory. Applications to the standard model of elementary particles.

subject: PHYS
title: String Theory
description: Introduction to string theory. Bosonic and super string theories and their spectra. String perturbation theory and conformal field theory. Nonlinear sigma models and spacetime structure. String compactifications and unification of forces. Non-perturbative results and methods; dualities and branes.

subject: PHYS
title: String Theory
description: Introduction to string theory. Bosonic and super string theories and their spectra. String perturbation theory and conformal field theory. Nonlinear sigma models and spacetime structure. String compactifications and unification of forces. Non-perturbative results and methods; dualities and branes.

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity
description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity
description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity
description: Gravity as geometry, differential geometry, Einstein's equation, relativistic stars, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology, gravitational radiation, and special topics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated with consent of instructor.

subject: PHYS
title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
description: Physics of stellar structure, equations of state and heat transport. Birth of stars and physics of brown dwarfs. Thermonuclear burning and main sequence stellar structure. Evolution of stars and mass loss. Origin, physical structure, and cooling of compact objects.

subject: PHYS
title: The Interstellar Medium
description: Physical processes that regulate the state of diffuse gas in and around galaxies: Ionization and thermal equilibrium; absorption line studies; spectral line formation; properties of dust grains and extinction; molecular gas and star formation; supernova explosions and hydrodynamic shocks.

subject: PHYS
title: High Energy Astrophysics
description: Accretion power in a range of astrophysical contexts, from quasars to galactic black holes. Rapid release of thermonuclear energy, Type I X-ray bursts, classical novae, Type Ia supernovae. Relativistic jets from black holes, non-thermal radiation processes, physics of gamma-ray bursts.

subject: PHYS
title: Extragalactic Astrophysics
description: Nebular astrophysics, active galactic nuclei, supermassive black holes, galaxies, clusters, dark matter, gravitational lensing, the intergalactic medium and galaxy formation.

subject: PHYS
title: Cosmology
description: Friedmann models, distance measures, cosmological parameters, thermal history of the universe, cosmological density fields, structure formation (top-hat model, Press-Schechter), big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background.

subject: PHYS
title: Galactic Dynamics
description: Stellar dynamics, Jeans equations, potential theory, orbit theory, linear stability analysis, kinetic theory, dynamical friction, applications to star clusters, galaxy morphology and mergers.

subject: PHYS
title: Soft Matter Physics
description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered will include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.
advisor_comments: IQB 238 and Physics 238 are the same course.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Biology of the Cell
description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.
advisor_comments: PHYS 239 and IQB 239 are the same course.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistics, Data Analysis, and Machine Learning for Physicists
description: A survey of statistical and machine learning techniques as applied in modern physics research, with extensive applications to real data. Some of the topics covered include Bayesian and frequentist approaches to statistics; formulating and integrating likelihood functions; confidence intervals with and without assumptions of Gaussianity; Markov Chain Monte Carlo; principal component analysis and dimensionality reduction; Gaussian process regression; and time series analysis. Assignments will make use of published research and data sets, and will require the application of analysis techniques covered in class.

subject: PHYS
title: Special Topics in Physics
description: The course varies from year to year according to current interests.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated with a different topic.

subject: PHYS
title: Colloquium
description: Colloquium.

subject: PHYS
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Weekly seminar on topics of research currently being pursued in the department of physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics Outreach
description: Active participation in an outreach program that presents physics demonstrations and experiments on the road to local schools in order to provide a valuable learning experience for K-12 students.

subject: PHYS
title: Teaching Assistant Seminar
description: Covers development of teaching techniques especially oriented to lower-division physics laboratory instruction. Theoretical aspects covered at beginning of each quarter. Practical techniques discussed including weekly meeting with class instructor, formal evaluation, and videotaping analysis.
advisor_comments: No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees. Required course for all teaching assistants.

title: Special Topics
description: Special seminar on research subjects of current interest. Each staff memberhas a seminar identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

title: Group Studies

subject: PHYS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual tutorial. Reading and research in special topics including work done as the basis for the dissertation. Each staff member has a directed reading and research course identified by a number code listed in the schedule of classes.

subject: PHYS
title: Dissertation Preparation
description: This course is reserved for writing the dissertation. Each staff member has a research course identified by a number code listed in the schedule ofclasses.

subject: POL S
title: Introduction to Political Philosophy
description: An introduction to central texts and problems of political philosophy with an emphasis on such concepts as liberty, equality, authority, justice, and obligation.

subject: POL S
title: Causal Inference in Political Science
description: This course is about what quantitative political scientists do when they can’t do experiments. You will learn more about when and how political scientists make causal statements about observational data. We will start by reviewing the promise and pitfalls of experiments as a tool for political scientists. Then, we will think about a series of other approaches that political scientists use to tease apart cause and effect in their work.
advisor_comments: POLS 106CI was replaced by POLS 103, and is the same course.
repeat_comments: Students can repeat this course with a repeatable grade from POLS 106CI, since POLS 103 replaces POLS 106CI.

prereq_gold: POL S 15 or (COMM 87 and COMM 88) or (PSTAT 5A and COMM 88)

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: American Political Development
description: This reading-intensive course examines the evolution of American political institutions, policies, and ideas. It will consider the interplay between constitutional design, social movements, economic forces, and cultural shifts, from the colonial period to the present.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: American Indian Politics
description: American Indian tribes play a significant role in the contemporary American political system. This is true at the national, state, and local levels. From a historical perspective, interactions between tribes and settler governments also shaped many of the governing institutions in the United States. This class examines the influence of American Indian tribes and their evolving relationship with federal and state governments. Issues and concepts covered include colonization, economic development, resource and environment, tribal sovereignty, assimilation, stereotypes, and American political development. This class is both focused on historical change and contemporary issues.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics: African American Politics
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: American Social Movements
description: Designed to teach students on the social origins and political impact of American social movements on the left and right. We explore the individual, social psychological, and institutional dynamics of movements.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Black Political Thought
description: Takes as a point of departure the push for equality among the Black community in the Black community. It surveys the various strategies and approaches undertaken by Black thought leaders toward that end.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Climate Change and Conflict
description: In this course we will learn about how climate change creates conflict around the globe. We will focus on conflict within civil wars and other forms of intrastate violence. Climate change is the single most important long-term threat to the peace and stability of the planet. The conflicts of the sort we look at in this class may be the most important short-term threat. Are they linked? If so, how? By the end of this class, you will be prepared to answer these questions. We will begin by looking the idea of climate change itself, to make sure we understand what exactly that concept means. Next, we will overview conflict and its causes. After that, we will analyze the debates in the academic literature about climate conflict linkages.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science: Causal Inference
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Climate Change Law
description: Examines the legal frameworks and policies that shape the fight against climate change. It examines key international agreements, federal and state regulations, and economic instruments designed to address climate change. The course also addresses the legal tensions between environmental goals and economic interests, as well as the challenges of enforcing climate change regulations at different levels of government. Through case studies and discussions, students will develop a deeper understanding of how legal systems are adapting to the evolving climate crisis and the role of law in promoting effective and equitable climate protection.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Legislative Politics - US Congress
description: This course will examine the nomination and election of congressmen, constituent relationships, the development of the institution, formal and informal structures, leadership, comparisons of House with Senate, lobbying, and relationship with the executive branch.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: International Relations in Culture
description: Explores cultural explanations of international relations with a particular focus on how pop culture contributes to the outbreak of violence. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of how culture and politics interacts, and apply these ideas to current politics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics: Democracy and Inequality
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Northeast Asian Politics
description: Consider the possibility of an Asian Century and the role that Northeast Asia might play in making that possible, or alternatively in hindering it. The course material and lectures will provide the advanced undergraduate with an introduction to the postwar political and economic developments and regional interrelationships between the major countries of Northeast Asia: China, North Korea, South Korea and Japan.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Climate Politics and Justice
description: How do political issues shape environmental quality in the Global South? Why have some governments been more successful in reducing environmental degradation than others? How do climate change and other forms of environmental degradation impact local communities? In this course, we explore the causes and impacts of environmental degradation, with emphasis on their unequal distribution across and within countries. We also analyze the political obstacles and opportunities to implement successful and equitable environmental policies. Topics include the energy transition, air and water pollution, land use and deforestation, the impact of extractive industries, and environmental justice.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Political Economy of the Energy Transition
description: Using a comparative analysis, the course examines the political economy of the transition to new forms of energy across the world.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Global Indigenous Politics
description: This course explores the contemporary politics of Indigenous Peoples and settler societies. It takes a sociological, legal, political, and anthropological approach to how politics operate within and around Indigenous Peoples. By adopting a comparative and international perspective, it examines the dynamics of critical relationships within the context of national, regional, and global political orders. We look at “standard” settler states often referred to as “neo-Britains,” such as the United States, Canada, New Zealand, and Australia, but also Indigenous Peoples and issues from Europe, Asia, and South America.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science: Gender Rights and Politics
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics: International Law and Human Rights
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Latinx American Political Development
description: This course examines the role of Latinx communities in shaping local, state, and national politics in the United States. It reviews contemporary modes of Latinx political organizing; examines the development of heterogeneous political ideologies among the prevalent subgroups; analyzes public policy issues surrounding citizenship and membership; evaluates the achievements and shortcomings of Latinx empowerment strategies; and it considers the electoral impact of Latinx voting outcomes.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science: Nuclear Security
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific course titles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: The Politics of the Biosphere: Ecosystem Conservation, Power, and Land
description: Forests and other ecosystems are crucial for societal and environmental reasons; nonetheless, they face significant threats across the world. This class explores the economic and political drivers of ecosystem degradation, the solutions that governments and non-governmental actors have implemented to address the issue, and the challenges to their success. Other topics include territorial and political rights of local communities, common-pool resources management, impact evaluation of anti-deforestation policies, and land reforms, among others.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Special Topics in Political Science: Psychology in International Relations
description: Lectures in special areas of interest in political science. Specific coursetitles to be announced by the department each quarter offered.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Qualitative Methods & Research Design
description: Introductory, module-based course on political science research design and qualitative methods of inquiry, including participant observation, interview methods, and case studies. Students pursue a topic of their choice deploying each technique to study it. Ideal for students contemplating an honors thesis or graduate school. The course begins by providing students with an introduction to the tools and techniques, strengths and limitations of various qualitative methods. It explores how to craft research designs to provide the greatest explanatory leverage and how to communicate most effectively with your intended audience.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Regionalism
description: Analysis and comparison of regional integration and cooperation across different parts of the world, with a focus on domestic and international economic institutions.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Violence
description: Why do societies turn on themselves? Violence, from homicide to civil wars and insurgencies to terrorism and political assassinations to genocide to state repression, shapes societies around the world, and no region is immune, from established democracies to fragile states. This course draws on case studies from across the globe, including both developed and developing nations, to explore three key questions: What forms does violence take? What factors drive it? And how can societies build resilience against it? Students leave with a comparative, global understanding of one of the most pressing challenges facing societies today.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Politics and Literature
description: This course will explore problems concerning alienation, obligation, power,freedom, and fulfillment as treated by ancient and modern authors.

subject: POL S
title: Political Concepts
description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Political Concepts: Critical Theory & Marxism
description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Political Concepts: Civil Disobedience
description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Political Concepts: Defense Against the Political Dark Arts
description: An exploration of themes in political theory concerned with sinister social forces that undermine good politics - and how to fight back against them. Topics include political manipulation, misinformation, charismatic leadership and rhetoric.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Political Concepts: Environmental Political Theory
description: Introduction to some of the main concepts of political theory, such as the individual and the state, freedom and equality, political obligation, and their relevance to modern society and government.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Democracy and Diversity
description: Introduction to the ancient and modern models of democracy which underpin contemporary democratic life. An analysis of the philosophical bases of democracy, diversity, political obligation, equality, liberty, consent, representation, and rights.

subject: POL S
title: Courts, Judges and Politics
description: The role and significance of the judiciary in the American political system. Such questions as: how cases go through the courts, how "interests" are represented through litigation, the processes by which judges are recruited, and the "independence" of the judiciary will be explored. The course will also entail an exploration of how judges reach decisions and the impacts and consequences of those decisions. The emphasis will be largely on the federal courts, especially the U.S. Supreme Court, and the main focus will be on "public," rather than "private" law.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Democratic Political Institutions
description: Study of the key political institutional structure of democracy in comparative perspective. Political institutions of the United States and peer democracies covered will include constitutions, the electoral system, the system of government (presidential vs. parliamentary), vertical relations (centralization vs. decentralization), and the legislature. In addition to familiarizing students with the variety and operation of these political institutions, attention will be paid to their advantages and disadvantages, political and policy effects, and implications for the challenges confronting contemporary democracies.
repeat_comments: POLS 106CD was renumbered as POLS 116.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Social Movement Politics
description: Social movements embody pure politics. They mobilize citizens and are a form of collective action. Scholars have shown that outcomes as wide-ranging as quality of governance, the survival of regimes and nation states, electoral mobilization, citizenship rights, and levels of violence during civil wars can be explained by movements and their attributes.
advisor_comments: Not available to students that have taken POL S 106SM.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Ethnic Politics
description: Examination of the political consequences of ethnicity. Theoretical approaches to issues addressing problems of multiethnic states in the developing world, and the successor states of the Soviet Union.

subject: POL S
title: Ethical Issues in International Relations
description: An examination of the possibility and desirability of normative international political theory and an exploration of the moral dimensions of statecraft; use of force, nuclear deterrence, humanitarian intervention,distributive justice, and human rights.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for additional units of credit as long as letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: Ethical Issues in International Relations: Just War
description: An examination of the possibility and desirability of normative international political theory and an exploration of the moral dimensions of statecraft; use of force, nuclear deterrence, humanitarian intervention, distributive justice, and human rights.
advisor_comments: Can be repeated for additional credit, provided letter designations are different.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for additional units of credit as long as letter designations are different.

subject: POL S
title: American Government and Politics
description: Political ideas, institutions, and processes of American government. The role of congress and the president in policy formation and of the supreme court in interpreting the constitution.

subject: POL S
title: Negotiation in Theory and Practice
description: This course focuses on negotiation in theory and practice. It uses lectures and hands-on exercises in class to build students skills. It draws on research on negotiation, with a focus on applying these ideas to political contexts and institutions. It also helps build practical skills in communication, leadership and decision-making.

subject: POL S
title: International Politics
description: An examination of theories concerning the actions, interactions, and relationships among nation-states.

subject: POL S
title: The Politics of International Monetary Relations
description: The politics of international monetary relations. The aim is to learn how to understand and evaluate the current functioning of money and finance in the global economy.

subject: POL S
title: International Organizations
description: The nature and function of international organizations, including a study of the United Nations and the European community.

subject: POL S
title: International Law
description: Nature and sources of international law; international legal personality; nationality, territory, jurisdiction; diplomatic and consular agents; treaties; war; neutrality.

subject: POL S
title: International Security
description: Examines how states use diplomacy, strategic coercion, and military force to achieve political objectives.

subject: POL S
title: American Foreign Policy
description: The United States in world politics. Policy making institutions, particularly the presidency, congress, state department, and the military establishment. Interaction between domestic and external politics.

subject: POL S
title: Foreign Relations Between China and the United States
description: The ideological and cultural attitudes of mainland China, with emphasis on general policies both within the communist world and other areas (South Asia, Africa, and America).

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Military Politics
description: Examines a militarys role in domestic politics by focusing on a diverse set of topics including civil-military relations, militarys role in citizen making, economic progress, conflict management, and nation building.

subject: POL S
title: Relations Between the United States and Mexico
description: A general examination of relations between the United States and Mexico in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Emphasis on issues such as the origins of conflict and cooperation, and current issue areas including immigration.

subject: POL S
title: Government and Politics of Japan
description: The organization and operation of Japanese politics, with particular attention to domestic political forces and problems.

subject: POL S
title: Gender Rights in World Politics
description: This class analyzes the state of women’s rights in world politics and how to respond to global challenges. We examine themes from international relations including international political economy, global security, and migration as drivers and locations of gender rights struggles. We also consider the relationship between gender rights and the comparative politics of development, democracy, social movements, and law and society. A feminist analysis will add the complementary issues of the politics of reproduction, rights in the private sphere, and the importance of gender roles and norms as a dimension of power.
repeat_comments: This course replaces POLS 106GR. Students can repeat POLS 106GR with a repeatable grade by taking POLS 139.

subject: POL S
title: Water Politics
description: Climate change and rapidly depleting water resources are the biggest challenges facing humanity in the 21st century. Claims over water by powerful sectors including commercial farming, industrialization and urbanization will get stronger and water scarcity will further marginalize the poor from their livelihoods. This course has examples from around the world, deals with the pressing challenges related to water, and gives the students a better understanding of politics related to water.

subject: POL S
title: Civil War
description: Patterns in the phenomenon of civil war and ethnic conflict. A survey of the causes of these conflicts and an exploration of the consequences. Special attention is given to several key cases of civil conflict to illustrate core concepts.

subject: POL S
title: Foreign Policy Decision Making
description: Examines how leaders and organizations make and implement foreign policy.

subject: POL S
title: Russian Domestic Politics
description: The course examines the basic characteristics of the Soviet ancient regime and the forces and institutions which shaped the emerging states and societies. Topics include: parliamentary and economic systems, political parties, interest groups, ethnicity, legitimacy, sovereignty and inter-state relations.
prereq_text: Political Science 6 and 15; not open to freshmen.

subject: POL S
title: The European Union
description: Introduction to the history and organization of the European Union (the institutions, policies, goals, and successes of the EU). Focus on the ongoing process of economical, political, social, and cultural integration in Europe since the Second World War. In English.
advisor_comments: POL S 145 and ITAL 161X are the same course

subject: POL S
title: Globalization and Politics
description: An examination and assessment of theories of globalization in relation to the distribution of political power on a global scale, future scenarios of global political domination, and the role of the nation-state in the international system of power.

subject: POL S
title: POLITICS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
description: A comparative analysis of the political system of a selected number of African, Asian and Middle Eastern countries, with particular development and modernization common to all of them.

subject: POL S
title: Israeli Politics
description: An introduction to the politics of Israel. Examines both Israeli domestic politics and Israel in comparative perspective.
prereq_text: Political Science 6 and 15; not open to freshmen.

subject: POL S
title: Introduction to Research in Political Science
description: An introduction to the design and evaluation of political research, from formulating clear questions and gathering appropriate data, to the use of simple statistical techniques for analyzing data and presenting evidence.
advisor_comments: Designed for majors. Quarters usually offered: Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall. Not open to students who have completed Political Science 104, 104A and 104AL.
repeat_comments: Students can repeat this course after taking POL SW 15.

subject: POL S
title: Politics of the Middle East and North Africa
description: This course provides an introduction to key theoretical debates in the comparative politics and international relations of the Middle East. We cover the major areas of political science research on the region while also building substantive knowledge about the politics of individual countries. This course aims to help students identify broad trends in the political, social, and economic development of the Middle East and critically evaluate existing explanations for those trends.

subject: POL S
title: American Political Parties
description: The nature, characteristics, and history of American political parties; party organization; political campaigns and finance; nominations, elections, and electoral problems.

subject: POL S
title: Public Opinion
description: A study of the formation and nature of public opinion including: the public's political sophistication; the role of emotion in political thinking; nature of political culture; growth of political alienation and the forms of political participation.
prereq_text: Political Science 15 or 104 or Sociology 3 or 104A or Psychology 5 or Communications 88.

subject: POL S
title: Congress Simulation
description: The organization, operation, and politics of congress examined through the lens of theory and demonstrated in conjunction with the required simulation lab POLS 155L.
prereq_text: Political Science 12; concurrent enrollment in Political Science 155L.

subject: POL S
title: Congress Simulation Lab
description: A simulation of the U.S. House of Representatives designed to teach the operation and politics of Congress, and requires concurrent enrollment in POLS 155 Congress Simulation lecture course.
prereq_text: Political Science 12; concurrent enrollment in Political Science 155.

subject: POL S
title: Asian American Politics
description: Survey of the historical and contemporary political experiences of Asian Americans and their pursuits for immigration, equality, citizenship, political identity, racial justice, cross-racial/ethnic coalition building and incorporation into the U. S. political system.
prereq_text: Political Science 12 or Asian American Studies 1 or Asian American Studies 2.

subject: POL S
title: U. S. Minority Politics
description: A comparative study of recent literature on the historical and contemporary political experiences of the four major racial and ethnic minority groups (Blacks/African Americans, American Indians, Latinos/Hispanic Americans, and Asian Americans) and their interactions with the dominant racial group (non-Hispanic white Americans) in the U.S.
prereq_text: Political Science 12. Not open to freshmen.

subject: POL S
title: Urban Government and Politics
description: Problems of politics and administration in urban and metropolitan areas.

subject: POL S
title: US Immigration Politics and Policy
description: Examines the politics of US immigration policy.

subject: POL S
title: Public Policy Analysis
description: The assumptions, goals, content, and consequences of selected domestic policies, concentrating on the period since 1960. Discussion of the nature of collective action, methods of policy analysis and evaluation, and problems of implementation.

subject: POL S
title: Political Communication in the U.S.
description: Political communication in the United States. Covering the interplay of news, social media, and other forms of communication with public opinion and political behavior.

subject: POL S
title: Media and Politics in Comparative and Historical Perspective
description: A comparative examination across countries of the theory and history of media and politics.

subject: POL S
title: Politics of the Environment
description: Analysis of environmental policy issues and their treatment in the political process. Discussion of the interplay of substantive issues, ideology, institutions, and private groups in the development, management, protection, and preservation of natural resources and the natural environment.
advisor_comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 178.
prereq_text: Political Science 12 or Environmental Studies 3; upper-division standing.

subject: POL S
title: Energy Politics and Policy
description: Introduces students to the politics and policy of the contemporary global energy system. Covers major public policies and politics related to both the electricity and transportation systems. Students learn energy technology characteristics and understand contemporary political debates over the energy system.
repeat_comments: Students who had taken POLS 106EP or POLS 106PE, and who earned a repeatable grade (a C- or lower), MAY retake the course with its new number.
prereq_text: Political Science 6 or 12, or Environmental Studies 1 or 3.

subject: POL S
title: Comparative Environmental Politics
description: Course is structured around the major issues in environmental politics, for example: global warming, nuclear waste, deforestation, and chemical pollution. The roles of economics, technology and social organization are each considered as explanatory variables for understanding environmental problems.
advisor_comments: Same course as Environmental Studies 177.

subject: POL S
title: Democracy and the Internet
description: Examines challenges to democratic process and public spheres associated with digital media, including: harms to privacy, misinformation, propaganda, anti-social behavior, political extremism and violence, and corporate power, with an emphasis on the US.

subject: POL S
title: Bureaucracy and Public Policy
description: The nature of American bureaucracy, its organization and culture and its role as a political institution.

subject: POL S
title: Introduction to International Political Economy
description: Introduction to the politics of international economic relations. Examination of alternative analytical and theoretical perspectives for their value in helping to understand and evaluate the historical development and current operation of the world economy.
advisor_comments: Same course as Global Studies 123. Not open for credit to students who have completed Political Science 186A.

subject: POL S
title: Classical Political Theory
description: A careful examination of major texts and thinkers in the ancient world and in medieval times.

subject: POL S
title: Modern Political Theory
description: Development of political ideas from the sixteenth century to the nineteenthcentury.

subject: POL S
title: Recent and Contemporary Political Theory
description: A reconstruction of the contending theories of political order with which western intellectuals, from the nineteenth to the present century, have confronted an era of world historical changes.

subject: POL S
title: Field Research in Political Science
description: Directed research on the political process through participant observation and relevant reading. Individually assigned, instructed, and supervised fieldwork. Students will examine first hand behavior in leading political roles in American politics.
advisor_comments: Students must have a 3.0 grade-point-average.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of department prior to enrollment.

subject: POL S
title: Group Studies
description: Themes will vary according to instructor.
advisor_comments: Subject to departmental approval, students may repeat this course. Only 4 units may apply to the major.

subject: POL S
title: Senior Seminar in Political Science.
description: Senior seminar in political science.
advisor_comments: Students should have a recommended minimum grade point average of 3.0 overall.

subject: POL S
title: Honors Thesis Seminar in Political Science
description: Political Science 197A-B-C is a three quarter sequence course with the final grade issued upon completion of 197C. Honors students, in three-quarter sequence of seminars, write original theses under close faculty supervision.
advisor_comments: Requires a 3.3 cum UCSB GPA and 3.6 major GPA for eligibility to apply to the program. A three-quarter course. Final grade issued upon completion of POLS 197C. By petition, 8 units allocated to core concentration, with 4 units toward electives.
