subject: SPAN
title: Posmodernismo
description: Study of the Spanish and Spanish-American Postmodernistas, exploring the link between the culture of modernity and the emergence of a colloquial, prosaic, but lyrical discourse in late nineteenth and twentieth century Spanish and Spanish-American poetry.

subject: SPAN
title: Literature and Cultural Identity in the Spanish Caribbean
description: Survey of Spanish Caribbean literature from the standpoint of interaction of culture and race. It traces the counterpoint among the diverse ethnic groups that populate the Caribbean and the manner in which the discourse ofthe oppressor and the oppressed intertwine.

subject: SPAN
title: Spain's "Disaster" and the Avant-Garde
description: Focuses on Spain’s political and cultural transformation from the world’s largest empire to an isolated country. The course covers the contentious discussions about the modernization of the country and the irruption of the Avant-Garde
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Latin America on Film
description: An exploration of Latin American film and how this medium represents the cultures, histories and politics of the region. We will study a selection of films encompassing different genres, styles and historical periods, including some key works by influential Latin American filmmakers.

subject: SPAN
title: Lorca, Tradition, Modernity, and the Avant Garde
description: A study of Lorcas poetry and theater in the context of the major artistic, sociopolitical and historical transformations of the early 20th century, exploring how traditional Spanish culture and avant-garde innovation intersect each other in his work.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently)

subject: SPAN
title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.
advisor_comments: Same course as LAIS 174.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Contemporary Spanish Cultural Studies
description: An interdisciplinary approach to the understanding of present-day Spain, focusing on popular music, TV and literature from the 1960s until today.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish-American Thought
description: Leading social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends from the sixteenth century to the present.

subject: SPAN

description: Social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends in the developmentof modern Mexico.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit by students who have taken Spanish 180.

subject: SPAN
title: Chicana/o Novels

advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.

subject: SPAN
title: Hispanic Poetry: 1900 to 1945
description: Reading and discussion of twentieth-century Spanish and Spanish-American poets and trends in their socio-historical context.
advisor_comments: Spanish 181 is the Spanish version of Spanish 181E.
repeat_comments: Spanish 181 is a legal repeat of Spanish 181E.

subject: SPAN
title: Special Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture
description: Special topics in Latin American literature and culture.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided the letter designation is different.

subject: SPAN
title: Science Fiction in Latin America
description: An exploration of science fiction narrative and film from Latin America. Through a selection of works by Latin American authors from the early 20th century until the present, we will study how the history, cultures, and traditions of the region have shaped the genre of science fiction, and how this affords a singular perspective to think about topics like technology, neoliberalism, ethnicity, colonialism, the environment, and the future of the planet.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided the letter designation is different.
prereq_text: Spanish 30 or Spanish 102L (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Study of Hispanic Literature by Author or Special Topics
description: Study of Hispanic literature by author or special topics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Gender in Basque Culture
description: Using Basque culture as a case study, this course explores how gender intersects with other crucial issues such as ethnicity, nationhood, and globalization.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Conflict, Memory, and Cultural Production
description: Explores how cultural artifacts like novels and films articulate individual and collective histories of violence.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Basque Studies through Literature and Culture in Translation (Spanish/English)
description: Delves deeper into the diversity of topics that make up Basque Studies, and analyses historical, but also contemporary socio-cultural topics related to the Basque country and the Basque diaspora abroad. Can be taken either as a continuation of SPAN 153E or a self-standing course on Basque Studies, where literary and cultural materials are presented in their English, Spanish, and possibly also French translations depending on student interest and language choice.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different. However, only 8 units may be applied towards the Spanish major.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Basque Film
description: Provides a critical examination of the history and poetics of Basque film from the 20th century to the present.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designation is different.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Contemporary Spanish-American Short Story
description: A study of the trends, themes and techniques of the contemporary Spanish American short story with emphasis on major authors such as Borges, Cortzar, Ocampo, Onetti, Rulfo, Carpentier, Garca Mrquez, and others.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: The Spanish-American Nueva Novela
description: Readings of such authors as Borges, Rulfo Fuentes, Vargas Llosa, Garcia Marquez, Donoso. Emphasis put on the innovative structure and language brought to Hispanic literature by the so-called Nueva Novela.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Selected Topics in Hispanic Linguistics
description: Topics for the course reflect the research interests of faculty members.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.

subject: SPAN
title: Teaching Spanish
description: An introduction to the field of Second Language Acquisition and Foreign Language Teaching. Special attention will be given to topics that have proved most problematic for native speakers of English who learn Spanish as a second language. After a general overview of Applied Linguistics, the course will cover topics dealing with teaching situations. This course is a theoretical and practical review of how to teach writing, reading, communicative competence, listening comprehension and culture at all levels of Spanish study.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.

subject: SPAN
title: Translation, Technology, and the Mind: An Introduction to Translation and Cognition
description: Translation, Technology, and the Mind is an introduction to technology in translation and interpretation. Students will learn about translation and interpretation, technologies used in the field and in research, and how translation/interpretation is performed in the mind. Throughout the course, students will have the opportunity to reflect on their own uses of technology as they develop their translation and interpretation skills.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 20 units, provided letter designations are different.

subject: SPAN
title: Modern Hispanic Drama
description: Representative dramatists of Spain such as Unamuno, Valle-Inclan, Garcia Lorca, Buero Vallejo, and others.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Modernismo
description: Introduction to the poetry and prose of Hispanic Modernismo. Major writers and their most representative works: Marti, Dario, Rodo, Lugones. Lyric poetry, short story, novel, the essay, and other forms are studied.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Vanguard Poetry in Spanish America
description: A survey of the poetry of the Spanish-American avant-guarde focusing on its three main tendencies: colloquial or antipoetic poetry, existentially or politically committed poetry, and self-referential, narcissistic poetry.
advisor_comments: LAIS 189 and SPAN 189 are the same course.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

subject: SPAN
title: Borges and His Precursors
description: This course focuses on Borges the Reader, and traces in particular his affinities with North American and European literatures.

subject: SPAN
title: Capstone Seminar - Peninsular Spanish Studies
description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Peninsular Spanish Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.
advisor_comments: Recommended major GPA of 3.5 or higher. Recommended cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.Please see Undergraduate Advisor for approval code.

subject: SPAN
title: Capstone Seminar - Latin American Studies
description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Latin American Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish American Women's Writing
description: An introduction to nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spanish American women's writings. Themes may include women's participation in the formation of national literatures, their engagement with a tradition of women's writing, and issues of authorship and authority.
advisor_comments: LAIS 194 and SPAN 194 are the same course.
prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently).

subject: SPAN
title: Senior Honors Independent Research
description: The student will engage in research lead ing to a paper of considerable depth and complexity on a topic dealing with the literature and/or languageof Spain and Spanish America.

subject: SPAN
title: Independent Studies in Spanish
description: Independent studies in selected subjects not covered by course offerings.
advisor_comments: Students must have a minimum 3.0 GPA for the preceding 3 quarters and are limited to 5 units per quarter and 30 units total in all 98/99/198/199/199AA-ZZ courses combined.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish and consent of department.

subject: SPAN
title: Topics in Peninsular Cultural Studies
description: Every iteration of this course will be organized around a different theme. We will include a wide range of cultural productions from Spain, such as films, popular genres, the press, political discourses, and other non-canonical texts and cultural artifacts related to culture as history. The cultural artifacts will be examined by using critical lenses including identity, race, ideology, power, class, andhistorical representation.

subject: SPAN
title: Emergency Poetics in Latin America
description: Emergency Poetics in Latin America provides graduate students with the chance to examine art and literature from Latin America and U.S. Latinx communities spanning the 20th and 21st centuries. This approach offers a unique methodology aimed at understanding these cultural expressions within their historical contexts through a transdisciplinary lens. Emergency Poetics utilizes linguistic and formal tools to convey urgent messages in response to imminent dangers, often diverging from established canons. This divergence categorizes works as experimental or impenetrable, allowing them to react dynamically to specific stimuli.

subject: SPAN
title: Research Methodologies and Theories of Literatures
description: Approaches and methods for research in Hispanic and Portuguese and Brazilian literatures. Techniques of literary scholarship will also be considered as well as the analysis and application of methods of current literaty theories and criticism.

subject: SPAN
title: Women Authors of the Spanish Language
description: An examination of women's strategies of self-figuration, traditions of female expression, women's relationship to authorship and authority, and the relationship of Spanish-language writing to contemporary feminist criticism.

subject: SPAN
title: Individual Hispanic Authors and Special Topics
description: Intensive study of the work of an individual Hispanic author, to be chosen by the instructor.
advisor_comments: Course may be repeated for a total of 24 units (six courses, each a different author).

subject: SPAN
title: Food and Politics in Spain
description: In this graduate seminar, we delve into the complex relationship between food and politics in Spain. We explore how food has played a crucial role in shaping the diverse cultures and national identities within the country. Additionally, we discuss topics such as the significance of "national products" and their role in nation branding, as well as the impact of food scarcity during Franco's dictatorship. Our approach will be multidisciplinary, incorporating scholarly books, cookbooks, and other materials to provide a comprehensive understanding of the topic. Furthermore, we will have guest speakers who will share their expertise and insights on the subject.

subject: SPAN
title: Migration, Border Regimes, and Transborder Aesthetics: The U.S.–Mexico Border
description: This graduate seminar examines migration as a structuring force of cultural production at the U.S.–Mexico border. Approaching the border as an aesthetic, political, and epistemological regime, the course analyzes how literature, visual art, film, performance, sound, and digital practices emerge from and intervene in systems of mobility, surveillance, control, and displacement. Drawing on critical migration studies, border theory, decolonial thought, political philosophy, and aesthetic theory, the seminar treats cultural production not just as representation but as a site of theoretical knowledge. While centered on the U.S.–Mexico border, the course situates this region within broader global debates on migration and sovereignty.

subject: SPAN
title: Studies in Spanish-American Colonial Literature
description: Selected topics from the sixteenth, seventeenth, and eighteenth centuries.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit with the consent of the department graduate adviser.

subject: THTR W
title: Performance in Global Contexts, Asia
description: This course surveys a range of Asian performances across a diversity of locations, from thetraditional theater forms of Japanese Kabuki, Indonesian Wayang Kulit, and Indian Kathakali tomodern forms in India and Japan to contemporary Chinese performance art. Theater forms like Chinese Jingju and Japanese Noh will prompt us to reevaluate what the performer does in rehearsal and in situations on and off the stage. By exploring recent modern and contemporary performance forms, we will reassess how an actor, dancer, or puppeteer can challenge the status quo and effect change. As we ask these questions, we will situate Asian performance within social, political, and historical contexts to understand its rich functions and significances.
advisor_comments: THTR W 2B is the online version of THTR 2B.
repeat_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed THTR 2B.

subject: THTR W
title: The People’s Voice/The Odyssey Project
description: A collaborative educational theater program between the Theater Department at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), and County of Santa Barbara Probation. Student participants from both institutions will partner in a work setting that fosters equity to process and perform original performance pieces using analog and digital technology. The framework for this class is ancient Greek canonical literature with healing and heroic dimensions. The Odyssey of Homer provides the template. Through a series of writing and drawing exercises, the participants discover the heroic elements in their lives and how to utilize them to tell the Odyssey story in their own words.
advisor_comments: THTR W 143 is the online version of THTR 143

title: Performance in Global Contexts: Africa and the Caribbean
description: Introduction to local performance traditions in Africa and the Caribbean, such as storytelling, ritual, and Carnival. The course also examines how African and Caribbean playwrights put those traditions to social and political uses by incorporating them into post-colonial plays.

title: Performance in Global Contexts: EUROPE
description: Introduction to theater and performance practice and traditions in Europe. Topics will include ritual, the rise of a public theater, the political uses of theater, the development of festival theater, and the uses of performance in non-theatrical contexts.

Students will read and analyze the structure of plays, write and stage their own short plays, and gain experience acting in and directing each other's work. subject: THTR
title: Design Fundamentals for Dance and Theater
description: In this course, you will be introduced to the fundamentals of design for theatre, dance, performance, and live events. You’ll be taught about four disciplines of design including Scenery, Costume, Lighting, and Projection along with a series of approaches to formulate and communicate your own design work to others. Inspired by texts, music, and research, you will create visual designs that express ideas and aesthetic choices while fulfilling practical requirements for the performer or participant in an intentional environment. Through hands-on projects and class activities, you will create designs for live performance through writing, research, 2D media and 3D models.
advisor_comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Theater W 19. THTR W 19 is the online version of THTR 19.

subject: THTR

description: Projects in the interpretation of plays through scenic elements with concentration on the design process and the dramatic use of space. Drafting projects including floor plans, elevations and basic perspective drawing.
advisor_comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR
title: Stage Lighting Design
description: Lecture-demonstration in instrumentation, color in light, control equipment, and basic lighting design theories. Technical drawing including light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design. Some practical application through laboratory and studio exercise.
advisor_comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR

subject: THTR

description: Exploration of basic elements and principles of projection design for live performance. Projects in the interpretation of plays through visual elements. Introduction to projection, video, and media design for live performance and installation. Projects involve interpretation of plays and music, technical approaches to equipment, and programming equipment for media designs.

subject: THTR
title: Costume Design
description: In this course students will receive a more detailed, but introductory exposure to the world of costume design. They will learn how costume design plays an essential function in the collaboration of live theatre, opera, television, and film. Students will experience the step-by-step creative process of this design discipline, while implementing strong character analysis skills and recognizing the importance of thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to build characters, from the ground up, using the power of dress.
advisor_comments: Open to non-majors. May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.

description: Using theater games, improvisation and storytelling, this course expands the imagination and frees the instincts of the actor. Exercises reflect the work of improvisation icons such as Viola Spolin, Augusto Boal, and Paul Sills. Students also explore techniques for sharing/teaching these games in community settings such as schools, senior citizen centers, etc. Prerequisite: Theater 5 or Instructor's Approval. Highly recommended for students focusing on Theater and Community.

description: This course introduces advanced design and directing students to key concepts and skills that promote successful theatrical collaboration. Directing and design teams will research all aspects of a play and develop a proposed unified production using a shared verbal and visual language.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Scenic Design
description: This course builds upon tools learned in THTR 22: Beginning Set Design to increase fluency in scenic design approaches and techniques. Focusing on building ideas from texts and music, you will evolve design approaches through research and critiques. Designs will culminate in scale models and supporting materials. Projects in THTR 122 will focus on opera, dance, and musical theatre with unique scenic demands including multiple locations, period detail, and awareness of performance styles and conventions.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Stage Lighting Design
description: Lecture-demonstration of controllable properties and functions of light. Includes technical drawing: light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design, drawing using light and shadow, perspective drawing. Practical application through studio exercise.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR
title: Design Portfolio
description: This course will introduce students to advanced topics in the art and craft of visual media design for projection and video with an emphasis on live performance.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR
title: Advanced Costume Design
description: In this course students will receive an advance and detailed perspective on the art of costume design. Through four different projects, they will explore different character development experiences, with a continued focus on thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to craft character, while focusing on the scope of a full production.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 10 units.

subject: THTR
title: Theatre Rendering Techniques
description: Advanced theatre rendering techniques for the theatre designer. Continued development in drawing and use of different mediums. Concentration on rendering light, shadow, and texture.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 6 units with instructor consent.

subject: THTR
title: History of Decorative Styles
description: A survey of the evolution of design styles and production trends in western theater, emphasizing the history of design and designers, including a study of both interior and exterior decoration with concentration on furnishing, accessories and the changing patterns of culture.

subject: THTR
title: Puppet Design and Construction
description: Explores the history of various puppet styles and will focus on the design and creation of three iconic puppet forms: Thai shadow puppets (Nang yai), rod puppets (Bunraku), and marionettes. Students will learn both the mechanical aspects and the artistic design elements of puppet creation by creating one of each of these three styles.

The workshop culminates in an invited public reading at the end of each week. Over the 3 weeks, participants have the opportunity to take on different functions in the process.

Classes consist of lectures, guest speakers, film viewing, and discussion where we interrogate what it means to be a performer in a sport like climbing. subject: THTR
title: Research Methods in Theater, Dance and Performance Studies
description: Introduction to select methods for conducting advanced research in theatre, drama, and performance. Students will read exemplary monographs and statements of method from leading scholars in the field. They will then practically apply those methods to an original, ongoing research project that will culminate in a substantive seminar paper.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Research Methods: Ethnography and Performance
description: Introduction to select methods for conducting advanced research in theatre, drama, and performance. The methodological focus, which varies according to instructor, may include ethnography, historiography, dramatic criticism, phenomenology, or audience reception, among others. Students will read exemplary monographs and statements of method from leading scholars in the field. They will then practically apply those methods to an original, ongoing research project that will culminate in a substantive seminar paper.

subject: THTR

description: This seminar introduces critical methods central to the fields of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Historiography
description: Covers diverse methods and theoretical approaches of historiography of performance and performance as historiography. Readings trouble ideas of history production and understandings of the past. We explore past assumptions about subject, time, and place central to traditional historiographical methods and identify new approaches and directions. And, we consider how theoretical and methodological approaches under the umbrella of historiography adjust to reflect changes in understandings of people, places, and systems of knowledge.
repeat_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Theories for Performance, Theater, and Dance Research
description: Introduction to key theories and conceptual frameworks for conduction advanced research in theater, dance, and performance studies. Students will read exemplary theoretical texts from established and newer scholarly voices. Topics vary and may include Marxism, Brecht, Artaud, theories fo the avant-garde, psychoanalysis, critical race theory, feminism, structuralism, post-structuralism, postmodernism, postcolonialism, and transnationalism.

subject: THTR
title: Theories of the Everyday and Performance
description: Examines theories of the everyday that relate to theater, dance, and performance studies.

subject: THTR
title: Theories for Performance, Theater, and Dance Research
description: Examines and reevaluates performance theory and its application with attention to global theater forms and performance practices.

subject: THTR
title: Histories of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
description: Introduction to pre-1900 historical time periods in theater, dance, and performance studies. Students read exemplary historical texts and learn key historiographical methods from established and newer scholarly voices. Periods and topics vary and may include material conditions of performance, gender and sexuality studies, global theater and dance, and embodied and dramaturgical approaches to dance and theater history.

subject: THTR
title: Modern and Contemporary Theory
description: A graduate level introduction to twentieth and twenty-first century critical theory. Topics vary and may include Marxism, Brecht, Artaud, theories of the avant-garde, psychoanalysis, feminism, structuralism, post-structuralism, postmodernism, and postcolonialism.

subject: THTR
title: Topics in Dramatic Literature and Theatre History
description: A survey course that introduces students to a range of historical periods, dramatic work, playwrights, artistic movements, and theatrical trends. Topics vary and may include classics in performance, translating drama, global theatre, violence in drama, dramatic genre, and literature and theatre.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Shakespeare Beyond the Global
description: Shakespeare has reigned as a global phenomenon in text, performance and film for over thirty years. But why? What is a global Shakespeare? How was a global Shakespeare devised? Can we move beyond the global? Can we think beyond the global? By considering these lines of inquiry, this seminar seeks to investigate the formations of Shakespeare as a global icon, global commodity, and global performance framework. We will also think through the violent histories of colonialism, racialization and empire that undergird the "Global Shakespeare '' movement. Authors and practitioners include: Preti Taneja, Kim F. Hall, Alexa Joubin, Ambereen Dadabhoy, Vishal Bharadwaj, Akira Kurosawa, Madeline Sayet, Sujata Iyengar, Ruben Espinosa, Gauri Viswanathan.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Playwriting and Dramaturgy
description: An investigation of the art of playwriting in terms of the dramaturgy of how plays work.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Topics in Dramatic Literature, Theatre History, and Performance Practices
description: This course investigates the intersections between art, literature, philosophy, and performance practices. It may include specific histories of theatre and performance, conceptual frames across cultures, genre studies, issues of translation, postcolonial analysis, and other topics.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: The Fate of Ophelia: Shakespeare and Popular Culture
description: This graduate seminar examines how Shakespeare circulates through contemporary popular culture. Though rooted in the early modern stage, Shakespeare's characters, plots, and language now form a global cultural vocabulary, appearing across film, television, music, fashion, advertising, and digital media. The course treats Shakespeare not as fixed canon but as a dynamic cultural resource that artists and audiences continually transform to speak to new historical moments. Drawing on adaptation studies, performance theory, and cultural criticism, the seminar explores why Shakespeare remains so culturally influential and how his works move across media and genres
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Special Topics in Performance Studies
description: Varies in content from year to year, but offerings may include studies of the avant-garde and performance art, sport as ritual and performance, theatre on trial, politics and war as performance, embodiment, and global performance traditions.
repeat_comments: Mary be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of American Dance
description: Border Crossing challenges accepted histories of dance modernism to consider how war, inequality, and injustice shaped twentieth century performance art. This graduate seminar bears witness to the exiled and marginalized dance artist - the Unsung - whose artistry, oftentimes invisible, is vital to the history of dance.
repeat_comments: Mary be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Special Topics in Performance Studies
description: Exploration of the history and theory of story and storytelling, both in its relation to dramatic and/or choreographed plot and as a performance mode in itself.
repeat_comments: Mary be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Critical Dance Studies: Special Topics in Dance History and Theory
description: This graduate seminar provides an introduction to the history and critical theory of dance inglobal contexts. The methodologicalfocus may include critical dance studies, historiography,ethnography, feminist theory, critical race theory, body theory - corporealities - art and architectural(site-specific performance) theory, and performance studies. Students read and analyze a widearray of critics, scholars, and artists and demonstrate fluency in critical dance studies through writtenpapers and weekly seminar discussion. Live Performance serves as archival source material.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Defiant Bodies: Art, Dance, Digital Media
description: Defiant Bodies: Art, Dance, Digital Media surveys an interdisciplinary array of visual art, digital media, and live performance. Together, we identify historiographic relationships between protest culture, human philosophy, and performance.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of Modern Dance
description: Border Crossings: Exilic Experience in the Making of American Dance, challenges previous histories of transglobal modernism to consider how war, inequality, and injustice shaped twentieth century performance art. The intellectual, pedagogical, and spiritual embodiment of a bicoastal exhibit and performance series, together as an intellectual community of scholar-artists, we investigate definitions of exile and exilic modernism as each engenders methodologies in the fields of Dance Studies and Performance Studies.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Body and Performance An Introduction to Critical Dance Studies as Curatorial Practice
description: Body and Performance is meant to introduce students to the fields of Dance Studies and Curatorial Practice, as well as to performative moments in the history of dance. We will learn to theorize the body in performance, and discuss how to curate the body in performance in found spaces. Part dance—history, criticism, ethnography, and body theory—and part curation—site-specific performance art—we will pursue a wide range of texts and performative works of art in a multiplicity of architectural spaces and stylistic genres. Designed as an introduction to dance and museum studies, Critical Dance Studies as Curatorial Practice is ultimately concerned with the historical, artistic, and physical spaces in which performance takes place.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Dancing the Diaspora
description: Dancing the Diaspora traces a genealogy of dance and choreographic practice in the Afro-Caribbean and American worlds. We examine a range of interdisciplinary texts, from theoretical discourses surrounding a range of issues -- diasporic identity, dance histories of religious and concert stage traditions, and art historical texts that deepen our aesthetic understanding of dancing bodies in West African and Africanist religious ritual and secular performance.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art
description: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art is a new graduate seminar that considers the historical condition of diasporic performance art. Furthermore, we study the ability of artists to translate exilic experience into artistic identity and materialist phenomenology; or, to be in exile in art.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment and Visual Art
description: Diaspora and Performance: Transnational Studies in Exile, Embodiment, and Visual Art is a new graduate seminar that considers the historical condition of diasporic performance art. Furthermore, we study the ability of artists to translate exilic experience into artistic identity and materialist phenomenology; or, to be in exile in art.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Contemporary American Dance During the Cold War Era
description: Contemporary American Dance During the Cold War Era is an interdisciplinary graduate seminar that examines how geopolitics have shaped the American stage. In an era of McCarthyism, overt patriotism, and covert nation-building, we study how the U.S. State Department used dance and dancing bodies to advertise American democracy to the world.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Critical Dance Studies: Special Topics in Dance History and Theory
description: This graduate seminar provides an introduction to the history and critical theory of dance in global contexts. The methodological focus may include critical dance studies, historiography, ethnography, feminist theory, critical race theory, body theory - corporealities - art and architectural (site-specific performance) theory, and performance studies. Students will read and analyze a wide array of critics, scholars, and artists and demonstrate fluency in critical dance studies through written papers and weekly seminar discussion. Live Performance will serve as archival source material.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: The Performance of Physicality
description: The Performance of Physicality explores history’s relationship to and artists’ perception of the body in performance and visual art. Crossing borders and time, we study theories of physicality and assess visual and theatrical representations. We will consider how we come to assess the physical world through visuality.
repeat_comments: Course cannot be repeated for additional units of credit.

subject: THTR
title: Performance of Physicality
description: Explores various case studies of the theatrical representation and perception of the human body in Europe, the Americas, and Asia in the twentieth century especially related to the construction of gender, race, class, nation,and sexuality.

subject: THTR
title: Contemporary American Dance during the Cold War Era
description: An interdisciplinary graduate seminar that examines how racism, immigration, imagination, and geopolitics have shaped perceptions of the dancing body in both classical and contemporary dance. Dance Studies course that examines how racism in the United States has shaped and been shaped by the American stage. In an era of overt patriotism and nation-building, we study how the dancers and choreographers themselves contributed to the racialization bodies in motion.
repeat_comments: This course is not repeatable for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Directing for Graduate Students
description: An investigation of the fundamentals and techniques of directing, including principles of staging, text analysis, and actor coaching.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: THTR
title: Practice in Design
description: Projects and study in design; practical application to projects.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: THTR
title: Practice in Dramaturgy
description: Projects in dramaturgy; practical applications and projects.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: THTR
title: Practice in Directing
description: Advanced problems in directing, practical applications, and projects. Culminates in directing one-act plays.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.
prereq_text: Theater 221 or 261; graduate standing; consent of instructor.

subject: THTR
title: Practice in Playwriting
description: An independent study in playwrighting. Students may work on a full-length play, a one act play, a solo performance text.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: THTR
title: Practice in Theatre and Dance
description: Projects in various areas of theatre and dance, including acting, stage management, production and directing.

subject: THTR
title: European Theatre and Drama
description: An examination of theatrical and dramatic traditions of Europe. Offerings vary, but may include ancient and medieval drama and theatre, the Renaissance, Shakespeare, as well as Enlightenment, Sturm and Drang and Romanticism, Realism, Naturalism, and Symbolism.
repeat_comments: May repeat for credit

subject: THTR
title: Theatre and Drama of the United States
description: An examination of trends and traditions in theatre of the United States. Roots of Broadway, U.S. Latino theatre, Asian American theatre, melodrama, the Group Theatre and its legacy, multicultural theatre and contemporary theater.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit.

subject: THTR
title: Teaching: Methods and Practice
description: Introduction to the problems and techniques of teaching dramatic art, through teaching responsibilities in departmental courses and through consultation with supervising faculty members.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit. Required of all teaching assistants. S/U grade.No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.
prereq_text: Graduate standing and current appointment as a departmental teaching assistant.

subject: THTR
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by the department chair.

subject: THTR
title: Master's Thesis Project, Research and Creative
description: Master's thesis project, research and creative.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of eight units. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degrees.

subject: THTR
title: Dissertation Research and Preparation
description: Dissertation research and preparation.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit to a maximum of 108 units. S/U grading. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.

subject: TMP W
title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.
repeat_comments: TMP W 120 is the online version of TMP 120. Students who have taken TMP 120 are not eligible to enroll in this course and receive additional units of credit.

subject: TMP
title: Issues in Technology, Business, and Society
description: Lecture series where entrepreneurial, technological, business, and governmental leaders share their lessons of experience and discuss current business issues. For anyone interested in entrepreneurship, management, technology development, and commercialization and the impact that innovation has on society.

subject: TMP
title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.

subject: TMP
title: Entrepreneurship
description: Learn how to start any type of venture; for profit, non-profit, service, sole-proprietorship, with a focus on high-tech ventures. Analysis of new business opportunities, development of customer-centric value propositions, financing, marketing, selling, and protection of intellectual property.

subject: TMP
title: Principles of Marketing
description: Introduces fundamental principles, processes, and tools of marketing which are used to create, communicate and deliver the value of products and services to customers, clients, partners, and society. This is done with an array of essential topics, such as the identification of customer needs and wants, assessment of the competitive environment, selection of the most appropriate target opportunities, development of an integrated marketing strategy, and disciplined execution.

subject: TMP
title: Fundamentals of Business Finance
description: Students learn essential tools to understand and analyze financial information and financing strategies for ongoing and new business ventures. This course is designed for those who will be participating in the decision-making processes of a small to large size business organization either as an analyst or an operating manager. Major topics covered include financial analysis and management, time value of money, interpreting financial statements and their analysis, cash flow analysis, capital budgeting, project evaluation, financial decision making, and valuing an existing or new venture. In addition to the practical application of financial theory, you will be asked to solve several business case studies.
advisor_comments: Not open to students who have completed TMP X130F through PaCE.

subject: TMP
title: Understanding and Managing Technology Organizations
description: Participating in, managing and leading successful careers, teams and organizations. Current theories and practices concerning motivation, organizational culture, communications, effective decision making, team effectiveness and others are presented and discussed.

subject: TMP
title: Introductions to Patents and Intellectual Property
description: Provides emerging inventors, entrepreneurs, and scientists with a working knowledge of intellectual property (patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets), with the main focus being on patents. Will cover the basic functions of patents, structure of patents, and patent prosecution.

subject: TMP
title: New Product Development
description: New product development requires technical and non-technical business persons to work across disciplines. Instruction is provided in a wide range of topics concerning customer driven product innovation. Students learn new product development processes, tools, techniques, and organizational skills.

subject: TMP
title: Understanding AI in Business: Core Foundations of Business Strategy
description: Aims to equip students with a fundamental understanding of the relationship between AI technology and business strategy. Begins with the basic mathematical foundations of AI. Introduces the technical foundations of AI, highlighting the roles played by the hardware, infrastructure, and application layers. Building on these dual foundations, students learn to analyze these different AI segments. Various business models will be introduced to help assess the competitive advantages across the AI segments. Finally, explores how AI can be strategically applied across different industries and sectors to drive innovation and business development.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191AI

subject: TMP
title: Investment & Financial Management
description: Achieving superior investment results within acceptable risk parameters is often deemed the top challenge for Wealth Managers. This is especially so in the face of fluctuating economics and shifting investor goals. A portfolio's "integrity" e.g., how well it is balanced, often drives performance and volatility. Takes a comprehensive approach to portfolio construction and management and explores how prevailing macro-economic conditions and investor priorities can be translated into viable investment strategies. Theory is balanced with actual case study scenarios to demonstrate how course concepts are practiced in the real world.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191FM

subject: TMP
title: Leadership in Technology & Innovation
description: Explores the dynamic intersection of leadership, technology, and innovation. Designed for undergraduate students from all disciplines, it delves into the essential skills and knowledge needed to effectively lead in today's rapidly evolving technological landscape. Students gain a comprehensive understanding of how leadership principles apply within the context of technology creation, development, and implementation.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191L

subject: TMP
title: Negotiation
description: Unlock the art and science of negotiation in this dynamic, hands-on course designed to help you build the skills needed to succeed in both personal and professional settings. Learn how to effectively communicate, identify win-win solutions, and confidently navigate high-stakes discussions. Through interactive case studies, readings, and role-playing exercises, develop strategies for resolving conflicts, influencing outcomes, and creating lasting agreements. Whether negotiating a salary, business deal, or group project, this course equips students with essential tools to negotiate successfully a range of situations. Perfect for students from all majors looking to enhance their career readiness.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191N

subject: TMP
title: Market Research
description: Provides a high level introduction to modern marketing research. Course covers the fundamental principles and techniques for market validation that are critical to launch, grow, and sustain a viable business.

subject: TMP
title: Sport Business Strategy & Innovation
description: An introduction to the creative business strategies of building (planning, organizing, implementing, and evaluating) a sport organization, with a particular emphasis on major and minor league professional sports. Explores traits of creative thinking and decision making theories in application towards selecting a hosting city, site assessment, arena/stadium financials, roster assembly, sales tactics, and marketing initiatives, among other areas. Moreover, students investigate consumer behavior elements to determine target audience criteria and its alignment with brand identity, partnership opportunities, and communication strategies.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191SP

subject: TMP
title: Venture Capital / Private Equity
description: Provides an overview of how VC and PE firms operate. Topics include how VC/PE firms are structured and how they manage a fund over the course of its life cycle: raising a fund, sourcing deals, evaluating investment opportunities, valuing businesses, negotiating term sheets with entrepreneurs, adding value to portfolio companies, and exiting investments. White this takes the perspective of the investor, also covers the funding life cycle of a typical start-up with an emphasis on what the roles of VC and PE are relative to other sources of financing. Course material will be presented primarily through case studies and selected readings.
repeat_comments: Same course as TMP 191VC

subject: TMP
title: Creating a Market-Tested Business Model
description: Course provides an experiential learning opportunity, showing how a successful business model can be created through the use of customer and market validation process.

subject: TMP
title: Decision Analysis
description: Through lectures, role playing and case studies, students will develop an understanding of how decisions are made, the factors and biases that affect them, the tools that have been developed as a result, and the limitations that remain. The goal is to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamentals of decision theory. By introducing real world applications that have a direct connection to the students, they can apply what they have learned to their own decisions.

title: Special Topics in Business and Management
description: Courses provide for the study of topics of current interest in the areas of, business, technology management, entrepreneurship, and other issues related to management and creation of sustainable businesses.

subject: TMP
title: Intellectual Property and Patent Litigation
description: Patent Litigation is a fact of life for entrepreneurs in high technology. If you have a viable technology in a commercially promising field, you will likely be sued for patent infringement or have to sue someone for infringing your patents. This course presents and discusses many important steps and issues in these legal processes. Illustrations of the role of these components in trials are given based on instructor’s 20+ years of experience as a technical expert witness, including cases involving Intel, Qualcomm, Broadcom, AT&T, Alcatel, Ericsson, Microsoft, and Apple, and common technologies, such as Wi-Fi access points, digital cellular, audio coding, speech coding, video coding, Bluetooth, multimedia protocols, and computer networks.
advisor_comments: May be repeated for credit provided there is no duplication of course content.

title: Managing Social Innovation
description: Social innovation and social entrepreneurship describe novel approaches to tackling complex social problems. Platforms and emerging technologies offer new possibilities for action. We adopt the perspectives of various actors (individual, non-profits, entrepreneurial companies, large companies, and governments) engaged in social innovation processes, debating the benefits, challenges, and trade-offs associated with their participation. The highly interactive class involves case studies, experiential exercises, and student presentations.

description: Introduction to basic marketing concepts and how these concepts can be applied to any organization, particularly technology firms. Additionally, they will be introduced to how management of the marketing function within an organization is critical to the organizations success.

description: Students gain exposure to various theories of organizing.

subject: TMP

description: Exploration of how organizing processes enable and constrain the development and use of technology innovations.

subject: TMP
title: Technology and Organizational Change
description: Examines fundamental questions and approaches to the study of technology and organizations including how organizational structures enable and constrain the development of new technologies, and how new technologies enable changes in the process of organizing. The purpose of the course is to provide students with a thorough grounding in various theoretical perspectives on technology development and use.

subject: TMP
title: Teams and Meso-Organizational Theory
description: Organizational science is an interdisciplinary field that draws primarily on psychology, social psychology, sociology, and economics. As such, the field spans from what is often called “micro” (organizational behavior) to “macro” (organization theory). This course introduces students to many of the core theoretical underpinnings of what sits in the middle: “meso” organizational theories. Meso-research generally looks at intra-organizational processes, or what connects individuals and organizations. Using teams as a pro-typical example, teams are groups of individuals where the dynamics between individuals shape organizational outcomes.

subject: TMP
title: Proseminar: Theory, Research, and Practicum
description: Required seminar that offers current advances, foundational, integrative, and socialization content.

subject: TMP
title: Qualitative Methods
description: Qualitative methods are increasingly common in social science fields. In this doctoral seminar, we will explore the research approaches and methodological practices associated with designing, conducting and publishing high-quality field research. We will focus on the processes of observation, interviewing, discovery, justification, theorizing, and writing. The course is relevant for those interested in conducting qualitative research (either by itself or as a mixed methods approach), as well as for readers of publications based on qualitative data. The course will be practicum-based; we will be using these techniques to collect and analyze data.

subject: TMP
title: Work in an Age of Intelligent Technologies
description: We have long predicted radical economic and social transformation given the introduction of ostensibly "intelligent" technologies into the world of work. Using this doctoral seminar, we assess these claims so that we can do more useful research. Focusing on work means we consider analysis from a wide range of disciplines and sources, ranging from economics, organization studies, sociology, human-computer/robot interaction, ethics, law, political science, corporate/public research and beyond.

subject: TMP
title: Readings in Technology, Work and Organizations
description: This seminar focuses on important and notable books in the fields of technology, work and organization studies. The books that comprise the syllabus vary from year to year. The agenda is not only to impart substantive knowledge and promote discussion and debate, but also to provide a venue for a community of scholars interested in technology, work and organizations. Because the seminars content is designed to change with each iteration, students may take this seminar more than once.

subject: TMP
title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
description: This course provides an overview of how VC and PE firms operate. Topics include how VC/PE firms are structured and how they manage a fund over the course of its life cycle: raising a fund, sourcing deals, evaluating investment opportunities, valuing businesses, negotiating term sheets with entrepreneurs, adding value to portfolio companies, and exiting investments. subject: TMP
title: Discourse and Institutions
description: Gives students a an understanding of how systems of meaning such as cultural frames, discourse systems, categorical logics, rhetorical forms, conventions of understanding, subjective field mappings, collective ontologies or institutional logics operate so as to define the nature of markets, technologies, organizations, and organizational environments.

subject: TMP
title: Digital Marketing
description: This course equips graduate students with modern strategic marketing skills for today’s digital and AI-enabled business environment. Students analyze markets, competitors, customers, and channels to develop actionable go-to-market strategies for startups and established tech companies. Emphasis is placed on upstream strategy, downstream execution, and real-world application through case studies, team projects, guest speakers, and an industry-reviewed capstone presentation.

subject: TMP
title: Strategy for Technology-Driven Companies
description: Business models and structures for value creation, innovation, competitiveness; leadership and decisions. Features case studies and discussions to understand approaches and techniques to manage technological innovation and change within their organizations, including design and incentivization of teams and organizations to promote innovation. Understanding industry and technology impacts on business model selection and evolution. Special emphasis on sustainable business practices and strategies to maintain a competitive global business.

subject: TMP
title: Finance and Accounting for Technology-Driven Companies
description: Covers the major concepts, principles, and analytical tools that support financial-based managerial decision-making. Modules include measuring and analyzing financial performance, planning and budgeting, developing forecasts and financial pro-formas, time value of money, cost of capital, risk/return trade-offs, capital budgeting and investing, cash and working capital management, and cost accounting and analysis. Emphasis will be on applying these concepts and tools in technology businesses.

subject: TMP
title: Data Science and Decision Making
description: Theoretical models and mathematical tools for quantitative analysis, statistics, decision theory, management. Students will learn how various business situations are modeled and optimized effectively using mathematical modeling and quantitative techniques. Examples include time-series analysis, regression, optimization (linear, nonlinear, and discrete), probabilistic modeling, decision analysis, and simulation.

subject: TMP
title: Project Management in New Product Development
description: Provides students with knowledge and tools to manage complex projects and operations to ensure that a project is completed on time, within budget, and with high quality by exploring specific techniques for accomplishing those three goals. Introduction to commonly used business systems and strategies for managing Value/Supply Chains, Information, Human Resources, considerations and strategies for global business operations. Prepares students to manage people, budgets, scheduling, and quality of projects.

subject: TMP
title: Innovation in the Digital Era
description: This course provides students with the knowledge and skills to foster and maintain innovation in firms. The course covers traditional topics in innovation as well as the increasingly central role of digital technologies as both facilitators of innovation and as innovation products.

subject: TMP
title: Creating Value Through Human Capital
description: Explores human capital topics including employee selection, performance management, training and development, compensation, downsizing, and human capital analytics. Provides an understanding of how organizations manage knowledge assets for strategic advantage, and offers skills for managing in knowledge-intensive organizations.

subject: TMP
title: Leading Technology Teams
description: Technology firms rely on teams for critical R&D and project work. Introduces research findings and practical skills to leverage team-based capabilities and avoid the pitfalls of teamwork. Opportunities to hone team leadership and teamwork skills through case analyses and experiential exercises.

subject: TMP
title: Entrepreneurship
description: This course covers the fundamentals of entrepreneurship, including product ideation, forming and building a startup team, market validation, business model development, go-to-market strategies, capital acquisition, and building competitive insulation.

subject: TMP
title: Learning to Work with Intelligent Machines
description: The age of intelligent technologies is upon us, and work will never be the same. Individuals, teams, and organizations that can discover and adapt to new ways of working with technologies such as AI and robotics will enjoy more success than those who do not. Through unconventional, practical use of AI itself, this course explores research-backed approaches that will help us develop skill with intelligent technologies - in ourselves and others. We build managerial ability in this domain as well: the knowhow required to design work that brings humans and intelligent technologies together to produce more valuable outcomes than they could apart.

subject: TMP
title: Digital Transformation
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and evidence about how companies are changing in the digital era. The course examines the drivers of digital transformation and explores the evidence on how successful companies make good strategic decisions in the rapidly changing digital environment, how companies can effectively manage and exploit their data assets, and how to implement digital tools in ways that improve organizational culture and collaboration.

subject: TMP
title: Negotiation for Technology Managers
description: The strategy and psychology of negotiation. You will learn about the science underlying the social dynamics of negotiations, gain insights into your own preferences, how to prepare for negotiations, and practice applying these lessons in role-play simulations. By the end of the course, you will have greater understanding and confidence in your abilities to create and claim value through negotiations in your personal and professional life.
prereq_text: Only students enrolled in the Master of Technology Management professional degree program may register for this course.

subject: TMP
title: Special Issues in Technology Commercialization
description: This course is intended to provide current focused research and theory on newly developing issues in specific technological or managerial subjects.

description: Courses provide for the study of topics of current interest in the areas of, business, technology management, entrepreneurship, and other issues related to management and creation of sustainable businesses.

subject: TMP
title: Leading Teams
description: Technology firms rely on teams for critical R&D and project work. Introduces research findings and practical skills to leverage team-based capabilities and avoid the pitfalls of teamwork. Opportunities to hone team leadership and teamwork skills through case analyses and experiential exercises.

subject: TMP
title: AI Building Intensive
description: Equips students with hands-on skills in applying AI to core business tasks, including rapid prototyping, preparing data for analysis and running regressions, and building agents for process redesign. Learn to integrate AI tools into real business workflows, moving from experimentation to practical application. At the end of the course, students will submit a professional portfolio of their work, demonstrating their ability to use AI strategically in a business context.

subject: TMP
title: Branding
description: A key part of developing a successful business is to build a well-regarded brand. In this course, students learn the fundamentals of building individual, product and organizational brands. The course emphasizes strategies and tactics for brand building and brand management in technology-based companies.

subject: TMP
title: Special Topics in Technology Management
description: Teaches students fundamentals of business communication, and develops skills for crafting and delivering persuasive and effective messages to different audiences.

subject: TMP
title: Digital Transformation
description: Digital technologies are accelerating the pace of change. To survive and thrive, todays organizations need to use these new technologies to continually innovate and redesign their current work practices. Digital transformation creates the opportunity to radically change the way work is done so that organizations can continue to grow and compete. This course provides a detailed framework for implementing digital transformation to enable fundamental organizational change.

subject: TMP
title: Current Issues in Technology Management
description: Focuses on the latest research and trends in managing technology teams and work. Topics may include those that integrate across other courses, as well introduce new concepts.

subject: TMP
title: MTM Internship
description: MTM students can gain hands-on, real-world experience through internship positions with technology-driven companies and organizations. The MTM Internship course will provide academic support and professional guidance to students during their internships. Activities include regular check-ins with the instructor, keeping a journal of skills used and learned, and a final paper or presentation based on the internship experience.

subject: TMP
title: Negotiation
description: The strategy and psychology of negotiation. You will learn about the science underlying the social dynamics of negotiations, gain insights into your own preferences, how to prepare for negotiations, and practice applying these lessons in role-play simulations. By the end of the course, you will have greater understanding and confidence in your abilities to create and claim value through negotiations in your personal and professional life.

subject: TMP
title: Capstone Project
description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor and industrial sponsor to tackle a management consulting project. Communication, reporting and presentation skills are also covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates skills acquired in courses completed in previous quarter.

subject: TMP

description: In this course, students will learn skills for effective communication in the workplace, including presenting and public speaking, email etiquette, delivering feedback, and using AI. Students will also participate in career readiness activities such as building LinkedIn profiles, networking, crafting elevator pitches, and career exploration. Finally, students will have the opportunity to improve their fluency with reading financial statements and using common business applications such as Excel.

description: W&L CS 160LJ, Linguistic Justice, focuses on how Writing Studies as a discipline approaches issues of language with a focus on justice. Rhetoric is such a key part of Writing Studies, so we will look at rhetorical situations that deal specifically with linguistic choices and expectations. Because this class will be taught at UCSB, which has both HSI and AAPI designations, we will investigate the linguistic injustices facing these communities and others in US classrooms, communities, and the larger political sphere. Issues of accessibility will also be addressed. Students can expect to read a mixture of public and academic scholarship on these topics and to engage in written genres that address both audiences.

The course asks students to determine whether or not a collection of ancient objects from an American museum should remain in the US or be sent back to Italy. Throughout the course, students excavate artifacts at a digital dig site, visit museums, explore Roman monuments, and navigate the shadowy world of the tombaroli (tomb robbers) and mafia-run black market for antiquities.

The course culminates in an oral presentation to the class and client on each team’s project.
prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.

Assignments might include a range of texts—such as academic essays, presentations, short videos, and podcasts—that examine the historical, ethical, and sociocultural dimensions of science.
prereq_text: At least one prior course from Writing 105AA-ZZ, 107AA-ZZ, or 109AA-ZZ; upper-division standing. Must be admitted to the Professional Writing Minor for enrollment.

subject: WRIT
title: Academic Writing Instruction Theory and Practice
description: Preparatory orientation and concurrent training in composition theory and pedagogy for newly appointed Writing Program teaching assistants. Topics include theories of composition pedagogy, academic literacies, principles of instructional design and curriculum development, effective classroom practices, and assessment of student writing.
prereq_text: Application submitted for Writing Program TA appointment.

subject: WRIT
title: Proseminar in Writing Studies
description: An introduction to the major lines of research and theory in the field of writing studies. The course emphasizes the roles writing plays in knowledge production and social organizations, and the contributions of research on writing to learning, instruction, and practice across disciplines, professions, and fields.

subject: WRIT
title: Pedagogies of University Writing: Theory and Practice
description: Explores theoretical foundations and practical approaches to teaching writing at the university and college level. Students will examine pedagogical theories, design writing prompts, and develop strategies for assessment and providing feedback. Assignments include writing teaching philosophies, crafting course materials, facilitating discussion, and reflective writing. By integrating theory and practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the various facets involved in teaching writing in a postsecondary context.
